consolidated.title: awb-package instructions are long, dense and overlapping
consolidated.description: The instructions run to about 11,700 words across awb-package SKILL.md, package-contract.md, review.md and helpers.md (45 KB), plus the templates and a 5,300-word README. Even for a headline preview, agents read everything to be sure no earlier step applied. Rules such as preview-mode precedence are spread over several paragraphs, and step 4 is a single paragraph of about 2,000 characters. review.md's scoped re-review procedure is elaborate yet can never finish a request, so agents skip it. Packaging turns were the longest turns in every run. Oct 15 taxi-B already called the references 'necessary but heavy', and phases #61, #64 and #66 added more text. co2-A-26's claim that the methods note has no size target is wrong: the template says 'a page or two'.
consolidated.oct15_ref: Oct 15 per-run taxi-B agent.md ('Reading long references ... necessary but heavy'); not in fix-plan
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-03: SKILL 2,514 / contract 2,576 / review 1,607 / helpers 5,052 words; headline preview 5.7 min, full draft 16.6 min. taxi-B-40: helpers about 5,000 words; scoped-review procedure skipped. co2-A-26: rules repeated in different wording; no slide-budget example. retail-B-30: helpers.md 45 KB; step 4 over 2,000 characters.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding's main claim is a measurable property of the release, and the installed copy in the runs is byte-identical to it (diff -rq on retail-B agent-home awb-package: SAME). Word counts: SKILL.md 2,514, package-contract.md 2,576, review.md 1,607, helpers.md 5,052, README 5,345. SKILL.md itself requires the contract ("Read the package contract first"), and the review and numbers steps send the agent to review.md and helpers.md. review.md says a scoped re-review "never" completes a request, so it is optional extra work, and taxi-B skipped it for that reason (taxi-B agent.md section 2). An agent on any interactive host (Copilot, Claude Code, Codex) has to read the same files.

Harness factors I checked, none of which creates the problem:
(1) Priming. relay.py's first-turn note tells the agent to log anything "too long" in the instructions, and the feedback prompt has a "too long" section. That makes length complaints more likely to be reported, but it does not make the files long.
(2) Truncation. Codex cut off large parallel reads (taxi-A agent.md rank 1, co2-A section 2), which caused re-reads. Interactive Codex truncates the same way, so this is host behaviour, not something codex exec adds.
(3) MCP failures. The five "failed" MCP calls in taxi-A turn 6 were check-draft and export calls exiting 1 on content problems. They were not timeouts or sandbox faults.
(4) Front-loaded answers. The persona answering the dataset and methods-note questions in advance shortened the work rather than lengthening it.
(5) Simulated home folder. It has no effect on the length of what the agent reads.

Weaknesses in the finding that do not change the verdict:
- The timing claim is overstated. In taxi-A's 5.7-minute preview, the instruction reads were two cat commands (SKILL and contract). The rest was reading project records, which Gather step 2 requires, plus drafting and a commit. The 16.6-minute full draft went mostly on reviewer-subagent waits, check-draft number repairs and export reruns. The Claude-agent packaging turns (40–58 min) were driven by 10–15 full review passes. Review churn is a separate issue, so "major" severity rests partly on costs this finding does not cause. retail-B's preview did read SKILL, contract and template, but took only 1.2 minutes.
- "45 KB" is wrong. helpers.md is 30,872 bytes, and the four files together are about 76 KB. The figure came from the retail-B agent's own estimate.
- The step 4 paragraph is 3,089 characters, so "about 2,000" understates it.
- The cited IDs co2-A-26, retail-B-30 and taxi-B-40 point at unrelated findings (a Codex web-tool error, a permission prompt, and nothing). The matching content is co2-A-22, retail-B-24/25, and taxi-B agent.md lines 36–37.

Confirmed parts of the finding:
- The methodology-note template line 7 says "Keep it to a page or two", so co2-A's "no size target" claim is wrong, as the finding says.
- The earlier "necessary but heavy" quote exists at docs/ux-simulation-2026-10-15/taxi-B/agent.md:58.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/SKILL.md:6 ("Read the package contract first") and the step-4 paragraph (3,089 chars, single paragraph); awb-package/references/review.md "After the review" ("a scoped re-review ... never does" complete a request; the scoped diff/snapshot procedure in the following paragraph); wc -w: SKILL.md 2514, references/package-contract.md 2576, references/review.md 1607, references/helpers.md 5052 (30,872 bytes, not 45 KB); README.md 5345; assets/package-format/methodology-note-template.md:7 ("Keep it to a page or two")

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding's main claim holds: the shipped instructions really are this long and overlapping. The word counts match the release exactly: SKILL.md 2,514, package-contract.md 2,576, review.md 1,607 and helpers.md 5,052, for 11,749 words. Templates and deck rules add about 5,500 more, and README.md is 5,345 words.

- **Step 4:** the opening paragraph of SKILL.md step 4 (line 68) is a single block of 3,089 characters, so "over 2,000" understates it.
- **Preview-mode rules repeat:** the precedence rule sits at SKILL.md:45. package-contract.md:39 restates the checkpoint, step 1 and step 7 mention it again, and README has 6 more mentions.
- **Scoped re-review is a dead end:** review.md:33 says a scoped re-review "never" completes a request or a release. review.md:37 still requires snapshot copies for every review and diffs against them. taxi-B (agent.md section 2) and taxi-A (notes: "No scoped shortcut") always ran full reviews, and taxi-B called the snapshots "mostly wasted."
- **Not one host's quirk:** agents raised the length complaint on both hosts: taxi-A and co2-A on Codex, taxi-B and retail-B on Claude. A real user's agent reads the same files and the user waits longer, so the cause is the release.
- **co2-A's "no size target" claim is wrong, as the finding says:** methodology-note-template.md:7 says "Keep it to a page or two."
- **Phases #61, #64 and #66 did add text:** the repo merges add 406, 665 and 102 lines to awb-package.

Several details are overstated or wrong, so the severity and the claimed effect on turn time are weaker than stated:

1. **Cited IDs don't match findings.json:**
   - co2-A-26 is a Zenodo web-tool finding; the length complaint is co2-A-22.
   - retail-B-30 is about a permission prompt.
   - taxi-B has no finding 40; the text exists only in agent.md.
2. **helpers.md is 30,872 bytes, not 45 KB.**
3. **"Read everything" is overstated:** the preview turns in taxi-A and retail-B read SKILL.md, the contract and the templates, but not review.md or helpers.md. retail-B's preview took only 1.2 minutes, so a slow preview is not universal.
4. **Long turns had other causes:** packaging was the longest turn in every run, but the longest ones were driven mostly by review-loop churn and number-check repairs, which are separate findings. taxi-B's 58.5-minute turn ran about 15 full reviews; retail-B's 40.4-minute turn ran 12 reviewer subagents. Reading time was not the main cost.

Conclusion: the defect is real and comes from the release, but its share of packaging time is smaller than the finding implies. "major" is arguable.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/SKILL.md:68 (step 4: one 3,089-character paragraph); awb-package/SKILL.md:45 with package-contract.md:39 (checkpoint and preview rules repeated); awb-package/references/review.md:33 (a scoped re-review "never" completes a request) and review.md:37 (snapshot and diff procedure required for every review); helpers.md is 5,052 words and 30,872 bytes in one section; methodology-note-template.md:7 ("Keep it to a page or two", which contradicts co2-A's claim)

consolidated.title: check-draft and state finding misread ordinary notation as untraceable numbers
consolidated.description: These are reported as unrecorded numbers: slash pairs (54.8/57.6, 368/53.5%), clock times (18:00), identifier pairs (264/265), tolerance values, date and citation years (2011, 2012, 1907), period labels, and raw source counts that validation already records. Year handling is inconsistent: 'January 2011 carries' counts as a number but 'December 2009 to' does not. The behavior is documented and fails safe, but only in the 45 KB helpers.md. It cost several failed preflights, allowed_numbers entries and rewording of sound prose. Oct 15 classified these false positives as intended (5.7) and shipped only the DOI skip.
consolidated.oct15_ref: fix-plan 5.7 (I; only the DOI skip shipped, in #63); synthesis section 5
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-02: 4 failed check-draft calls; helpers.md 'Tracing' says '3/4' and '14:05' never trace. retail-A-04: state finding warning on '2011'; check-draft rows for 2012, 1,067,371 and 368/53.5%. retail-B-32: inconsistent year rule; allowed_numbers entry '2011'. co2-B-21: bare year '1907'.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding is real and the release causes it. I couldn't tie it to any part of the harness. The number reader is deterministic release code, so it gives the same rows on any host. I fed the release's check_numbers the prose from the runs, in a scratchpad file, with no recorded values. It reported 54.8/57.6, 18:00, 264/265, 368/53.5%, a bare citation year 2012, 'before 1907 and', and 'January 2011 carries'. That matches the run logs:
- taxi-A, agent-006.jsonl: the check-draft numbers rows include 264/265, 54.8/57.6, 18:00, 18:59 and 0.00000001 percentage points.
- retail-A: state finding warned 'seasonality-comparison: 2011 is not a value its table... record' (agent-003). check-draft listed 2012, 1,067,371 and 368/53.5% (agent-005). The agent then reworded the finding to drop the years.
- retail-B: the shipped manifest has the allowed_numbers entry {"text":"2011","reason":"calendar year in month names..."}.
- co2-B: check-draft listed findings.md line 111 '1907' (agent-006) and earlier 219, 2025, 1750 and 1990, each of which needed an allowed_numbers entry.

Checking the harness factors one by one:
- Agent model: two runs with Codex as the agent (taxi-A, retail-A) and two with Claude as the agent (retail-B, co2-B) hit it, on three datasets. That rules out one model's writing habits.
- Sandbox, simulated home folder, relay and persona front-loading: none of them touch the tokenizer.
- Auto-approved MCP tools: if anything they understate the cost. On a host that prompts for each call, every failed preflight costs another approval.
- Design intent: the reader is meant to fail safe (awb_draft.py comment at lines 1311-1314; helpers.md 'Reading fails safe'). A deliberate design still costs a real user friction.

Parts of the finding are overstated:
1. taxi-A's '4 failed check-draft calls': all four read-only awb/read check-draft calls also failed on 'manifest.json records no inventory list; run check-draft without --verify-only'. Only the first two had numbers rows, so the numbers check caused two failed preflights, not four. The taxi-A agent also called its slash-heavy formatting its own efficiency mistake.
2. 'Year handling is inconsistent': the rule is consistent. My probe also reports 'December 2009 to' when nothing is recorded, because both years are followed by a word. The difference retail-B saw comes from tracing: 2009 appears in recorded settings or check text for some of the results the draft uses, while 2011 had no match for country-growth. A user still can't predict which year will be flagged, but the cause is tracing, not the year rule.
3. helpers.md is 30,872 bytes, not 45 KB. The repair path is also in awb-package/SKILL.md step 3 (line 84), which names dates and comparison years. Only the exact list of contexts lives in helpers.md.

None of these corrections move the cause away from the release.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:1319-1345 (_YEAR, _ENDS, _IN, _NOT_QUANTITY: a year is skipped only where 'the period ends', so 'January 2011 carries' and 'before 1907 and' are read) and :2629 (_structure_passed fails on any numbers row); awb-package/references/helpers.md:39 (Tracing: '3/4', '14:05' 'reported and never traces') and :40 (Reading fails safe); awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py:1643 (the state finding 'is not a value its table... record' warning); awb-package/SKILL.md:84 (repair by rewording or allowed_numbers)

verdicts.reasoning:
The core behavior is real and comes from the release. The shipped number reader in awb_draft.py reports these as untraced numbers on purpose: slash joins (54.8/57.6, 264/265, 368/53.5%), HH:MM times with no am/pm, UTC, GMT or seconds (18:00), a year followed by a word ('January 2011 carries', 'December 2011 is left out', 'before 1907 or'), and citation years ('(2012)'). The `state finding` command uses the same reader, so it warns on the same numbers (awb_provenance.py). The findings and methodology templates give no advance warning. Writers learn the rules only after check-draft reports rows. Any real user writing ordinary prose such as '18:00 remains the busiest pickup hour' or 'December 2011 is left out' will hit them, on any host.

Run evidence confirms it:
- taxi-A relay/agent-006.jsonl item_26 lists 32 `numbers` rows, including 264/265, 18:00, 18:59, 54.8/57.6 and 0.00000001 percentage points.
- retail-B: I ran the release's check_numbers against its draft with no allowances. It reports 2011 on findings.md lines 24, 25, 33, 106, 149 and 164, plus 1,067,371, 11,297 and 12,133.
- co2-B: check-draft reported '1907' at findings.md line 111.
- retail-A: agent.md line 75 shows the `state finding` warning on 2011, and line 79 shows the check-draft rows.

Several sub-claims are wrong or overstated:
1. **Year handling is not inconsistent.** Both 'January 2011 carries' and 'December 2009 to' are read by the release; I probed _quantities and both return their year. In retail-B, 2009 and 2010 happen to match values in the recorded results exactly (recorded_values contains Decimal('2009') and Decimal('2010')), while 2011 matches nothing. That is the coincidental tracing helpers.md documents under 'Limit', not a context-rule bug.
2. **The rules are not 'only in the 45 KB helpers.md'.** helpers.md is 30.9 KB. awb-package/SKILL.md line 84 itself names dates and years, the comma rewording, and the allowed_numbers route.
3. **Only two of taxi-A's four failed check-draft calls involved numbers.** item_26 and item_33 returned identical number rows. item_35 and item_43 failed only on the inventory error from the read-only path. The taxi-A agent had also read helpers.md (item_10) before drafting, and that file says plainly that `3/4` and `14:05` never trace. The agent's own feedback (agent.md line 144) calls its heavy slash notation 'my efficiency mistakes'.
4. **Flagging source counts and tolerances is the intended check.** It traces only to represented results, and SKILL.md lines 80-85 send such numbers to export or to allowed_numbers with a reason naming the record.
5. **Two of the cited evidence IDs are wrong.** retail-A-04 is about SQL parameters and retail-B-32 is about 'Now the friction log'. The matching findings are retail-A-03 and retail-B-25.

In every run, one round of rewording or allowances fixed the rows and the final check-draft passed. Severity therefore looks closer to minor than major; co2-B-21 and retail-B-25 were themselves rated minor. The finding stands as a product-caused friction (a documented design trade-off), with the year-inconsistency claim removed.

consolidated.title: The 'with its tolerance' rule pushes technical tolerances into audience text, sometimes invented after the fact
consolidated.description: #66 made review step 3 require findings.md and the methods note to state each completed check 'with its tolerance'. In taxi-A, 'zero-record tolerance' ended up on the released appendix slide after the user had removed it from the note. In co2-B, a 0.15 Mt tolerance went first into the How we know headline, then into a visible bullet after the user asked for notes only. In retail-B, internal filter retention ratios (90%, 95%, 50%, 3%) went onto the How we know slide and the note. co2-B's agent invented the 0.15 Mt tolerance after seeing a 0.13 Mt maximum gap, and the released note presents it as the check's standard. The templates repeat the pattern ('within 0.5%').
consolidated.oct15_ref: new; introduced by fix-plan 6.3 / #66 change 4 (review.md step 3)
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-08: released findings.md line 127; review.md step 3; findings-template.md line 66; methodology-note-template.md line 29. co2-B-07: package-contract 'with its tolerance'; U5 and U6 repeat the request. co2-B-08: agent-notes turn 4 'had to invent a 0.15 tolerance'. retail-B-05: reviewer passes 1-2 demanded the minimum ratios; U6 'Remove the technical filter thresholds'; R-audience-method-001. Git: 'with its tolerance' entered review.md in #66 (e4a7049, b0386ba).

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and did not find one. In all three runs the tolerance wording came from release text, carried either by the reviewer subagent that review.md tells the agent to launch or by the writer reading that same rule. The cause was not the relay, the sandbox, the simulated home folder, the non-interactive host, or the personas. None of the three persona BRIEFs mentions tolerances. They only describe non-technical audiences, which is a realistic setting.

co2-B (agent was Claude via claude -p):
- In the full-draft turn (relay/agent-004.jsonl lines 85-100), the first draft said "within 0.13 Mt", the largest observed gap.
- The reviewer objected that the reconciliation cited only an exploration query (l.174). The agent then created a world-reconciliation result with a 0.15 tolerance in both the SQL and the values judgment (l.190), after already seeing 0.13. The workbench text it was following tells the agent to state the check, with its tolerance, in a passing values judgment.
- The next reviewer pass (l.267) flagged "within 0.13 Mt" as lacking "the check's tolerance". The agent then put "within a 0.15 Mt tolerance" into the How we know headline (l.273-274).
- In U5 the user asked to keep the tolerance in the notes. The agent did move it (agent-005 l.32 removes it from both the headline and the bullet). The reviewer then flagged the bullet: "gives neither the result nor the 0.15 Mt tolerance ... The user's choice ... covers only the headline" (l.79). The agent put the tolerance back into the visible bullet (l.83), and U6 had to repeat the request.
- So the user's instruction lost to the release's review rule, not to ambiguous persona wording. review.md's "After the review" section also leaves no way to waive a narrative problem with the user's consent.

retail-B (agent was Claude):
- The first reviewer pass (agent-005 l.179) flagged "checked for expected row counts at each filter" because it "does not give the tolerance (the stated minimum ratios)". The agent added 90% and 95%.
- The next pass (l.263) demanded the 50% and 3% filter tolerances as well.
- U6 then asked to remove them, and the user's correction was saved as rule R-audience-method-001.
- The finding cites retail-B-05 for this, but the threshold item is actually retail-B-04. retail-B-05 is the related late-reconciliation item.

taxi-A (agent was Codex):
- Codex read the review.md step 3 rule before drafting (agent-006 l.7) and wrote "with zero-record tolerance" into both the How we know slide and the note (l.72).
- The user asked only for the note to change. The agent fixed only the note, so the phrase is on the released appendix slide (storage/releases/.../001/findings.md:127).
- The narrow fix on the slide is partly the agent's own behavior. The phrase itself exists because of the rule.

The templates show the same pattern ("within 0.5%"). Git confirms that "with its tolerance" entered review.md and the package contract in #66 (e4a7049, b0386ba). A real user on an interactive Claude Code or Codex host gets the same review.md Brief and the same subagent reviewer, so they would hit this too.

Two caveats on the facts:
- The co2-B user later explicitly kept the tolerance in the methodology note (U7). Its presence in the released note is user-approved, though the 0.15 figure was still chosen after the fact.
- The per-run impact was minor in taxi-A and co2-B. The retail-B user rated it major.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/references/review.md:22 (step 3: "in `findings.md` and the note, the check in plain words, with its tolerance ... A sentence without one is a narrative problem"); awb-package/references/package-contract.md:48 (same rule for the writer); awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:66 and methodology-note-template.md:29 (example "within 0.5%"); awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:17 and awb-init/references/provenance.md:7 (the state finding warning's fix: "state the check, with its tolerance, in the detail of a passing values or metrics judgment"); review.md "After the review" (any narrative problem blocks completion and release; only warning violations can be accepted by the user)

verdicts.reasoning:
The shipped files cause this. review.md step 3 and package-contract.md line 48 require every sentence in findings.md and in the audience methods note that says something was checked, reconciles, sums or matches to name the check "in plain words, with its tolerance". Neither file makes an exception for exact checks or for checks that had no tolerance set in advance. Nor do they say that "exactly" counts, or that the tolerance must have been chosen before the data was seen. The findings template requires the How we know slide to describe the validation performed, and its example puts the tolerance on the slide itself ("totals reconcile to the finance ledger within 0.5%", line 66). The methods-note template repeats the same example at line 29, and the note has no speaker-notes section to move the number into. The `state finding` warning sends the writer the same way: state the check, with its tolerance, in the detail of a passing values judgment, then rerun. That makes picking a tolerance after the fact the easiest fix. The only thing that pushes back is template line 66's "Put what the audience needs on the slide and the rest in the notes", which does not cover the note.

The run evidence holds up:
- **taxi-A:** in U7 item 6 the user asked to drop "with zero-record tolerance" from the methods note, and the agent did. The released 001 findings.md line 127 (How we know, appendix) still says "...location joins preserved record counts, with zero-record tolerance". agent.md traces the phrase to the reviewer's tolerance demand.
- **co2-B, invented tolerance:** exploration first recorded "within 0.13 Mt" (agent-full.txt line 116 and later). The agent then built a world-reconciliation result with `gap > 0.15` and a values detail saying "within a tolerance of 0.15 Mt" (line 604). It changed the How we know headline from "within 0.13 Mt" to "within a 0.15 Mt tolerance" (line 621). agent-notes says "had to invent a 0.15 tolerance in the values judgment so a 'tolerance' exists". The released note (line 32) and slide notes (line 144) present 0.15 Mt as the check's standard, though they also disclose the 0.13 Mt maximum gap.
- **co2-B, visible bullet:** in U5 the user asked to keep the tolerance in the notes. Reply 5 still put it in a visible validation bullet. The agent's notes say the user's request "conflicts with the contract rule", and the number left the slide only after U6 repeated the request.
- **retail-B:** after review pass 1, the agent replaced "Each result was checked for expected row counts at each filter" with "at least 90% of lines kept by the period filter and 95% by the line-type filter..." in findings.md and the note (agent-005.txt lines 173 and 283). agent.md lists "missing check tolerances" among the reviewer's demands. In U6 the user asked to remove these technical thresholds.

The agents did not ignore an instruction. Each time, the release rule pushed them toward the tolerance, and they worked against it only when the user objected. The agents did contribute in two places. In taxi-A the agent removed the phrase only where the user named it. In retail-B the agent chose to claim that every result passed its checks, which the rule then turned into a list of thresholds.

On severity, "major" looks overstated. The per-run findings for taxi-A-08, co2-B-07 and co2-B-08 were each rated minor. The users caught most instances. The released co2-B text discloses the observed gap next to the tolerance. retail-B-05's own major rating is about checks being recorded late, not about tolerance wording. The citation of #66 commits is only roughly right: "with its tolerance" first entered the state-finding warning in #63, and review.md picked it up in #66.

('totals reconcile to the finance ledger within 0.5%')"); awb-package/assets/package-format/methodology-note-template.md:29 (same example, and the note has no notes section); awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:17 and awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py:1653 (the state-finding fix: "state the check, with its tolerance, in the detail of a passing values or metrics judgment... and rerun")

consolidated.title: Drafts pass check-draft and review while missing parts of the brief or carrying substantive errors the user catches
consolidated.description: Review step 3 checks consistency, claim strength, provenance and caveats, and check-draft's questions check only confirms that methodology.md repeats each question. Neither checks that every part of a question appears on a visible slide, that the brief's standing requirements (such as a one-page note) are met, or that a claim about how a source is built is documented. In taxi-A, Q3's hour-of-day and borough part sat only in speaker notes. taxi-B's 15 reviews missed an over-long note, a base-fare definition that left out flat fares, Newark's short trip durations, and methods text admitting that counts and joins were not checked. co2-B's reviewer accepted an unsupported claim that OWID's World series also omits China's and India's missing years. This is the same pattern as Oct 15 (five user corrections after review in taxi-A, the false 'sum to World' in co2-B). Sentences claiming a check are now caught (see the fixed list).
consolidated.oct15_ref: fix-plan 6.4 (R) and 6.3; synthesis section 6 'What the reviews missed'; #66
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-01: msg 7 correction 1; helpers.md questions check; review.md step 3. taxi-B-02: msg 6 lists four corrections after reply 5 said 'a final independent review found no problems'; brief.md line 24 'one-page methodology note'. co2-B-04: A6 'the world total leaves out China's and India's emissions in them too'; U7 challenge; DQ-008 still carries the claim.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for harness causes and found none for the core of the finding. In both variants the reviews ran the way the release prescribes. taxi-A (Codex agent) launched real fresh reviewer subagents; their rollouts are in taxi-A/agent-home/.codex/sessions/2026/10/16/rollout-*16-0*.jsonl. The first returned two missing-citation problems, and the second returned "review: clean" on the draft whose Q3 hour-of-day and pickup-borough answer sat only in speaker notes. That reviewer followed review.md's Brief exactly, and the Brief has no check that each part of a question appears on a visible slide. check-draft's questions check only confirms that methodology.md repeats each result's question word for word (helpers.md:36). The Claude user's persona brief does not coach this correction; the user simply compared the slides with the five questions. The agent's own feedback (agent.md rank 5) also blames missing question-coverage review.

In taxi-B the Claude agent launched 15 separate Plan subagent reviews in turn 5 (agent-005.jsonl), plus more later. Its reviewer prompts even listed brief.md as a useful read and added the user's extra requirements, going beyond the release, and the 15th review was still clean. Two of the four problems the user then caught are clean release evidence. First, the first methods note ran 770 words, while brief.md line 24 records "a one-page methodology note". The release's own methodology-note-template.md:7 says "Keep it to a page or two", and the review Brief never tells the reviewer to read brief.md. Second, base fare was defined as the meter's time-and-distance fare, which step 3 has no check for. A third, the methods line that row-count and join checks were "not assessed", is allowed by design: analysis.md lets a not-assessed check stand if it is "justified with a caveat", so the review passes it. The fourth, Newark's short durations, is a gap in analytical depth rather than in review scope.

Nothing about non-interactive runs, the sandbox, auto-approved MCP tools, the simulated home, the relay, or front-loaded persona answers changed what the reviewer was told to check. In fact, the front-loaded one-page requirement was recorded in the brief and was still missed.

The co2-B leg is weak and partly a harness effect. Turn 6's first reviewer explicitly endorsed the inference that "the World total also lacks them". That inference rests on a recorded reconciliation: countries plus international aviation and shipping match World in every year within 0.15 Mt. So the claim is arguably supported, not an error. The Codex user's challenge is also cued by co2-B/human/BRIEF.md:28 ("Questions about how OWID constructs a series are best answered by OWID's documentation"). Even if that leg is dropped, the taxi-A and taxi-B evidence shows a real user on a normal interactive host would get drafts that pass check-draft and the full review while missing parts of the brief.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release defines a review and a check-draft that leave out the three checks the finding names, and the core evidence in all three runs holds up.

What the release says:
- check-draft's `questions` check (helpers.md:36; awb_draft.py question_problems, around line 1047) only confirms that methodology.md repeats each represented result's question word for word. Nothing compares the brief's questions with the visible slide bullets.
- Review step 3 (review.md:22) covers matching caveats, claim strength, revalidation flags, tracing findings and the note back to methodology.md, and sentences that claim a check. It has nothing on whether every part of a question appears on a slide, whether the brief's standing requirements are met, or whether a claim about how a source is built is documented.
- The release points drafts the wrong way in two places. findings-template.md:15 says content that does not fit "goes to another slide or into the notes", and check-draft's outline row repeats that advice (awb_draft.py:2024, 2029). methodology-note-template.md:7 says "Keep it to a page or two", which conflicts with a brief asking for one page. Length is checked only for the deck's slide count (SKILL.md step 7), never for the note.

What the runs show:
- **taxi-A:** confirmed. Reply 6 reported that the full review and check-draft passed. In message 7 the user's first correction was that Q3's hour and borough part sat only in speaker notes. The agent then added rule R-question-coverage-001. The agent's own feedback (rank 5) asks for a check that maps each question's parts to visible slide content.
- **taxi-B:** the 15 review snapshots (agent-home/scratch/review-1 to review-15) confirm the reviews. Before message 6 the note was 867 words, against "one-page methodology note" at brief.md:24. Its base-fare definition said "the meter's time-and-distance fare" (review-15 note, line 18). Newark's short trip durations were not in the caveat. All three were caught by the user, not the reviews.
- **co2-B:** confirmed. Reply 6's speaker notes said the world total leaves out China's and India's missing years. The review passed it, the user challenged it in message 7, and DQ-008 in quality.md still carries "so World omits them too". The agent's feedback says the reviewer accepted the inference.

Where the finding overstates:
- taxi-B's "methods text admitting that counts and joins were not checked" is not a review miss. It is an honest caveat the release's own validation flow allows: a not-assessed check may be justified with a caveat (workbench-guides/analysis.md:17), and the record-keeping commands then write a "not assessed" caveat. A reviewer should keep that disclosure, not flag it.
- The co2-B claim had some basis. A recorded reconciliation shows countries plus international transport match World in every year, so "unsupported" is debatable. Still, the review brief never asks whether claims about how a source is built are documented.
- The base-fare and Newark items are domain and analysis judgements that no checklist guarantees catching.

None of this depends on the simulation harness. A real user on an interactive host gets the same review scope and the same template guidance. The release's way of turning a user's correction into a review rule only stops repeats after the first miss. So the release is the cause, but one of the cited sub-examples should be dropped and another softened.

consolidated.title: Codex agents link and quote skill instruction files to the user to justify pauses
consolidated.description: In all three Codex-agent runs, the agent linked or quoted SKILL.md files to the user: taxi-A three times across two turns, retail-A five times across three turns, co2-A once. #62 had added 'never send them to a skill or instruction file' to the project AGENTS.md, and the agents had read it. Users declined to open the files, and taxi-A's user ranked this the top pain point. co2-A-09 was tagged unclear: it happened once, and the project AGENTS.md did not yet exist at session start. Product is better evidenced, because in two runs it recurred across turns after the rule had been read. Oct 15 attributed this behavior to host instructions (4.7).
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-05: transcript lines 47, 62 and 225; AGENTS.md template line 30. retail-A-06: A1 twice, A4, A6 twice. co2-A-09: transcript line 41.

verdicts.reasoning:
The behavior is real, but it comes from Codex's own base instructions, not from the release. So the "product" label fails its second test: the release has to be the cause.

1. **The host prompt asks for exactly this.** Every Codex rollout stores the model's base instructions in session_meta.base_instructions (for example agent-home/.codex/sessions/2026/10/16/rollout-2026-10-16T15-17-11-01a14625-...jsonl in taxi-A). They say: "The user gets very frustrated when you stop and ask for confirmation or permission, so make sure to explicitly explain why you need the confirmation (for example, a SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, memory, or approval auto-review block) and where it came from ... Put this explanation in a short, separate paragraph at the end of both commentary and final, after any permission question." The same prompt also says "When referencing a real local file, prefer a clickable markdown link."

2. **Every flagged instance has that shape.** Each one is a short separate paragraph at the end of a message, after the question or pending checkpoint, linking a SKILL.md and quoting its wording:
   - taxi-A reply 1 does it twice, once in the commentary (rollout item 62, transcript line 47) and once in the final answer (item 127, line 62). That is "both commentary and final", word for word.
   - taxi-A line 225, retail-A lines 45, 56, 302, 369 and 411, and co2-A line 41 follow the same pattern.
   - The taxi-A agent's own friction log calls it a "mandatory skill-quote explanation". The release's awb-init report section (SKILL.md lines 48-60) has no such requirement, so the mandate came from the host prompt. That makes the referee's tag_reason for taxi-A-05 ("the skills drive it") wrong.

3. **The release forbids it, and the host prompt wins.** Line 30 of the release's AGENTS.md template says "never send them to a skill or instruction file". Codex loaded the project AGENTS.md as instructions partway through each run (taxi-A item 134, retail-A item 105, co2-A item 100). The agent still cited skill files afterwards (taxi-A item 741, retail-A A4 and A6). The base system prompt outranks AGENTS.md.

4. **It is specific to the Codex host.** The three Claude-agent runs (taxi-B, co2-B, retail-B) got the same harness note and the same skills, and have zero SKILL.md or skill-path references in their transcripts.

5. **What the simulation did not cause.** The instruction is in every GPT-6 model's base prompt in models_cache.json (gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna). The user's real ~/.codex/models_cache.json has the same text, and their real config also uses gpt-6.1-sol. So non-interactive exec, the sandbox and approval_policy=never did not cause it. Codex used this same prompt in both exec and the interactive client. A real Codex user on GPT-6 would most likely see it too.

**Why "harness" despite that.** None of the three verdicts fits exactly. The cause is the agent host (Codex's GPT-6 prompt), which is neither the release nor the relay, and that matches Oct 15's "host instructions" (4.7) call. Under the brief's definitions it is not a release product defect, so I label it harness, meaning not caused by the release. It should be recorded as a host-instruction conflict that real Codex users will see.

**Possible product follow-up.** The release's AGENTS.md says "send them to", which the agent apparently did not read as covering a link plus a quote. Wording that names the case directly might help, for example "explain a pause in plain words; never link or quote a skill or instruction file". Whether any project-level rule can beat a system-level instruction is untested.
verdicts.release_evidence: Contradicts the finding: analytics-workbench-skills/awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:30 forbids sending the user to a skill or instruction file, and awb-init/SKILL.md:46-60 never asks for skill quotes or links. The cause is outside the release: taxi-A/agent-home/.codex/sessions/2026/10/16/rollout-2026-10-16T15-17-11-01a14625-951a-79d3-b8a3-9076e94622e1.jsonl line 1 (session_meta.base_instructions, "explicitly explain why you need the confirmation (for example, a SKILL.md, AGENTS.md ...) ... short, separate paragraph at the end of both commentary and final"), the same text in agent-home/.codex/models_cache.json for all GPT-6 models.

verdicts.reasoning:
The behavior is real, and every cited instance checks out. In taxi-A, transcript lines 47 and 62 (reply 1) link and quote awb-init SKILL.md, and line 225 (reply 5) links and quotes awb-package SKILL.md. In retail-A, lines 45 and 56 (A1), 302 (A4), and 369 and 411 (A6) each link a SKILL.md. In co2-A, line 41 links awb-scope SKILL.md. The taxi-A user ranked this the top pain point in feedback/human.md.

The release does not cause it. No SKILL.md, reference, template or README tells the agent to cite or quote skill files to the user. awb-init's report section says "Report in plain words". The shipped project AGENTS.md template already forbids the behavior at line 30: "never send them to a skill or instruction file". The agents had this rule in context. In taxi-A, turn 1 cat'd the template (its output contains the rule) before writing line 47. Codex also injected "# AGENTS.md instructions for …project" into the resumed session at turn 2 (rollout line 134), before the line-225 violation.

The cause is the Codex host's own base instructions. These are present in every Codex-agent rollout's session_meta.base_instructions for retail-A, co2-A and taxi-A. They come from Codex's models_cache.json, not from the harness kit, and config.toml has no instruction override. The text reads: "make sure to explicitly explain why you need the confirmation (for example, a SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, memory, or approval auto-review block) and where it came from ... Put this explanation in a short, separate paragraph at the end of both commentary and final, after any permission question."

Every observed instance matches that shape exactly: a separate closing paragraph, placed after the question, that names the SKILL.md as the source of the pause. This is also what the agent's own notes call the "mandatory skill-quote explanation" (taxi-A agent-notes.md line 20). The Claude-agent runs (taxi-B, co2-B, retail-B) use the same release and show zero SKILL.md mentions. The harness's Claude system prompt (kit/claude-agent-system.md) has no rule against linking that could explain that difference.

The agent ignoring AGENTS.md:30 repeatedly reflects a system-level host instruction outranking a user-level project rule. It does not mean the release causes the behavior. The finding's own reasoning ("product is better evidenced because it recurred after the rule was read") shows the counter-rule is ineffective, not that the release is the cause.

Caveat on the label: a real Codex user on this model would see the same behavior, so this is a host behavior rather than a simulation artifact in the narrow sense. It fails the "release is the cause" half of the product test. A product-side mitigation remains possible but is not causation. AGENTS.md:30 is phrased around "send them to" when asking for a decision, and the agent can read a citation that justifies a pause as a different act. A rule that explicitly says "when explaining a pause, give the reason in plain words; never link, name or quote SKILL.md or AGENTS.md" might reduce it, though it would still compete with the system prompt.
verdicts.release_evidence: The release prevents it rather than causing it: release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:30 says "never send them to a skill or instruction file", and awb-init/SKILL.md:50 says "Report in plain words". The cause is outside the release, in the Codex host base instructions (taxi-A/agent-home/.codex/models_cache.json; session_meta.base_instructions in rollout-2026-10-16T15-17-11-01a14625-951a-79d3-b8a3-9076e94622e1.jsonl): "explicitly explain why you need the confirmation (for example, a SKILL.md, AGENTS.md ...) and where it came from ... in a short, separate paragraph at the end of both commentary and final".

consolidated.title: The hard 15-word headline cap has no override and is not disclosed to the user
consolidated.description: awb_draft.py sets HEADLINE_WORDS = 15 for every headline, with no exception path, and neither the README nor the headline checkpoint mentions it. Agents squeezed headlines with slashes, dropped clauses ('45 countries cut emissions while growing') and rewrote headlines the user had already approved. taxi-B's zone headline now leads with a $564.64 Newark figure the agent itself doubted. In co2-A the agent mentioned the 'template word limit' only after the user restored their own wording, and that led to C-21. The cap predates Oct 15 but was not reported then. taxi-B-21 was tagged unclear (its headlines were previewed outside the checkpoint); co2-A and co2-B give better evidence for product.
consolidated.evidence: co2-A-01: awb_draft.py lines 1772 and 2019; A5 'Your exact headline exceeds the template's word limit'. co2-B-38: A5 'To fit your wording within the 15-word headline limit, I dropped ...'. taxi-B-21: reply 5 'Headline wording was tightened from the version you approved'; findings-template 'at most 15 words'.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and did not find one. The cap and its lack of override come from the release code, not from how the simulation was run.

1. **The cap is hard and blocks release.** `outline_problems` adds a row for any headline over HEADLINE_WORDS = 15. `_structure_passed` needs `outline == []`, and `release()` refuses to run unless `_structure_passed` holds. The release has no exception, waiver or allowed-text path for headlines. The `allowed_numbers` mechanism covers numbers only. In co2-A, the agent had to patch the installed `src/packaging/draft.py`, adding a `headline_length_exceptions` field, before the user's wording could pass. That patch is absent from the release, which confirms the release has no override.

2. **The user is never told about the cap.** README.md describes headlines (line 11) and the headline checkpoint (lines 66-70) but never gives a word limit. The checkpoint section of awb-package/SKILL.md (lines 43-52) does not mention the limit or tell the agent to disclose it. Only the agent-facing findings-template.md (line 14) and the helper docs state it. The co2-A human feedback names exactly this gap: a "template word limit I had never heard of" and, under README, "Missing: that headlines have a word limit."

3. **The user behaviour was natural, not planted.** The co2-A persona asked for a two-clause, 21-word Answer headline. Neither BRIEF.md nor the harness note mentions headlines or word counts, and nothing was front-loaded. Any real user who wants a contrast sentence on the Answer slide would run into this.

4. **The cap drove the agents' rewrites.** The co2-A agent notes say the slashes were used "to fit all three requested evidence clauses into one sentence within the 15-word package rule." They also say "Helper hard-coded 15 words with no user-override mechanism." In co2-B, a different model (Claude via claude -p) said "To fit your wording within the 15-word headline limit, I dropped..." That is two model families, Codex and Claude, giving the same reason. Model-specific role behaviour is therefore unlikely.

**Possible harness factors I checked and set aside:**
- Non-interactive `codex exec`: on an interactive host the agent still has only two choices, override the user's wording or modify the helper.
- Auto-approved writes: these explain why the co2-A agent could patch the checker without asking. That is C-21, not this cap.
- Relay: I found no relay errors.

**Caveats:**
- **taxi-B is the weakest case.** Its "approved" headlines were multi-sentence summaries previewed before the agent read the package rules. The Newark headline also owes something to the template's rule that a headline carries its key number. So taxi-B is mixed evidence.
- **Some of the co2-A evidence is weaker than reported.** The first clause drop (reply 4) arguably fell within the user's "one idea per headline is fine" allowance.
- **co2-B was not silent.** The agent disclosed the limit and offered to reword.

None of this changes the core result: co2-A shows a release-caused block, with no override, on wording the user explicitly asked for.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:1772 (HEADLINE_WORDS = 15); awb_draft.py:2019-2020 (over-cap headline row, no exception path); awb_draft.py:2624-2626 (_structure_passed requires outline == []); awb_draft.py:4072 (release refuses unless _structure_passed); README.md:11 and 66-70 (headline and checkpoint described, no word limit); awb-package/SKILL.md:43-52 (checkpoint section never mentions the limit); awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:14 (cap stated only in the agent-facing template)

verdicts.reasoning:
The release causes this.

**Release side**
- `awb_draft.py` sets `HEADLINE_WORDS = 15` at line 1772.
- `outline_problems` emits a failing row for any headline over that count at lines 2019-2020, and nothing exempts a headline from it.
- That row blocks two things:
  - "Done" in awb-package, which needs `check-draft` to print `passed: true`.
  - The release itself: the `awb-release` gate (`check-draft --verify-only`) refuses on any row.
- Other checks have a user-facing escape: `allowed_numbers` for numbers, and user acceptance for `warning` review-rule violations (`review.md` lines 33-35). Outline rows have none.
- The cap is written only for the agent: `findings-template.md` line 14, `package-contract.md` line 45, `helpers.md` line 28.
- The user-facing material never mentions it:
  - README line 11 says only "one-sentence headline", and the README's checkpoint section (lines 66-70) gives no word count.
  - The SKILL.md headline checkpoint (lines 43-52) does not tell the agent to state the limit when showing headlines.
  - No instruction covers a user who dictates or approves a headline over 15 words.
- The one place a user could find it is a CHANGELOG line, which ordinary users are unlikely to read.

**co2-A (strong evidence)**
- In reply 3 the agent squeezed the Answer headline into slashes ("China/India/Indonesia lead increases; US/Japan/Germany ...").
- In reply 4 it dropped the second clause without giving the reason. Caveat: the user's message 4 did allow one idea per headline.
- The user restored the exact two-clause wording in message 5. Only then did the agent say "Your exact headline exceeds the template's word limit."
- To pass the gate, the agent patched the installed helper. I diffed `project/src/packaging/draft.py`, `package-format/findings-template.md` and `package-format/manifest-template.md` against the release: they add a `headline_length_exceptions` bypass.
- The user's feedback (`feedback/human.md` items 2 and 23) says they had never heard of the limit, that the README should mention it, and that restoring the wording cost about half a turn. The agent's feedback ranks it as its first major pain point.

**co2-B (real but milder)**
- Transcript line 396: the agent dropped "45 countries cut emissions while growing" from the user-approved Answer headline "to fit your wording within the 15-word headline limit."
- It said so and offered to restore it, and the user accepted. Approved content still changed because of a limit the user only learned about afterwards.

**taxi-B (weak evidence)**
- The headlines the user approved were multi-sentence summaries. The agent wrote that preview before invoking awb-package, ignoring a template rule it should have read. Reply 5 then disclosed "Headline wording was tightened from the version you approved."
- The Newark $564.64 lead in the zone headline is more the agent's choice of key number than something the cap forced. A 15-word "few-trip zones lead; JFK leads 10,000+ zones" headline would have fit.
- This run supports the finding only loosely, consistent with its earlier "unclear" tag.

**Note on the cited IDs**
- In `taxi-B/feedback/findings.json`, taxi-B-21 is an unrelated check-draft finding, and co2-B-38 does not exist there. I checked the cited passages in the transcripts directly instead.

**Conclusion:** a real user on a normal interactive host who asks for a headline longer than 15 words hits a hard release blocker. The release gives no override and does not disclose the limit to the user, so the agent must silently trim, argue, or edit the helper. Major severity is defensible.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:1772 (HEADLINE_WORDS = 15) and :2019-2020 (failing outline row, no exemption); awb-release/SKILL.md:24-26 (release gate refuses on any check-draft row); awb-package/references/review.md:33-35 (only review-rule warnings are user-acceptable); cap stated only in agent-facing awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:14, references/package-contract.md:45 and references/helpers.md:28; no mention in README.md:11 or :66-70 or in the awb-package/SKILL.md:43-52 headline checkpoint

consolidated.title: Ranking thresholds and exclusions are set or proposed after seeing results, without asking
consolidated.description: awb-scope and awb-clean have a rule that a method choice the brief does not settle is the user's decision; analysis.md has no such rule for a threshold, minimum or exclusion, and nothing says to fix one before looking at the leaders. taxi-B applied a 1,000-trip ranking minimum inside a query without asking. It then recommended a 10,000-trip minimum because unusual zones led, and recommended dropping rate-code-99 card trips whose zero tips contradicted the agreed zeros-included median. taxi-A recorded single-trip zones in a top-ten ranking only as a limitation, and the user had to set the floor. retail-A's released cancellation ranking still includes an item whose value is almost entirely one event. taxi-A-12 and retail-A-28 were tagged unclear (single judgments); taxi-B's two documented instances support product. Oct 15 section 7 reported retail-A's cancellation ranking dominated by one-off orders.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-04: reply 3 'With the current minimum of 1,000 trips'; msg 4 'I hadn't agreed to the 1,000-trip minimum'. taxi-B-05: reply 3 'I recommend leaving them out' and 'I recommend a 10,000-trip minimum'; msg 4 'unusual results alone aren't grounds to drop them'. taxi-A-12: transcript lines 91 and 119. retail-A-28: £6,539.40 of the item's £6,576.57 is one event.

verdicts.reasoning:
The central instance is taxi-B, and no harness cause holds up there. The other runs show at most a weaker form of the problem.

taxi-B: the agent was Claude under claude -p, resuming the same session each turn.
- At the start of turn 3 it read project/workbench-guides/analysis.md (file_path in relay/agent-003.jsonl).
- It then added `min_zone_trips = 1000` to settings.toml on its own (agent-003.jsonl, tool call at line ~95). The user's message 3 mentions no minimum; it only says 'proceed with exploration and all five answers', which a real user would also say.
- After the ranking ran and small Queens zones led, it recorded 'What minimum number of valid trips should a pickup zone need...' as a user decision (line ~196). Its reply recommended 10,000.
- The relay is clean: the harness log shows normal turns and no relay mistakes.
- The agent's own feedback (feedback/agent.md item 3) blames the same gap.

Harness explanations I tested and rejected:
1. The headless host has no AskUserQuestion tool (the init tool list shows only the awb MCP tools). This doesn't matter. The agent did not treat 1,000 as a decision when it set it, so a mid-turn ask tool would not have been used. The release itself says to ask in the reply message (AGENTS.md line 30).
2. Persona front-loading: neither persona brief mentions a minimum.
3. Model role: Claude as the agent is a real product configuration.
4. The simulated home folder, the sandbox and MCP auto-approval have no bearing on this.

The release gap is real:
- analysis.md (Add a result section) says nothing about a threshold, minimum or exclusion added during analysis being the user's decision, or about fixing one before seeing the leaders.
- awb-clean SKILL.md (Decide) says the user decides changes of meaning, and awb-scope line 42 says to ask about method choices. Both apply only during scoping or cleaning.
- Both agents (Claude in taxi-B, Codex in taxi-A) missed the zone floor at scoping, and nothing in the analysis step catches it.

Weaknesses that keep confidence at medium:
- The rate-code-99 exclusion was put to the user as a decision, not applied. It also had data-quality grounds beyond the result: every such trip records a zero tip, all from one vendor, with an unknown rate code. The 10,000 minimum was likewise asked, not applied.
- retail-A: the £10,000 threshold was asked during scoping, before any results. The agent disclosed the one-off £6,539.40 flannel cancellation (transcript line 247), and the persona accepted the ranking. That is a disclosed judgment call, not an unasked threshold.
- taxi-A: the Codex agent applied no threshold and flagged the single-trip leaders (line 91). It only failed to propose a floor.
- The evidence labels are wrong. In the runs' findings.json, taxi-B-05 is about drift between findings and the release, and retail-A-28 is about a CLI --project flag. Neither is about this issue.

Only one documented case shows a threshold set without asking (taxi-B's 1,000). That case is not a harness artifact, and the missing release rule plausibly causes it.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:9-19 (the 'Add a result' section has no rule that a result-level threshold, minimum or exclusion is a user decision). Compare awb-clean/SKILL.md:32 ('The user decides every other issue, because each changes meaning') and awb-scope/SKILL.md:42 ('ask the user every open decision... method choices included'). Both apply only during cleaning or scoping. Run evidence: taxi-B/relay/agent-003.jsonl, where the agent reads analysis.md and then writes min_zone_trips = 1000 into settings.toml.

verdicts.reasoning:
Verdict: product. The taxi-B evidence is solid, the gap in the release is real, and the other two runs add little.

What the run evidence shows:

1. **taxi-B holds up.** The transcript has reply 3 saying "With the current minimum of 1,000 trips" and message 4 saying "I hadn't agreed to the 1,000-trip minimum either". The relay log (agent-003.jsonl) shows the agent writing `min_zone_trips = 1000` into settings.toml with a script while it built the results, without asking. The investigation's history.md (line 131) admits it: "drops the 1,000-trip minimum I had applied without agreement".
   - After seeing that unusual zones led the ranking, the agent proposed a 10,000-trip minimum.
   - After seeing that rate-code-99 card trips with zero tips pulled the Brooklyn and Bronx medians to 0%, it proposed dropping them. That contradicts the agreed rule that zero tips count.
   - Both of those were put to the user with a recommendation and an alternative, so they were asked. They were post-hoc proposals, not silent changes. Only the 1,000-trip minimum was applied without asking.
   - The user's brief did not prompt the objection; the user raised it unprompted. The user (feedback/human.md, pain point 1, rated major) and the agent (feedback/agent.md, item 3) each blamed the same gap.

2. **taxi-A is weak.** Line 91 shows the Codex agent saw single-trip leading zones and recorded only a limitation. Line 119 shows the user setting the 1,000-trip floor. Nothing was set without asking. The agent just never proposed a floor, which is why the run tagged it unclear.

3. **retail-A does not support the finding.**
   - The £10,000 threshold was proposed during scoping and agreed before any results (transcript lines 35 and 67).
   - Leaving out the storage jar was the user's own request (line 128).
   - The flannel item's £6,539.40 single cancellation was disclosed (line 247), and the user accepted all five answers. Under the agreed definition it is a real cancellation, so this is not a threshold or exclusion set after the results.

4. **Two cited IDs are wrong.** In findings.json, taxi-B-05 is a different finding (records drifting from the released package) and retail-A-28 is about a CLI flag. The quoted taxi-B text does exist in the transcript, as reply 3 and message 4.

What the release says:

- **analysis.md has no rule on who decides.** Its "Add a result" section (lines 9 to 17) never says that a threshold, minimum or exclusion the brief does not settle is the user's decision. It also never says to fix one before looking at the leaders. Its scope judgment only asks for explicit filters to be described.
- **awb-explore permits unasked exclusions.** At line 49 it tells the agent to make question-specific exclusions itself and "say so", not ask.
- **The other skills do have the rule.** awb-scope line 42 says to ask about every open decision, method choices included. awb-clean line 31 says "The user decides every other issue, because each changes meaning".
- **The nearest guard is in the wrong place.** awb-explore line 22 says "settings change only when the user settles a population or period choice". But that is in the explore skill, not in the analysis guide the agent reads when adding results, which is when taxi-B added the minimum.
- **The AGENTS.md invariant is only a soft guard.** At line 38 it says "Preserve results that challenge the expected explanation". That works against the rate-code-99 proposal, but it says nothing about ranking floors.

Conclusion: a real user on a normal host would hit this whenever a ranking or minimum comes up that scoping did not foresee. Confidence is medium rather than high because only one run cleanly documents it as product.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:9-17 ("Add a result": no rule that a threshold, minimum or exclusion is the user's decision, and nothing about fixing one before seeing results); awb-explore/SKILL.md:49 (the agent makes local exclusions itself and must only "say so"); contrast awb-clean/SKILL.md:31 ("The user decides every other issue, because each changes meaning") and awb-scope/SKILL.md:42 (ask about every open decision, "method choices included"); the partial guard awb-explore/SKILL.md:22 ("settings change only when the user settles a population or period choice") is only in the explore skill, not in the analysis guide.

consolidated.title: Review-forced edits change user-approved text, and release freezes them unseen
consolidated.description: After the user approved slides or text, review repairs, review rules and contract rules kept rewriting it, even after the user asked for no more unrelated wording changes. review.md lets the user accept only warning-severity violations, so there is no way to accept or waive a narrative finding. At release, the mandatory full review forced edits that were frozen into 001 in the same turn without being shown to the user: a rewritten Newark line plus trims in taxi-B, and 'every country' changed to 'the countries behind each ranking' in co2-B. #64's rule to show the changed slides covers only revisions the user requested. retail-B's full draft also departed from the approved preview: exact figures, a reworded approved headline and an unannounced appendix slide.
consolidated.evidence: co2-B-02: U7 'avoid another round of unrelated wording changes'; A7 lists six review-required changes to approved slides. taxi-B-10: reply 7 'I'll trim other lines', then 'Releasing.'. co2-B-34: A8 'Repairing it as a package revision', then released. retail-B-14: A5 'Headlines that differ from the preview'; 3 appendix slides instead of 2. Release: awb-release step 2; awb-package Delivery milestone.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not trace the main mechanism to the harness.

Relay and setup:
- The relay inputs agent-007.in.md and agent-008.in.md in co2-B are the user's words exactly as written, and taxi-B's U7 is the same.
- The persona never said "release without seeing it".
- The agent system prompt tells the agent to end its turn when it needs an answer, so nothing in the harness pushed it to finish in one turn.

Both release-time freezes come from the release text:
- awb-release step 2 says a narrative problem or error "stops the release; repairs are package revisions through awb-package, which reviews again". It does not say to show the repaired text or wait for the user before running `release`.
- awb-package's Delivery milestone requires showing the changed slides and waiting only for "A revision requested with it", meaning one the user asked for.
- review.md's After the review says a passing review needs no error and no narrative problem, and that the user may accept only `warning` violations. The user has no way to waive a narrative finding.

What happened in the runs:
- **co2-B:** U7 asked to avoid more unrelated wording changes. In A7 the agent flagged the conflict in its notes ("The skill gives no way to accept/waive narrative problems with user consent"), made the edits anyway and listed six review-required changes. In A8 the release review changed "every country behind the rankings" to "the countries behind each ranking". The diff of review-copy vs released/001 findings.md confirms the change was frozen in the same turn, and the user was told only afterwards.
- **taxi-B:** in A7 the release review raised an error, a fix to the Newark line, and then a word-count warning. The agent trimmed other lines of the approved note rather than ask, then said "Releasing." The released methodology-note.md drops lines the user had approved in A6, for example "both months start on a Monday and have 31 days" and the named airport-study and tipping decisions.

Harness factors I considered:
- **Auto-approved tools:** the relay passes `--allowedTools` for Bash, Edit and mcp__awb. On an interactive Claude Code host in default mode, the user might see edit diffs or a permission prompt for the release command.
- **Hidden progress text:** the prompt says the user sees only the final reply, but a real host shows interim text such as "I'll trim other lines".

Neither is a gate the product designs or relies on. Users in accept-edits mode would not see the diffs, and approving a release command does not show what text changed. Two separate Claude agents read step 2 the same way, as repair and continue within the turn, which points to the text rather than one model's quirk.

Parts of the finding are overstated:
- **retail-B:** the departures were announced in A5 under "Headlines that differ from the preview" and "3 in the appendix rather than 2", with an offer to restore the original France headline. The user approved them in U6 ("the extra supporting-tables appendix slide is fine"), and retail-B's release review was clean with no edits. So "unannounced" is wrong, and retail-B does not support "frozen unseen".
- **co2-B A7:** those changes were shown and then approved in U8.

The supported core is narrower: narrative findings cannot be waived, and repairs at release are frozen without being shown first. That rests on co2-B A8 and taxi-B A7, and its cause is the release text.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-release/SKILL.md:18 (narrative problem 'stops the release; repairs are package revisions through awb-package, which reviews again'; no show-before-freeze step); awb-package/SKILL.md:97 (show-and-wait limited to 'A revision requested with it'); awb-package/references/review.md:33 (passed review requires no narrative problem; user may accept only warning violations). Corroboration: co2-B project/deliveries/.../review-copy/findings.md:158 'every country behind the rankings' vs released/001/findings.md:160 'the countries behind each ranking'; taxi-B released/001/methodology-note.md trimmed vs A6-approved text.

verdicts.reasoning:
The central claim holds in co2-B and taxi-B, and the shipped text causes it. Two parts of the finding are overstated, and retail-B does not show the problem.

What the release says:
- awb-release step 2 makes a full review mandatory at every release request. An error violation or a narrative problem stops the release, and the fix is a package revision through awb-package. The same step then expects the agent to "review again in full" within this release request, so it assumes the repair and the release both happen in that one request.
- Nothing in awb-release says to show the repaired text to the user and wait for a yes before running `release`.
- The only show-and-wait rule is awb-package's Delivery milestone, the #64 rule. It covers only "A revision requested with it", meaning a change the user asked for. README line 86 promises the same, only for changes the user requested.
- review.md "After the review" lets the user accept only warning violations. Error violations and narrative problems must be repaired, so the user cannot waive a reviewer's finding on text they already approved.
- README line 71 tells users the release will ask about draft labels and warnings. It does not say the release may rewrite approved text.

Run evidence, checked in the transcripts and relay logs:
- **co2-B, reply 8:** The user had approved everything. The release review (relay agent-008) reported one narrative problem: "Three tables let donors check every country behind the rankings." The agent changed it to "the countries behind each ranking", re-reviewed, and released 001 in the same turn. The user saw the change only in the report after the freeze. The simulated user rated it minor ("preserves the meaning I approved").
- **taxi-B, reply 7:** The user approved the revised note in message 7. The first release review (relay agent-007) raised an error, R-rates-001, against a Newark line in methodology-note.md. That same line had passed the previous clean review, so the reviewer drifted. The agent rewrote the line. The second review raised the 500-word warning. The agent said "Rather than ask you to accept it, I'll trim other lines". The trims then caused a narrative problem, which it repaired before a fourth review came back clean, and then "Releasing." The user never saw the trimmed lines. The report after release quotes only the Newark line. The trims were partly the agent's choice: the release allowed asking the user to accept the warning. The Newark rewrite itself was forced by the review.
- **co2-B, earlier rounds:** Message 7 did ask to avoid unrelated wording changes, and reply 7 does list six changes the review required. But that reply showed them before release and offered to undo them, and the user approved in message 8. Before release this was churn the user saw, not a freeze they didn't see. The lack of a waiver is still real: if the user had undone those changes, the review would have blocked the release again.
- **retail-B:** This run does not support the "frozen unseen" part. Reply 5 told the user about every departure from the preview under "Headlines that differ from the preview": exact figures, the France/Australia headline flagged by a rule built from the user's own earlier correction, and a third appendix slide with the reason. In message 6 the user approved the extra slide and asked for rounding. The release turn changed no text. Calling the appendix slide "unannounced" is wrong.
- **Cited IDs:** Several IDs do not match findings.json. taxi-B-10 and retail-B-14 are different findings; the matching one is retail-B-11; co2-B-34 does not exist. The quoted text does match the transcripts.

Bottom line: a real user on a normal host would hit this whenever the mandatory release review finds something in approved text, and reviewer drift makes that likely. Repairs then go into the frozen numbered release without approval, because the instructions never require showing review-forced repairs before `release`. Severity is closer to minor-to-major than clearly major: in both affected runs the changes were small accuracy repairs, and both were at least partly disclosed after the freeze.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-release/SKILL.md:18 (an error or narrative problem stops the release; repairs go through awb-package; "Within this release request, review again in full" — no step to show repairs or wait for approval before `release`); awb-package/SKILL.md:97 (Delivery milestone shows changed slides and waits for a yes only for "A revision requested with it"); awb-package/references/review.md:33 (a review passes only when the user "has accepted every warning violation" — errors and narrative problems cannot be waived); README.md:71 and :86 (release questions cover only draft labels and warnings; changed slides are shown only for a change the user asks for)

consolidated.title: awb sql cannot bind parameters, and its read-only refusal advises dropping --read-only
consolidated.description: A saved query that uses settings $parameters cannot be tried through awb sql. The CLI takes only --limit, --out and --read-only, and the MCP read sql tool always passes --read-only and has no parameter input. Under read-only, any EXPLAIN failure, whether unbound parameters or an ordinary ambiguous-column binder error, is reported as 'refused a statement whose plan cannot be checked ... run it without --read-only', which steers agents toward write mode. A missing relative .sql path is parsed as SQL text. Oct 15 taxi-A hit the same unbound-parameter error through MCP SQL.
consolidated.oct15_ref: Oct 15 per-run taxi-A agent.md (MCP SQL: prepared-statement parameters not provided); not in fix-plan
consolidated.evidence: retail-A-03: agent-notes 'Values were not provided for the following prepared statement parameters: cohort_end, ...; run it without --read-only'; awb_landing.py lines 1300-1301. co2-A-07: binder error on an ambiguous 'year' column. retail-B-24: 'awb.py sql --help' shows only --limit, --out and --read-only. retail-B-25: 'syntax error at or near queries'.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none. Every piece of the finding comes from fixed code in the release and shows up the same way on two different agent hosts: Codex over MCP in retail-A and co2-A, and Claude calling the CLI directly in retail-B.

1) No way to bind parameters. cli_sql (awb_landing.py:1519-1533) defines only query, --limit, --out and --read-only. retail-B relay agent-002.jsonl captures the real `sql --help` output showing exactly those options. The MCP read tool always builds `[sql, --read-only, ..., --, query]` (awb_mcp.py:345-351) and its schema has no parameter field. Meanwhile result queries are designed to use settings `$name` parameters (settings.toml:7, run.py:47). The project's own AGENTS.md:24 tells agents to "run every query with awb.py sql". So the release pushes agents into this path, and the agents did not invent it. Without --read-only, connection.sql(text) fails on unbound parameters too, so neither mode can run such a query.

2) Misleading refusal. _refuse_writing_plan (awb_landing.py:1287-1301) catches every exception from EXPLAIN. Unless the failure is the missing-excel-extension case, it re-raises as "refused a statement whose plan cannot be checked (...); run it without --read-only". That covers unbound parameters (retail-A, MCP read sql on queries/validation.sql, reported verbatim in agent.md:69 and agent-notes.md:30) and plain binder errors (co2-A, ambiguous "year", which I confirmed in raw tool output in relay/agent-003.jsonl). In both cases the advice is wrong, because dropping --read-only fixes neither error.

3) A missing path becomes SQL. _sql_argument (awb_landing.py:1490-1497) falls back to treating the argument as SQL text when no file exists. Raw output in retail-B agent-002.jsonl shows `Parser Error: syntax error at or near "queries"` for five queries/*.sql paths given relative to the investigation folder.

Harness causes ruled out:
- The sandbox and the simulated home folder do not affect these deterministic DuckDB errors.
- Auto-approval does not matter, because the read tool forces --read-only by design.
- No relay or persona input is involved.

One harness factor slightly softens the impact without being the cause. Following the advice would mean calling the write-capable data tool, which a normal interactive host would put behind a permission prompt; the sims auto-approved MCP tools.

Caveats:
- The cited IDs retail-A-03, retail-B-24 and retail-B-25 point to unrelated entries in findings.json. The real evidence is in agent.md and agent-notes.md (retail-A item 3; retail-B notes lines 24 and 26), and only co2-A-07 matches.
- retail-B's own "Values were not provided" error came from run.py after the agent mis-sliced its settings file, not from awb sql.
- Neither agent actually dropped --read-only, so "steers agents toward write mode" describes a wrong message, not harm that was observed.
- The Oct 15 taxi-A instance is not in the current taxi-A folder.
- The wrong-folder path error was partly the agent's fault, since the help text says paths are project-relative.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/awb_landing.py:1300-1301 (any EXPLAIN failure becomes "run it without --read-only"); awb_landing.py:1524-1533 (cli_sql defines only query/--limit/--out/--read-only, no parameter binding); awb_landing.py:1490-1497 (_sql_argument treats a missing path as SQL text); awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py:345-351 (read sql always passes --read-only and takes no parameters); awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:24 ("run every query with awb.py sql") alongside workbench/investigation/settings.toml:7 (result queries read $name parameters)

verdicts.reasoning:
The shipped code does what the finding says, and all three runs show it happening.

Cause in the release:
(1) Parameters can't be bound. `cli_sql` (awb_landing.py:1519-1531) takes only a query, --limit, --out and --read-only. The MCP read tool (awb_mcp.py:345-351) only accepts command, query and limit, and always builds `sql --read-only -- <query>`. The only thing that binds settings `$name` parameters is run.py's `run()` (investigation/run.py:45-48). Running run.py also overwrites results, evidence and the state.md row, so it is not a way to try a query. Meanwhile AGENTS.md:24 tells agents to "run every query with `awb.py sql`". So the documented path fails on any saved result query that uses `$start` and the like.
(2) Misleading refusal. In read-only mode, `_refuse_writing_plan` catches every EXPLAIN failure (awb_landing.py:1298) and raises "refused a statement whose plan cannot be checked (...); run it without --read-only" (lines 1300-1301). That covers unbound parameters and ordinary binder errors such as an ambiguous column. The advice is wrong in both cases. For a binder error the fix is in the SQL. For unbound parameters, running without --read-only still fails: I checked with the project's own duckdb, and plain `connection.sql('select $start')` raises "Binder Error: Unexpected prepared parameter". So the message points agents toward write mode for nothing.
(3) A missing path becomes SQL. `_sql_argument` (awb_landing.py:1488-1496) resolves the argument against the project root. If no file is there, it returns the argument as SQL text, which gives a bare parser error.

Run evidence checks out:
- retail-A/feedback/agent-notes.md:30 has the exact MCP read-sql error ("Values were not provided for the following prepared statement parameters: cohort_end, ... ; run it without --read-only").
- co2-A/feedback/agent.md:77 and agent-notes.md:44 have the ambiguous "year" binder error wrapped in the same message.
- retail-B/referee/logs/agent-002.txt:49 shows the `sql --help` call. retail-B agent-notes record that `awb.py sql` takes no parameters and that `syntax error at or near "queries"` came from running a relative path from the investigation folder.

Caveats:
- The retail-B relative-path case partly comes from the agent ignoring awb-explore/SKILL.md:41 ("run it from the project root"). The fall-through to SQL text with no "file not found" hint is still the product's doing.
- Every agent ignored the escalation advice and recovered, using literal values, a fixed qualifier, or by iterating through run.py. retail-B rated its part minor. "Major" may be too high, but the defect is real and the release causes it.
- The Oct 15 taxi-A instance is from an earlier round. It does not appear in the current taxi-A folder.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/awb_landing.py:1298-1301 (every EXPLAIN failure becomes "plan cannot be checked ...; run it without --read-only"); awb_landing.py:1519-1531 (cli_sql takes only query/--limit/--out/--read-only, no parameter binding); awb_landing.py:1488-1496 (_sql_argument treats a missing path as SQL text); awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py:345-351 (MCP read sql always passes --read-only, no parameter input); awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/run.py:45-48 (only run() binds $name parameters); awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:24 ("run every query with `awb.py sql`")

consolidated.title: Fresh reviewers give inconsistent verdicts on unchanged text
consolidated.description: This is separate from the cost in C-01: the gate assumes the reviewer finds everything in one pass, and it does not. In retail-B, the approved France/Australia headline passed R-concentration-001 in passes 2-4, then was flagged as an error in pass 5 with the text unchanged.
