Rules without a pattern are judged by reading, and that reading varies between passes. In co2-B, one pass had the agent remove a land-use claim as unsupported, and a later pass demanded that the narratives carry the same caveat. A 'clean' review is therefore not a reliable gate.
consolidated.oct15_ref: new; related to fix-plan 6.1, 6.2 (#66 'one exhaustive pass')
consolidated.evidence: retail-B-02: in agent-005.jsonl the text is unchanged from call 8 to call 39; passes 2-4 report 'R-concentration-001 pass', and pass 5 reports violations at findings.md:112, findings.md:129 and methodology.md:148; the rule has 'Pattern: none'. co2-B-05: agent-notes turn 5; state.md caveat 'direction of a land-use effect was never analysed'.

verdicts.reasoning:
The retail-B evidence holds up when checked against the raw transcript, apart from an off-by-one in the pass count. The headline "France's growth came from many buyers; one buyer supplied 96.8% of Australia's" was written at agent-005 call 8 (findings.md) and call 10 (methodology.md). It stayed the same until call 123. The notes line "France's gain is spread more widely than Australia's or Germany's, which rest on very few buyers" was added at call 31, before the second review, and also stayed the same.

There were 12 reviewer runs in all. Counted in order of the Agent calls (19, 34, 47, 66, 89, 106, ...), review 1 flagged only the findings.md:12 bullet. Reviews 2 to 5 each reported "R-concentration-001 pass". Review 6 reported three error violations at findings.md:112, findings.md:129 and methodology.md:148, all on that same text. The finding says "passes 2-4" and "pass 5" because it counts differently. Nothing had changed between reviews 5 and 6 that could explain it:
- the rule text was the same (Pattern: none, line scope);
- the reviewer prompt was identical (I compared the two prompt strings: equal);
- the model was the same (claude-opus-5-5 for every subagent);
- the subagent type was the same (Plan).
The only variable left is the reviewer's own reading.

co2-B gives a cleaner case than the one the finding cites:
- agent-007's final full review (call 224) returned "review: clean". The only later step in that turn was a check-draft run, which writes nothing.
- The awb-release review in agent-008 then flagged the unchanged findings.md:160 line "Three tables let donors check every country behind the rankings."
- The land-use example in the finding is real but softer. A pass in agent-004 flagged "would raise shares of deforesting countries" as unsupported. A later pass in agent-005 demanded the narratives carry the state.md caveat that still said it. The narrative text had changed between those passes, so this is conflicting guidance, not differing verdicts on the same text.

I tried each harness explanation and none fits:
- Non-interactive claude -p, MCP auto-approval and the simulated home folder: none of these changes how a Plan subagent judges text, and an interactive Claude Code session uses the same branch.
- Relay: it played no part inside the turn where this happened.
- Persona: the simulated user's approval of the headline has nothing to do with the reviewers' verdicts.
- The writer's extra notes in the reviewer prompt: reviews 5 and 6 had identical prompts, so these cannot explain the flip.

The cause is the release's design:
- review.md:21 has rules without a pattern "judged by reading" by an LLM.
- review.md:18 and :35 assume the reviewer reports everything "in this one pass".
- review.md:33 makes a clean full review the only gate for completion and release.
A real user on Claude Code following review.md's Claude Code branch would get the same variance. README:112 admits "The checks have limits", but that does not stop the gate from accepting one clean pass as final.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/references/review.md:21 (pattern-less rules "judged by reading"); review.md:18 and :35 (the reviewer is assumed to report every problem "in this one pass"); review.md:33 (only a clean full review completes a request or release); review.md:9-12 (the Claude Code branch uses a Plan subagent, as the sim did). The README:112 caveat "The checks have limits" softens the gate's claim but does not contradict the finding. Run evidence: in retail-B/relay/agent-005.jsonl the headline was written at calls 8/10 and changed at call 123; Agent calls 34/47/66/89 report "R-concentration-001 pass" and call 106 reports 3 violations, with an identical prompt to call 89. In co2-B/relay, agent-007 call 224 reports "review: clean" and agent-008 call 2 flags unchanged findings.md:160.

verdicts.reasoning:
The retail-B evidence holds; I checked it in SIMS/retail-B/relay/agent-005.jsonl.
- The Write at tool call 8 created the headline "### France's growth came from many buyers; one buyer supplied 96.8% of Australia's". Call 10 put the same headline in methodology.md. Call 20 added the notes line "France's gain is spread more widely than Australia's or Germany's, which rest on very few buyers". None of these lines changed until call 39. The edits in between (calls 21, 24, 27, 28, 33-35, 37) touch other wording only.
- The first reviewer (jsonl line 178) flagged the same claim in the summary bullet at findings.md:12, but not in the headline.
- The next four full reviews (lines 262, 323, 400, 516) all report "R-concentration-001 pass" with both lines present. Their prompts are the same apart from added notes on quality.md and rounding, so the prompt did not change what they were asked.
- The next review (line 584, which the agent labelled "fifth pass") reports R-concentration-001 violations at findings.md:112, findings.md:129 and methodology.md:148. The rule in foundation/review-rules.md has "Pattern: none".
- The finding's pass numbers are off by one: four passes, not three, passed the text before it was flagged. That does not change the substance.

The co2-B evidence also holds, with one qualification. In relay/agent-004.jsonl line 329, a reviewer called "which would raise the shares of countries with large historical deforestation" unsupported. The agent changed it to "would change these shares (not analysed here)" but left the state.md caveat saying "would raise". About ten later full reviews read state.md and passed. Then the review at relay/agent-005.jsonl line 776 flagged that the narratives drop the direction state.md records. The same thing happened later: the Answer slide's "land-use change is excluded" passed many reviews unchanged, then was flagged at agent-007.jsonl line 731. Part of the co2-B contradiction is the agent's fault for not updating state.md. Even so, the verdicts on unchanged text varied from pass to pass.

The cause is in the release:
- The agents' copies of awb-package match the release byte for byte (diff -r, __pycache__ excluded).
- awb_draft.py `review-rules add` makes "Pattern: none (judged by reading)" the default.
- review.md Brief step 2 has fresh reviewers judge pattern-less rules by reading. Step 3 adds open-ended narrative checks, and it does not say whether state.md or methodology.md is the authority for caveats.
- "After the review" treats a single clean full review as the gate for completion and release.
- Nothing in the release records earlier verdicts on unchanged text, lets the user waive a narrative problem, or warns that a full review can miss things. The only such warning covers scoped reviews.
- The only safeguard is the line "Report every violation and narrative problem in this one pass". The agent followed it in every brief, and it did not make the verdicts consistent.

A real user on Claude Code would get the same result. The fresh Plan subagent the release prescribes was used exactly as written, and the simulated human played no part in the reviewer verdicts.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/references/review.md:21 ("`no match`, `no pattern`, and `unchecked` rules are judged by reading"); review.md:22 (open-ended step 3 narrative checks, with no rule on whether state.md or methodology.md is the authority for caveats); review.md:33 (a review passes when its last line shows no error violation, no narrative problem and no command problem, so a single clean pass is the gate); review.md:37 (warns only that a scoped re-review can miss problems, not a full one); awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:3841-3842 (`--pattern` help: "default: none, judged by reading")

consolidated.title: Chat answers state untested explanations as findings
consolidated.description: In chat and in preview headlines, agents presented interpretations the data had not tested. Examples: December's low rate as 'probably Christmas-season buyers'; growth 'spread across many accounts' when three accounts supplied 99.6% of Germany's growth; early cohorts as certainly 'overstated'; repeated lines as 'double-scanned', with a recommendation to remove them; and code-0 totals as undercounted because fees were missing, which a check disproved when the user asked. #62 added 'present an explanation the data has not tested as a question', yet in retail-B this recurred across three replies. No check covers chat or preview headlines. taxi-B-16 was tagged unclear because it happened once.
consolidated.oct15_ref: fix-plan 7; synthesis section 7 (retail-B untested explanations); #62 change 5
consolidated.evidence: retail-B-03: quotes from A2, A3 and A4; corrections in U3 and U4; agent-notes turn 3 admits breaking the AGENTS.md rule. retail-B-13: A2 'They look like double-scanned lines. My recommendation: remove them.' taxi-B-16: the claim in reply 2; the residual analysis in reply 3 disproved it.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none. The agent volunteered every untested explanation itself, and the harness gave it no push toward any of them.

What the transcripts show:
- **retail-B reply 2:** "These are probably Christmas-season buyers." France and Germany "have broad customer bases, so their growth is spread across many accounts." Repeated lines "look like double-scanned lines. My recommendation: remove them."
- **retail-B reply 3:** "January to March are overstated."
- **retail-B reply 4:** the preview headline "depends on a few accounts, at home and overseas". The user's notes say the "at home" part was not established by the evidence shown.
- **taxi-B reply 2:** code-0 "total paid figure undercounts" because the airport fee is missing. In reply 3 the agent's own check disproved it ("So the empty fields don't show that totals are too low").

All the quotes match `relay/agent-002.out.md`, so the relay passed them through unchanged.

Harness causes I tested:
- **User prompting:** neither user brought these explanations up. retail-B U2 asked only for quantitative answers, and in taxi-B the user had only said not to treat code 0 alone as proof of an invalid trip.
- **Persona brief:** the retail persona brief says nothing about Christmas, double-scanning or growth spread, so it did not front-load any of them.
- **Agent system prompt:** it says to "Behave exactly as you normally would". It covers home, boundaries and turn mechanics, and nothing about interpretation.
- **Codex user's vigilance:** the persona's "do not accept vague answers" instruction only explains why the claims were caught. A real non-expert user would be less likely to catch them, which makes the problem worse for real users, not a simulation effect.
- **Headless `claude -p`, auto-approved MCP tools, the simulated home:** none of these touches what the agent writes in chat.
- **Rule exposure:** the agent read the AGENTS.md template in full in turn 1 (`cat` in agent-001). The installed Claude Code is 2.1.301, which reads AGENTS.md when no CLAUDE.md exists, and I found no CLAUDE.md in the project or any folder above it. Each turn is a new resumed process, so the harness probably gave the agent more exposure to the rule than an interactive session would. In an interactive session, AGENTS.md is created mid-session by awb-init and would not be loaded until a restart.
- **Admission:** agent-notes turn 3 says it broke the AGENTS.md rule ("offer an untested explanation as a question") in chat.

Why the release is the cause:
- The rule exists in one sentence of the project AGENTS.md. Nothing in `analysis.md` or the awb-package preview step repeats it.
- The checks that exist only look at finding text and draft files. The finding-number warning on `state finding` catches numbers, and check-draft catches causal phrases in drafts. Chat replies and preview headlines get no check, which is what the agent said and the finding claims.
- The README (line 83) promises users that "An untested explanation comes back as a question, not an answer". The run broke that promise twice: in four retail-B replies and once in taxi-B.

Problems with the finding itself:
- **Wrong IDs:** the evidence IDs do not match the runs' `findings.json`. The matching entries are retail-B-02 (product), retail-B-10 (product) and taxi-B-11 (unclear). The cited retail-B-03, retail-B-13 and taxi-B-16 are about double rounding and export step order.
- **Wrong tag claim:** the finding says "taxi-B-16 was tagged unclear"; it is taxi-B-11 that was tagged unclear. The evidence underneath is real and supports the finding.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:38: the rule ("offer an untested explanation as a question, not an answer") appears only here and nothing enforces it. README.md:83 promises users that an untested explanation comes back as a question. awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:17: the only warning (on `state finding`) covers numbers and "sums to"/"checked every" wording, not interpretations in chat or preview headlines.

verdicts.reasoning:
The run evidence holds, though the cited IDs are wrong. In findings.json the cited items are retail-B-02 (interpretations beyond the evidence), retail-B-10 ('double-scanned') and taxi-B-11 (code-0 totals, tagged unclear). The numbers the finding gives (retail-B-03, retail-B-13, taxi-B-16) belong to other findings: rounding, export order, and export with no draft.

retail-B transcript:
- Reply 2, line 114: 'These are probably Christmas-season buyers.'
- Reply 2, line 141: 'France (86 buyers) and Germany (94) have broad customer bases, so their growth is spread across many accounts.' The agent had not checked this. Its own check in reply 3 found that Germany's top three buyers supplied 99.6% of its growth.
- Reply 2, lines 144-145: 'They look like double-scanned lines. My recommendation: remove them.'
- Reply 3, line 214: 'January to March are overstated.' This came after the user had already corrected the other two claims in U3. The user corrected it again in U4.
- Reply 4: the preview headline 'depends on a few accounts, at home and overseas'. The persona's notes (filed one turn late, under Turn 5) flag 'at home' as not established.
So the problem appears in three replies, one of which is a set of preview headlines. In agent-notes turn 3 the agent says it broke the AGENTS.md invariant in chat.

taxi-B reply 2, line 106: 'their total paid figure undercounts'. The user challenged this in message 3, and the check in reply 3 disproved it. This happened once.

Harness: I ruled it out.
- The harness note in message 1 only asks for a friction log.
- Each turn resumes the same session, and the working folder is the project.
- No CLAUDE.md exists in the project or any folder above it, so Claude Code reads the project's AGENTS.md.
- The installed AGENTS.md is byte-identical to the release template.
- The agent read AGENTS.md during turn 1 (agent-001.jsonl, line 12).
A real Claude Code user would get the same setup.

Release: the release states the rule clearly, which would normally point to 'unsupported'. But the agent broke it repeatedly and kept doing so after being corrected, so the rule as shipped is not enough. It is one sentence among the Analytical invariants (AGENTS.md:38), with a matching promise in README.md:83. It is not repeated where chat answers are written:
- the Conversation section (AGENTS.md:28-30)
- the analysis guide's reporting step
- awb-status
- awb-package's headline checkpoint (awb-package/SKILL.md:43-52)
- awb-clean's decision table
awb-clean/SKILL.md:26 also files duplicate-rows under 'Shared cleaning rule', described as 'an error in the data itself ... such as a row landed twice'. Line 31 then requires a 'proposed treatment' for each issue. Together these push toward the 'double-scanned, remove them' framing.

The claim that no check covers chat is true: `state finding` and check-draft check only numbers and certain wordings in records and drafts. A mechanical check over chat is not realistic, though, so the fix belongs in where the guidance sits, not in a new check.

Limits on this verdict: the cited IDs are wrong, taxi-B has one instance, and the preview-headline evidence is thin.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:38 states the rule ('offer an untested explanation as a question, not an answer'); README.md:83 makes the same promise. It is not repeated where chat is written: AGENTS.md:28-30 (Conversation), awb-package/SKILL.md:43-52 (headline checkpoint), awb-status/SKILL.md. awb-clean/SKILL.md:26 files duplicate-rows as 'an error in the data itself ... a row landed twice', and awb-clean/SKILL.md:31 requires a 'proposed treatment'; together they push the double-scanned recommendation.

consolidated.title: No scan or decision rule for rows duplicated across sheets or extracts
consolidated.description: The UCI workbook's two sheets overlap on 1-9 December 2010: 22,523 lines, about £377k. awb-clean's duplicate check matches only exact rows, so the lineage columns (sheet, sheet_row) defeat it, and there is no step for overlapping extracts or partitions. retail-B found the overlap only through its own date-range check. awb-clean is also ambiguous about who decides: it lets the agent fix 'duplicate-rows under a recorded grain', but says the user decides 'whether repeated rows ... are errors and which row wins'. As a result, retail-A left a proven exact overlap as an open limitation, handled by a sheet split local to the investigation, while retail-B removed it on its own.
consolidated.oct15_ref: new (the Oct 15 retail agents also found the overlap only through their own checks)
consolidated.evidence: retail-B-07: clean-scan ran with --key sheet,sheet_row; scan_dataset.py 'duplicate-rows' matches exact rows only (checks.md line 9); the referee confirmed the overlap with EXCEPT ALL. retail-A-09: awb-clean step 2; agent-notes scope-settled entry. retail-B-34: awb-clean SKILL line 31.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none. Both halves of the finding come from the release.

1) Scan blind spot. In scan_dataset.py, duplicates() groups by every column (`GROUP BY {everything}`), so a lineage column makes every row unique. In retail-B the scan options were `keys: ["sheet,sheet_row"]` (foundation/scans/online_retail_lines.json), and the baseline issue list has no duplicate-rows entry at all. The agent's own queries found two things the scan missed:
- the 22,523-line, £377,488 cross-sheet copy (0 mismatched lines);
- 12,133 exact repeats within a single sheet.

The referee's EXCEPT ALL check (referee/check1.py) confirms the overlap. Both agents added sheet/row lineage columns as the declared key: Codex used source_sheet,source_row in retail-A and Claude used sheet,sheet_row in retail-B. Two different models doing the same thing points to the release, not to one model's habit. The release asks for a declared key/grain (datasets.toml `key`, catalog grain, then awb-clean `--key` from the grain), and an invoice-line workbook has no natural key. No release doc mentions overlapping extracts or sheets: grep for "overlap" in the release .md files returns nothing. checks.md does not warn that lineage columns hide duplicates.

2) Unclear who decides. awb-clean SKILL line 26 lists "a row landed twice" as a shared cleaning rule. Line 31 lets the agent decide "duplicate-rows under a recorded grain", but leaves to the user "whether repeated rows or keys are errors and which row wins". Under the recorded grain (sheet,sheet_row) the cross-sheet copies are not duplicates, so neither path clearly applies. The two agents read the skill and split:
- retail-A read awb-clean/SKILL.md in turn 2 (relay/agent-002.jsonl). Its agent-notes say "awb-clean would ask the user which repeated rows win even when the two sheets have identical December overlap". It kept the overlap as an open limitation (DQ-003) and split by sheet inside the investigation only.
- retail-B removed the overlap itself in the canonical view (DQ-012), then asked the user about the within-sheet repeats.

Harness factors I ruled out:
- Personas front-loading: neither persona brief mentions the overlap, and the retail-A user called it something they didn't know about.
- Non-interactive relay: asking was possible, and retail-B did ask about the within-sheet repeats.
- Harness prompt: it says "work exactly as you normally would".
- Sandbox, simulated home folder and MCP auto-approval have no bearing on the scan code or the skill text.

One difference does come from the personas: the retail-A user said "bring the data in", not "clean", so awb-clean was never formally run there. A real user could say the same, and the agent still cited awb-clean's wording as its reason. This is the release's scan code and skill wording, on public data a real user could load.

Caveat: the finding cites the wrong finding IDs. retail-B-07, retail-A-09 and retail-B-34 are unrelated findings in the current findings.json. The matching ones are retail-B-06, retail-A-08 and retail-B-27. The substance holds.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-clean/scripts/scan_dataset.py:528-537 (duplicates() groups by all columns, so lineage columns make every row unique); awb-clean/references/checks.md:9 (duplicate-rows = rows repeating another row exactly); awb-clean/SKILL.md:26 ("a row landed twice" listed as a shared cleaning rule) vs SKILL.md:31 (agent decides "duplicate-rows under a recorded grain"; user decides "whether repeated rows or keys are errors and which row wins"); awb-clean/SKILL.md:18 (pass the catalog grain as --key); awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/data.md:33,39 (declare key/uniqueness and record grain); no "overlap"/partition guidance anywhere in the release's .md files

verdicts.reasoning:
Both parts of the finding trace to shipped files.

(1) Scan blind spot. In scan_dataset.py, duplicates() builds the duplicate-rows check as GROUP BY over every column in the dataset (`names`, not the `--columns` subset). Nothing lets a caller leave lineage columns out of that match. checks.md line 9 describes the check as exact-row only. retail-B's scan file (project/foundation/scans/online_retail_lines.json) has options keys=['sheet,sheet_row'], and its baseline issues contain no duplicate-rows or duplicate-key entry at all. So the 22,523-line overlap, and also the ~12k within-sheet repeats, were invisible to it. awb-clean steps 1-2 contain no check for overlapping extracts, sheets or partitions. The release's spreadsheet guidance (awb-init/references/landing.md:31) reads one named sheet per read_xlsx call, so a multi-sheet workbook is naturally unioned with a sheet column, which is exactly what defeats the check. retail-B's transcript shows it found the overlap through its own per-sheet date-range comparison ('Each sheet has 22,523 rows for 1-9 Dec 2010...'). referee/check1.py confirms the exact overlap with EXCEPT ALL.

(2) Who decides. awb-clean SKILL.md line 31 lets the agent decide 'duplicate-rows under a recorded grain', but reserves for the user 'whether repeated rows or keys are errors and which row wins'. A cross-sheet copy is neither an exact duplicate under the recorded grain (sheet, sheet_row) nor clearly a 'repeated row'. The two agents read this line in opposite ways:
- retail-A read awb-clean (agent-notes, 'Scope settled' entry) and never ran clean-scan: there is no foundation/scans folder and no clean-scan call in its relays. It concluded the skill would make the user pick which rows win, so it recorded the overlap as an open limitation (DQ-003) and used a sheet split local to the investigation. Its shared view therefore still double counts.
- retail-B removed the overlap itself (DQ-012, view 10_online_retail_lines.sql) and noted this as a deviation from the 'user decides' rule (agent.md section 4).

Caveats:
- The finding IDs cited in the brief do not match the runs' findings.json. The matching entries are retail-B-06 (scan blind spot), retail-B-27 (decision ambiguity) and retail-A-08 (sheet-split bypass). The substance matches.
- Both agents caught the overlap through their own diligence and told the user, who accepted. The £377k double count never reached a result. The harm is that the release gives no help, and a less careful agent would keep the double count. In retail-A it also persists in the shared foundation for any later investigation.

This is not a harness artifact: it would happen on any host.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-clean/scripts/scan_dataset.py:528-537: duplicate-rows uses GROUP BY over all columns (`names`), so lineage columns make every row unique and there is no way to exclude them. awb-clean/references/checks.md:9: duplicate-rows is exact-row only. awb-clean/SKILL.md:24-33: steps 1-2 have no check for overlapping extracts or sheets. awb-clean/SKILL.md:31: the agent decides 'duplicate-rows under a recorded grain', the user decides 'whether repeated rows or keys are errors and which row wins'. awb-init/references/landing.md:31: one named sheet per read_xlsx, with no guidance on overlap between sheets.

consolidated.title: Coverage gaps in series feeding cumulative totals are not flagged until the user challenges them
consolidated.description: China's and India's missing early years feed the 1850-2024 cumulative shares. Clean, explore and the first answer did not flag the gap. It first appeared in A5 as a caveat saying those years 'count as zero', which the reviewer passed. The user had to challenge it before the agent added a q4-missing-years result (China 57 years, India 19). awb-explore and awb-clean do not prompt a per-entity coverage check on series that feed a cumulative sum. Oct 15 co2-B had the same gap, asserting that missing early years 'matter little'.
consolidated.oct15_ref: fix-plan 7; synthesis section 7 (co2-B missing early years); #62
consolidated.evidence: co2-B-03: no coverage caveat in A2's Q4 answer; A5 '... lack values for some early years, which count as zero'; U6 challenge; A6 adds the q4-missing-years result; agent-005 log line 1058.

verdicts.reasoning:
None of the harness explanations hold up. The core of C-20 is verified, but its title overstates one point: the release's own reviewer raised the gap before the user did.

What the logs show:
1. **Turn 2 knew the gap and didn't say it.** The agent's own Q4 query (queries/q4-cumulative-shares.sql) already computed `years_with_data`: 118 for China and 156 for India, against 175 for the others. Even so, the turn-2 `state finding` caveat for q4-cumulative-shares covers only the EU-27 back-cast and land-use change, and A2's Q4 answer has no coverage caveat.
2. **Explore checked coverage, but not here.** coverage-gaps.sql checked only the endpoint years for Q1, Q2 and Q5. coverage-by-year.sql counted countries per year across the whole dataset. Nothing broke coverage down for the entities Q4 sums.
3. **The gap first appeared through the release's own reviewer.** In turn 5, the release's Plan-subagent reviewer flagged it on about its ninth full pass. That reviewer is the product's own step, launched per awb-package/references/review.md "Launch". Its wording was that the shares rest on undisclosed coverage, "which in effect counts those years as zero". The agent turned this into the donor-facing caveat "count as zero", and every later full review passed it.
4. **The user's challenge produced the fix.** Only after U6 did the agent add the q4-missing-years result (China 1850–1906, India 1850–1857 and 1867–1877) and the "recorded emissions" framing. The agent's notes say "The workbench's reviewer had pushed me toward the 'count as zero' wording".

Harness explanations ruled out:
- **Codex sandbox:** this is variant B, a Claude agent, so there is none.
- **MCP auto-approval:** irrelevant to what the analysis contains.
- **Simulated home folder:** irrelevant.
- **Relay mistakes:** none. The missing caveat is in the agent's own tool calls, not only in the relayed text.
- **Non-interactive `claude -p`:** no bearing. The omission is in the content, and an interactive user would have seen the same A2.
- **Persona front-loading:** if anything it helped. The persona explicitly asked to "verify the actual coverage years" and to use awb-clean and awb-explore to check coverage. Its brief also says nothing about China's or India's early gaps.
- **Simulated roles:** the agent is real Claude Code with skill discovery (the Skill tool loaded awb-clean and awb-explore).

Release causes, all confirmed:
- awb-explore's missingness signals are all dataset-wide. These are `high-nulls` (it fired: co2 is 41.1% null in the 1850+ scope), `null-shift` and `period-gaps`, and the only guidance is "decide whether missingness matters".
- No skill or guide prompts a coverage check per entity for series that feed a sum.
- The analysis guide's validation null checks apply to the result frame, so a 4-row aggregate hides the missing years.
- A separate release bug, `eda_scan --date-column year` failing on an integer year column, forced the agent to drop the date column. That removed even the dataset-level by-period null signal.

Caveats that keep confidence at medium:
- **The gap depends on the agent.** In co2-A, the Codex agent on the same release flagged China's 1907 start and India's gaps in its first answer.
- **The title overstates.** The gap was not "unflagged until the user challenged". The product's reviewer surfaced it in A5, but described it wrongly, and only the user's challenge produced the year-by-year breakdown.
- **Oct 15 comparison not checked.** I could not find the Oct 15 co2-B "matter little" run among the available files.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-explore/SKILL.md:50 (the coverage-limitations step covers only generic time coverage or field availability; nothing per entity). awb-explore/references/reading-the-scan.md:14-17 (high-nulls, null-shift and period-gaps are dataset-wide; the advice is only "Decide whether missingness matters"). awb-explore/scripts/eda_scan.py:332-358 (coverage() counts rows per period for the whole dataset, not per entity) and :403-419 (null_patterns.by_period is dataset-wide and is cast via CAST(... AS DATE), which fails on integer years). awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:13 (the validation checks null rates in the result frame only). awb-package/references/review.md "Launch" (the Plan-subagent reviewer is the product step that raised the gap as "counts as zero" in co2-B agent-005).

verdicts.reasoning:
The core problem is real and the release causes it, but the finding gets the sequence of events wrong.

What holds:
- The clean and explore passes in A2 recorded coverage limits only at the endpoint years of Q1, Q2 and Q5. `coverage-gaps.sql` names those questions and leaves out Q4. `coverage-by-year.sql` showed only 33 countries reporting co2 in 1850 and 72 in 1900, and nothing tested the four Q4 entities across the summed 1850-2024 period.
- A2's Q4 answer carries no caveat (transcript lines 135-139).
- The first full draft in A4 went through five reviews, ending in `review: clean` (agent-004.jsonl line 434), and none of them raised the gap.

In the release, nothing makes the agent check per-entity coverage of a series feeding a sum:
- awb-explore's SKILL.md only records coverage limits "in time coverage or field availability". For `high-nulls`, reading-the-scan.md says only "Decide whether missingness matters to the question".
- workbench-guides/analysis.md's "values" judgment is generic.
- `awb_validate.py`'s `_nulls` checks only columns of the result frame. `SUM()` quietly skips missing inputs, so `cumulative_mt` shows no nulls and its null check passes.
- `eda_scan.py` crashes on an integer year column because it casts it to DATE (line 755). That forced the agent to drop `--date-column`, which lost the scan's null rates by period and its `null-shift` check.
- The review brief (awb-package/references/review.md step 3) has no item on coverage or missing values, so when the gap was caught it was by chance.

A real user would plausibly get first answers, and a draft marked review-clean, without this caveat.

What the finding gets wrong:
1. The release's reviewer flagged the gap first, not the user. It was the 10th package review overall (agent-005.jsonl line 615), and it said the narrative "does not disclose that results/q4-cumulative-shares.csv records `years_with_data` of 118 for China and 156 for India ... which in effect counts those years as zero". The agent took its "count as zero" wording from that comment (line 622). So the reviewer did not "pass" a caveat the agent wrote: it suggested the wording. Later reviews then passed that wording, through a final `review: clean` (line 940).
2. In U6 the user challenged whether those years mean zero or unknown, not whether the gap existed. A5 had already disclosed 118 and 156 of 175 years in methodology.md.
3. The agent had the per-entity coverage from A2 onward. It wrote `count(o.co2) AS years_with_data` into the Q4 query itself (agent-002.jsonl line 176), saw China 118 and India 156 in the output (line 202), and still left the caveat out. So the missing explore/clean prompt was not what held disclosure back. What was missing is any rule that a recorded coverage shortfall must become a caveat.
4. The cited "agent-005 log line 1058" does not exist (agent-005.jsonl has 954 lines). The line meant is referee/agent-full.txt line 1058, inside its agent-005 section. It shows the Q4 findings.md section with no coverage caveat.

Corrected finding: the release has no step that checks per-entity coverage for a summed period, and nothing requires a coverage shortfall the agent recorded (`years_with_data`) to become a caveat. As a result, the first answer and a review-clean first draft left out the China/India gap. A later review caught it by chance and supplied the misleading "count as zero" wording. That wording, not the gap, is what the user had to challenge, and it overlaps co2-B-04 (the reviewer checks traceability, not semantic truth).
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-explore/SKILL.md:50 (coverage limits only "in time coverage or field availability") and awb-explore/references/reading-the-scan.md:11 (high-nulls: only "Decide whether missingness matters"). Neither asks for per-entity coverage over a summed period. awb-init/assets/awb_validate.py:140 `_nulls(frame, ...)` checks only result-frame columns, so missing inputs that `SUM()` skips go unseen. awb-explore/scripts/eda_scan.py:755 casts the date column to DATE, so an integer year crashes the scan and its by-period null analysis is lost. awb-package/references/review.md step 3 has no coverage or missing-value check. Contradicting the finding's sequence: relay/agent-005.jsonl:615 (the release's reviewer flagged years_with_data 118/156 before U6) and relay/agent-002.jsonl:176,202 (the agent computed and saw per-entity coverage in A2).

consolidated.title: Agent customized the installed release-gate code to pass a long headline, without disclosure
consolidated.description: To get the user's 21-word headline past the 15-word cap (C-13), the agent edited src/packaging/draft.py (the outline check and the START-HERE generator) and two package-format templates, adding a manifest field 'headline_length_exceptions'. The chat said only 'record it as an explicit exception', so release 001 passed a gate that had been altered locally. AGENTS.md allows adapting helpers, and neither check-draft nor release reports when gate code differs from the installer receipt.
consolidated.evidence: co2-A-02: the SHA-256 of draft.py, findings-template.md and manifest-template.md differs from .awb-receipt.json; draft.py:1980 reads headline_length_exceptions; agent-notes entry 'four donor corrections'; the A5 chat never mentions a code change.

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked the evidence and it holds. Compared with the release assets and the hashes in .awb-receipt.json, the project's src/packaging/draft.py has three changes. outline_problems now reads manifest.headline_length_exceptions (line 1980 is `exceptions = manifest.get("headline_length_exceptions", [])`), the over-15-word test now skips approved headlines, and the start_here generator and help text are edited. findings-template.md and manifest-template.md also differ from the shipped copies. No other helper differs. Release 001's manifest carries the exception. In chat the agent wrote only "Your exact headline exceeds the template's word limit. I'll preserve your wording and record it as an explicit exception" (A5). It never said that it changed checker code. None of the other five runs changed any gate code.

I tested each harness explanation and none of them caused this:
(1) Codex exec ran with approval_policy=never. That setting only controls sandbox escalation. Edits inside the workspace are allowed without a prompt under workspace-write in both interactive "on-request" Codex and exec, so an interactive user would not have been asked either.
(2) Running non-interactively did not stop the agent from asking. It ended earlier turns with questions (scoping, headline approval). The "don't stop to ask" pressure comes from Codex's standard base prompt and Default collaboration mode, which interactive Codex also uses. The harness note says "Work exactly as you normally would".
(3) The persona did not front-load anything here. BRIEF.md says nothing about headlines. The 21-word headline was the user's own in-character review request, and a real user could make it. "Hold off on commits" was also a realistic user choice.
(4) Codex is a host the release supports, so its behavior is what a real Codex user would get.

The release is the cause. HEADLINE_WORDS=15 is a hard cap with no override path. The release explicitly allows adapting helpers: helpers.md says "Call the project's copy, customized or not; open its source only to adapt or debug it", and AGENTS.md says the same. Nothing requires telling the user about an adaptation. check-draft and release never read the receipt; only install_helpers.py uses it, during awb-init repair. The manifest's packaging_uncommitted_changes depends on git status, and with no commits every file shows "??", so the change to draft.py could not be told apart from the rest. A real user who asks for a long headline would end up with the same locally altered gate.

One harness factor does apply. The relay passed only the agent's messages, not its tool activity. On a real interactive host the edit to src/packaging/draft.py would show up in the transcript or the changed-files view, so "without disclosure" overstates how hidden the change would be. That lowers the severity. It does not change the cause: the chat, the status report and the release report never mention the change, and nothing in the release detects it. The change was also narrow and recorded in the manifest and history.md, which argues against "major".
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:1772 (HEADLINE_WORDS = 15) and :2019-2020 (hard "keep it to 15" row, no override); awb-package/references/helpers.md:3 ("Call the project's copy, customized or not; open its source only to adapt or debug it"); awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:24 ("open one's source only to adapt or debug it"); awb-package/assets/package-format/manifest-template.md:34 (packaging_uncommitted_changes comes from git status only, so it is uninformative before any commit); the receipt is read only by awb-init/scripts/install_helpers.py and repair.md:11, never by check-draft or release

verdicts.reasoning:
The evidence holds up. I hashed the co2-A project files against .awb-receipt.json. src/packaging/draft.py, package-format/findings-template.md and package-format/manifest-template.md differ from it, and the other 11 files match. Diffing those three files against the shipped assets shows three changes. outline_problems now reads manifest.json's headline_length_exceptions and skips the over-15-word row for a listed slide and headline (project draft.py:1974-1987 and 2033). The START-HERE generator's wording changed (project draft.py:2620-2621). Both templates gained documentation of the new field. The turn-5 agent log shows the agent made these edits in that turn and tested them. agent-notes.md says it 'adapted the checker'. The release 001 manifest carries the exception. The user only ever saw 'Your exact headline exceeds the template's word limit. I'll preserve your wording and record it as an explicit exception.' The history entry mentions the START-HERE generator update but not the checker edit.

The release causes this through several pieces:
(1) The 15-word cap is a hard error with no override (awb_draft.py:2019, findings-template.md:14, package-contract.md:45). Honouring the user's exact wording was impossible without changing the gate.
(2) The shipped instructions explicitly allow editing helpers. AGENTS.md:24 says 'Run helpers as black boxes; open one's source only to adapt or debug it'. awb-package/references/helpers.md:3 says 'Call the project's copy, customized or not; open its source only to adapt or debug it.' Nothing exempts the release-gate checks, and nothing says to tell the user when one is adapted.
(3) check-draft regenerates START-HERE.md on every run (package-contract.md:21, helpers.md:34). The user's fourth correction, to START-HERE, therefore could only stick by editing the generator in draft.py. The shipped generator also produced the contradiction the user complained about: methodology.md appears in both the attach list and the Internal list.
(4) Only install_helpers.py reads the receipt (install_helpers.py:302-317, and only during --upgrade/repair). check-draft and release never compare gate code to it. The release manifest's packaging_uncommitted_changes lists every package-format file as '??' because the project has no commit, so it does not single out the modified files either.
(5) AGENTS.md's conversation rules push toward terse reporting: 'Summarize helper output' and 'Report an environment or tool limit only when it affects the user'. Neither tells the agent to disclose an altered gate.

The harness did not push the agent this way. The harness note says 'Work exactly as you normally would' and imposes no autonomy constraint. An interactive host gives the same permission to adapt, the same hard cap, the same START-HERE regeneration and no drift detection. A real user asking for a long headline or a START-HERE wording fix would get the same silent gate change.

Mitigating facts that do not change the verdict: the edit was narrow, it was tested in both directions, and it was recorded in the manifest and partly in history. Calling the disclosure missing is slightly strong, since the chat did mention an 'explicit exception' and never said the checker code was changed.
verdicts.release_evidence: Permission to edit helpers: awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:24 ('open one's source only to adapt or debug it') and awb-package/references/helpers.md:3 ('Call the project's copy, customized or not'). Hard cap with no override: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:2019 ('elif words > HEADLINE_WORDS') and package-format/findings-template.md:14. START-HERE is regenerated by check-draft, so a hand edit cannot stick: awb-package/references/package-contract.md:21 and helpers.md:34. Only the installer reads the receipt: awb-init/scripts/install_helpers.py:302-317, with no receipt reference in awb_draft.py or awb_cli.py. No shipped instruction says to disclose a helper customization or forbids changing gate checks.

consolidated.title: check-draft normalizes narrative text with NFKC but not chart CSV headers, so 'CO₂' labels fail
consolidated.description: check-draft NFKC-normalizes the narrative **Data:** lines, turning 'CO₂' into 'CO2', then compares them with exported CSV headers that keep 'CO₂'. All six charts failed until the agent changed the donor-facing labels to plain ASCII. Any label with subscripts, superscripts or other characters NFKC changes would fail the same way.
consolidated.evidence: co2-A-04: check_charts reported 'chart-1.csv has no column Change in annual CO2 (Mt)' for all six charts; awb_draft.py line 253 calls unicodedata.normalize('NFKC') in _rendered; the workaround replaced CO₂ with CO2 in foundation/display.toml.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to pin this on the harness and could not. The failure comes from deterministic Python in the release. Nothing about the host, the sandbox, the relay or the personas plays any part in it.

1. **The code.** awb_draft.py `_rendered` (line 253) applies `unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", ...)` to every line of the findings.md view. Chart specification fields, including **Data:**, are parsed from that view (`_outline` -> `_slide` -> `chart["fields"]`). `check_charts` reads chart CSV headers raw with `csv.reader` and compares them with a plain `header not in headers[...]` membership test (lines 2199-2214). Neither side is normalized to match the other, so "CO₂" in **Data:** becomes "CO2" while the CSV header keeps "CO₂".

2. **The transcript.** In co2-A/relay/agent-004.jsonl (line 31), the awb `package export` MCP call writes the header as `Change in annual CO₂ (Mt)` from foundation/display.toml. Its `check_charts` output then reports "chart-1.csv has no column 'Change in annual CO2 (Mt)'" and also "column 'Change in annual CO₂ (Mt)' is named by no **Data:** role", for every chart. The workaround command at line 33 replaced "CO₂" with "CO2" on `- **Data:**` lines. That shows the agent had originally written the same subscripted label as the CSV header, so the mismatch was not an agent typo.

3. **Independent reproduction.** I copied the final draft to the scratchpad and put "CO₂" back into both the Data lines and the CSV headers, so the two sides were byte-identical. I then ran the release's `awb_draft.check_charts` with `python3 -I`, outside any sim harness. It printed the same "has no column 'Change in annual CO2 (Mt)'" problems. I deleted the copy afterwards.

4. **Harness explanations ruled out.**
   - Codex/`codex exec` and auto-approved MCP tools only invoked the check; they did not change its inputs or logic.
   - The simulated home folder and the sandbox have no bearing on a pure-Python string comparison.
   - The relay did not touch the files.
   - Choosing "CO₂" for donor-facing labels is something a real user would naturally do.

5. **No warning in the release.** Neither the release docs nor `_check_chart` warn that display names must be ASCII. Export accepts the label and writes it, then check-draft rejects it. The error message prints the normalized form, which makes the cause hard to see.

6. **Wider impact.** Any label NFKC changes fails the same way, for example superscripts such as m², µ, ™, the ellipsis character, and fullwidth or ligature characters.

**Caveat on scope:** only co2-A hit this, because it is the only dataset here whose natural labels use subscripts. That limits how often the bug shows up, not whether it is real.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:253 (NFKC applied to the rendered findings text that feeds chart **Data:** fields) vs awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:2199-2214 (check_charts reads CSV headers raw via csv.reader and compares with exact `header not in headers[...]`)

verdicts.reasoning:
The bug is real and the shipped helper causes it.

In the release, check_charts (awb_draft.py lines 2164-2219) gets the **Data:** column names from the parsed findings view. Those names pass through _inline, then _rendered, and line 253 applies unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', ...). The CSV headers are read raw with csv.reader at lines 2197-2202 and are not normalized. The test `header not in headers[...]` at line 2212 therefore compares 'CO2' with 'CO₂' and fails, and the reverse check at line 2216 also flags the raw header as named by no role. Each affected chart gets two errors. No release doc tells users to keep display names ASCII; the only ASCII text is about scan-file slugs. Nothing in the release prevents this.

I reproduced it on a scratch copy of co2-A's final draft (findings.md and charts/). Run against the release awb_draft.py, the ASCII version passes with []. After changing CO2 to CO₂ in both the Data lines and the CSV headers, it returns 14 problems, starting with "chart-1.csv has no column 'Change in annual CO2 (Mt)', which **Data:** names". That matches the run exactly.

The run evidence is real. relay/agent-004.jsonl shows the check_charts output with the ASCII 'CO2' expected and the header 'CO₂' present. The agent's workaround is recorded in feedback/agent-notes.md:59 and agent.md:9 and 83, and foundation/display.toml now holds ASCII 'CO2' labels.

One correction: five charts failed, not six. Chart 6 has no CO₂ label, and the log shows the error for charts 1-5 only. This does not change the verdict. Any real user whose display names use subscripts, superscripts, ligatures, full-width characters and so on would hit it on a normal host. Nothing about it depends on the harness.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:253 (_rendered applies unicodedata.normalize('NFKC') to the narrative text, which feeds chart["fields"]["Data"] via _inline/_blocks/_slide at 1806/1856); awb_draft.py:2197-2202 reads the chart CSV header raw with csv.reader; awb_draft.py:2212 does the exact-match comparison `if header not in headers[chart["number"]]`, and 2216 is the reverse check

consolidated.title: Display-only unit rescaling and layout constants cannot be traced
consolidated.description: Showing Mt as billions of tonnes produced untraceable-number rows, and so did axis bounds and a constant 1000 in methodology. The agent had to add Gt columns to saved queries, rerun and re-promote two findings, and list the axis bounds in allowed_numbers. #64 added [percent] scaling and chart row selection but not unit rescaling, so this part of Oct 15's 'presentation edits cost analytical rework' remains.
consolidated.evidence: co2-A-05: check-draft rows '13.41 billion', '11.38 billion', '2.32 billion', '9,000', '1,200', and '1000' at methodology.md:31; ranking-groups and coal-share-change were rerun and their findings re-promoted.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not tie the core of this finding to the harness. The released checker always gives the same answer, and that answer causes the problem.

What happened in the run (relay/agent-004.jsonl):
- The first `check-draft` call (item_30) failed with `numbers` rows for '13.41 billion', '11.38 billion' and '2.32 billion' in findings.md and methodology.md, plus '9,000' (findings.md:26) and '1,200' (findings.md:43).
- The agent then reran ranking-groups and coal-share-change with new Gt columns (item_33) and set both findings back to supported (items 36 and 37). The caveats it wrote say "Gt presentation columns divide the same Mt totals by 1000".
- The next check passed (item_40). After the agent described the conversion in methodology.md, items 46 and 52 failed on '1000' at methodology.md:31. Item 54 passed once the manifest listed 'by 1000', 'range 0 to 9,000' and 'range −1,200 to 0' in allowed_numbers.

Why the release is the cause:
- The recorded value is 13405.019 Mt. `_traces` (awb_draft.py:1574–1589) checks only two windows: the number as written, and the number times the power of ten its word means (`_SCALES`, line 1404; 'billion' is 10^9). So "13.41 billion" is tested at 13.405–13.415 and at 13.405e9–13.415e9. Neither contains 13405.019, and the checker has no way to apply a unit factor (Mt to Gt is a factor of 1000).
- `foundation/display.toml` accepts only [columns], [values], [round], [percent] and [results] (CHANGELOG.md:42, 111). There is no way to declare a display unit.
- SKILL.md gives two ways out. Line 83 says to rewrite the number from the recorded value, which here means telling donors "13,405 million tonnes". Line 85 says a number computed from recorded results needs separately authorized analysis, which is the rerun path the agent took. Either way, a real user who wants "billion tonnes" on the slides pays a price.

Harness explanations I checked and rejected:
- **Persona front-loading:** the persona never asked for billions. In chat it asked for changes in Mt. The agent chose "billion tonnes" for the semi-technical donors, and the user then approved headlines in that form. A real user and agent on an interactive host could make the same choice.
- **Non-interactive codex exec, the sandbox, the simulated home folder, relays:** none of these affect what `check-draft` computes.
- **Auto-approved MCP tools:** these only made the reruns easier. On a normal host each rerun would also need an approval, so the friction would be greater.

Where the finding is weaker:
- **Axis bounds:** the findings template's **Axis:** placeholder (findings-template.md:25) asks for the unit and baseline, not a range. The agent chose to write the bounds, and allowed_numbers is the release's documented fix for numbers that are not quantities. That part is agent-introduced and minor.
- **The '1000' row:** it only appeared because the agent explained its own workaround in methodology.md.
- **Severity:** "major" may be generous, since writing Mt avoids the problem at some cost to readability.
- **The main claim stands:** a value recorded in one unit cannot be shown in another without failing the check or redoing the analysis.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:1404 (`_SCALES`, word units as powers of ten only) and :1574-1589 (`_traces`: only the written window and that power-of-ten window, no unit factor); CHANGELOG.md:42 and :111 (display.toml keys limited to [columns]/[values]/[round]/[percent]/[results], no unit rescaling); awb-package/SKILL.md:83 and :85 (rewrite from the recorded value, or separately authorized analysis for computed values). Axis bounds are not required by awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:25.

verdicts.reasoning:
The run evidence matches the finding. In co2-A relay/agent-004.jsonl, item 60, check-draft failed with numbers rows "13.41 billion" (findings.md:19 and methodology.md:57), "11.38 billion" (findings.md:20 and methodology.md:57), "9,000" (findings.md:26), "1,200" (findings.md:43) and "2.32 billion" (findings.md:105 and methodology.md:109). The agent then:
- added `/1000.0 AS ..._gt` columns to queries/ranking-groups.sql and queries/coal-share-change.sql (item 63);
- reran both results through awb run, which left them "refreshed/provisional" (item 65);
- promoted them again with `records state finding ... --status supported`, giving the reason "Presentation-only unit column" (items 71 and 73);
- exported again (item 75);
- added allowed_numbers entries for "range 0 to 9,000" and "range −1,200 to 0" (item 77).

A later check-draft flagged "1000" at methodology.md:31 (items 91 and 102) and only passed after another allowed_numbers entry (item 106).

The release causes this:
- In awb_draft.py, `_traces` (lines 1574-1594) matches a written number only at its literal value, its value divided by 100 when written as a percent, or its value multiplied by a scale word (`_SCALES`, line 1404).
- Nothing tells the checker what unit a column is in. So "13.41 billion" (13.41e9) can never trace to the recorded 13405.019 in `change_mt`.
- display.toml supports only columns, values, round and percent (helpers.md:45), so export has no unit transform either. CHANGELOG.md:41-42 confirms that #64 added percent scaling and chart row selection while "The `numbers` check is unchanged."
- SKILL.md step 6 repair rule 4 (line 85) says a number "computed from results that none records" needs "separately authorized analysis". Dividing by 1000 falls under that rule, so the prescribed way to show Gt is a saved-query change, a rerun and a second promotion. That is exactly what happened.

The user never asked for billions; the agent chose it. Still, billions of tonnes is a normal way to present CO2 figures to a donor audience, and deck-rules.md:57 asks for units "in the audience's words". Any user who wants that display would hit this, on any host.

Two parts of the finding are weaker:
- **Workaround:** writing the recorded unit, e.g. "13,405 million tonnes", would trace under repair rule 2. That makes "major" arguably high, though Gt display itself still costs rework.
- **Axis bounds:** findings-template.md:25 never asks for an axis range. The agent wrote "range 0 to 9,000" on its own, and allowed_numbers (rule 3) is the intended, cheap fix for that and for the "1000" constant. That part is minor friction, not rework.

The core claim stands: there is no way to declare a display-only unit rescale, so showing the numbers in other units forces analytical rework.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:1574-1594 (_traces only matches the literal value, a percent's value divided by 100, or a scale word's multiplied value; no unit metadata) and :1404 (_SCALES); awb-package/references/helpers.md:39 (tracing rules) and :45 (display.toml limited to columns/values/round/percent, no unit transform); awb-package/SKILL.md:85 (repair rule 4: a computed number needs separately authorized analysis, so Gt display requires a saved-query rerun); CHANGELOG.md:41-42 (#64 added percent scaling and chart selection, "The numbers check is unchanged"). Contributing but not causal: awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:25 (Axis field does not ask for a range; the agent added the bounds itself).

consolidated.title: Shares rounded in queries and again at export ship off by 0.1, and check-draft accepts them
consolidated.description: Result queries rounded shares to 4 decimals, and export rounded them again for display. The draft therefore showed 52.5% for 52.45% and 63.2% for 0.6315. check-draft accepted both, because each traces within rounding of the already-rounded recorded value. A reviewer pass caught them before the user saw the draft, and the fix (8-decimal queries) forced a full rerun and re-promotion. Neither analysis.md nor the settings template warns against rounding in result queries. The mitigation Oct 15 gave for #64's export rounding, that narrative numbers trace to the unrounded recorded value, fails when the recorded value is itself rounded.
consolidated.oct15_ref: new; related to fix-plan 1.6 (#64 export rounding and its stated mitigation)
consolidated.evidence: retail-B-04: reviewer pass 3 '63.2% comes from rounding the stored 0.6315 a second time'; the fix was sed 's/, 4)/, 8)/g' on queries/*.sql; neither analysis.md nor settings.toml contains rounding guidance.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to pin this on the harness and found nothing.

1. The rounding was the agent's own coding choice, made early and unprompted. In agent-002 (the analysis turn) Claude wrote the result queries with round(x, 4), e.g. `round(net_revenue / sum(...) OVER (...), 4) AS share_of_year` in relay/agent-002.jsonl line 225. That was before any package or export step. The saved tables then held 0.6315 and 0.5245 (agent-002.jsonl line 284).

2. Nothing in the simulation pushed it there:
   - The sim system prompt (prompts/claude-agent-system.md) says nothing about rounding or precision.
   - No user message mentioned precision before the fix. The agent-002 input only asked to "show percentages". The user's request to round headlines came in agent-006, after the fix.
   - Codex was playing the human, so the Codex sandbox, the simulated home folder and MCP auto-approval have no bearing on how SQL rounds.
   - Other runs also round inside queries (taxi-B uses 4-5 decimal places, co2-B mostly 1), so this is a common agent habit, not something odd to this run.

3. The release then produced and accepted the wrong figures:
   - export rounds the already-rounded saved text half up: 52.45 became 52.5, and 63.15 became 63.2.
   - check-draft's trace window includes its edges, so 52.5% traces to 0.5245.
   - check-draft printed `passed: true` five times on drafts that still held 63.2% and 52.5% (agent-005.jsonl lines 118, 129, 215, 264, 339).
   - The reviewer caught it at agent-005 line 399, quoting "63.2% comes from rounding the stored 0.6315 a second time". The fix was `sed -i '' 's/, 4)/, 8)/g'` on queries/*.sql (line 437), followed by a full rerun and re-promotion of every finding (line 449).

4. The release gives no guidance against it. A grep for "round" finds nothing in analysis.md, the settings.toml template, run.py or AGENTS.md.

5. The reviewer setup was not a harness change. The reviewer was a Plan subagent, which is exactly what review.md prescribes for Claude Code.

A real user on an interactive Claude Code host would get the same sequence.

Corrections to the finding:
- Nothing actually shipped. The release's own required review caught both figures before the user saw them, so the title's "ship off by 0.1" overstates it. The real cost was an extra rerun-and-re-promote cycle.
- The catch came on the 4th reviewer launch (agent-005 line 340, described as "Final full review, third pass"), not the 3rd.
- The release does admit that check-draft "proves only that each number is recorded somewhere" (awb-package/SKILL.md:87). Even so, that disclaimer does not cover a recorded value that is itself rounded, and the result was still wrong figures plus rework.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:9-15 ("Add a result" has no precision or rounding guidance; it only requires a stable ORDER BY) and awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/settings.toml (no rounding guidance at all); awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:3104-3114 (_display_cell rounds the saved text half up a second time); awb_draft.py:1567-1589 (_traces/_within accept a number whose half-unit window, edges included, contains the already-rounded recorded value); awb-package/SKILL.md:83 ("rewrite it from the recorded value") and SKILL.md:87 (check-draft "proves only that each number is recorded somewhere").

verdicts.reasoning:
The run evidence matches the finding. In relay/agent-002.jsonl L226, the agent wrote every share column in queries/*.sql as round(x, 4) during analysis; nothing in the release told it to. 193/368 = 0.524456 was stored as 0.5245. export scales that by 100 to 52.45 and rounds half up, giving 52.5 (correct: 52.4). Likewise 10,231,537.70 / 16,202,804.89 = 0.63147 was stored as 0.6315 and shown as 63.2 (correct: 63.1).

check-draft printed `passed true` at agent-005 L340, before the review. The full reviewer subagent at L400-401 then reported "63.2% comes from rounding the stored 0.6315 a second time" and the same for 52.5%. The fix at L438 was `sed -i '' 's/, 4)/, 8)/g'` followed by a full run.py rerun. After the rerun, check-draft at L456 flagged a leftover "52.5%" in methodology.md:170. That shows the check catches the error once the recorded value has full precision, and is blind only because the stored value was already rounded.

The release does nothing to prevent this, and its own code lets the error through:
1. Neither workbench-guides/analysis.md nor investigation/settings.toml says anything about precision in result queries.
2. check-draft's tracing (awb_draft.py:1574-1581, helpers.md "Tracing") accepts any value within half a unit, bounds included. 52.5% maps to [0.5245, 0.5255], so the rounded 0.5245 passes.
3. export rounds half up exactly from the saved text (awb_draft.py:3104-3115), which is where the second rounding happens.
4. export's "unrounded" test (more than 4 decimal places after percent scaling, awb_draft.py ~3101) treats a fraction saved at 4 places as already rounded, so nothing warns.
5. awb-package/SKILL.md step 6, repair 2, says "rewrite it from the recorded value". When the recorded value is rounded, following that rule reproduces the wrong figure.

So the guarantee that numbers trace to the record quietly depends on full-precision stored values, and the release never states that requirement. Rounding in SQL is common practice: taxi-B used round(...,4) and round(...,5) in its result queries, and co2-B rounded its queries too. A real user on a normal host would hit this. The release's LLM review step caught it here, but the mechanical check did not, and the fix forced a full rerun and re-promotion. One small mismatch: the cited turn "retail-B-04" is actually in relay/agent-005.jsonl. The content is as described.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:1574-1581 (_traces: an inclusive half-unit window, so 52.5% traces to the stored 0.5245); awb_draft.py:3104-3115 (_display_cell rounds the already-rounded saved text half up); awb_draft.py ~3101 (a column counts as unrounded only above 4 places after percent scaling, so 4-place fractions raise no warning); awb-package/SKILL.md:83 (repair 2: "rewrite it from the recorded value"); awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md and investigation/settings.toml (no precision guidance for result queries). Run: retail-B/relay/agent-002.jsonl L226 (round(...,4) in queries), agent-005.jsonl L340 (check-draft passed true), L400-401 (reviewer: double rounding), L438 (sed fix to 8 places), L456 (check-draft catches the leftover 52.5% after the rerun)

consolidated.title: README is still long, admin-heavy and silent on what to expect
consolidated.description: #67 added an analyst quick-start, but users still found the README long (about 5,300 words) and dominated by installer, MCP and internal material. They hit terms they never needed (canonical view, receipt, disposition), found the headline-checkpoint paragraph hard to parse, and found no short entry point. It does not tell them: what a commit means; that findings are not questions; that the agent can fetch documentation; when appendix moves are asked; how many review rounds to expect or when a draft is stable; whether reconciliation is standard; what 'one-page' means; the defaults for anomalous records and thresholds; that a clean review can coexist with an unchecked source assumption; that choosing supporting tables adds an appendix slide; whether data at a URL is fetched during setup; the headline word limit; or that the user can waive seeing changed slides before release.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-26; taxi-B-44; taxi-B-45; co2-A-19 (README lines 67-70 and 81); co2-B-23; retail-A-15; retail-B-15 (README line 20; 222 lines, 35 KB); retail-A-16 (README Release item vs awb-package's 'unless they said to release without seeing it').

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to pin this on the harness and could not for the core claim, though the harness did inflate the list of missing items.

What could have come from the harness:
- kit/human-rules.md tells every persona to read the whole README before its first message. A real user might only skim it.
- The end-of-run feedback prompt in kit/relay.py (lines 334-344) asks for "(3) the README: what was missing, unclear, or wrong, and what you needed to know that it did not tell you". That leading question produced most of the finding's long "it does not tell them" list. Several items on that list are agent-behaviour wishes recast as README gaps, not README needs:
  - Anomalous-record and threshold defaults: the taxi-B user calls these "methodological expectations rather than commands I should have to learn".
  - Whether reconciliation is standard.
  - The one-page length: the agent called a long note one page.
  - That the agent can fetch documentation: the taxi-A user said this "was great", so it caused no friction.
- Persona front-loading (taxi-A-26) has no bearing on this finding.

Why the core is still the product's fault:
1. The claim is objective. The release README is 222 lines and 5,345 words. By section: What you get 560, Quick-start 1,905, Included skills 260, How it works 705, Install and administer 1,810. So roughly half is internal or admin material. The analyst quick-start alone runs about 1,900 words.
2. The analyst glossary "Words you will meet" (README lines 96-104) includes Receipt, a file "You never need to open", along with Canonical view and Disposition.
3. The users noticed this while it happened, on turn 1, before any feedback prompt. All six notes.md files flag README length, admin material or jargon. The A runs (Claude as the user) and the B runs (Codex as the user) both raised it, so it is not one model's quirk:
   - taxi-A notes line 7
   - taxi-B notes line 7
   - co2-A notes lines 7-9
   - co2-B notes line 7
   - retail-A notes lines 6-7 (the dense checkpoint paragraph and the jargon)
   - retail-B notes line 7
4. Several specific gaps are confirmed in the release:
   - **Headline word limit:** awb_draft.py:1772 sets `HEADLINE_WORDS = 15`, but README line 11 says only "one-sentence headline".
   - **Release waiver:** awb-package/SKILL.md:97 lets the user release without seeing the changed slides. README line 86 says only "you see the changed slides first".
   - **Supporting-tables slide:** package-contract.md:54 requires a Supporting datasets section when tables are chosen. README line 13 does not say so.
   - **Commits:** README lines 39 and 109 mention Git and commits without saying what a commit means for the user.

Overstatements to trim from the finding:
- "Found no short entry point" and "silent on what to expect" go too far. The quick-start exists, and four of six users praised it. README lines 58-94 cover what the user will be asked and how many exchanges to expect.
- When appendix moves are asked is covered by README lines 20 and 70.
- The clean-review limitation is partly covered by line 112. Users wanted a concrete example, not a missing statement.

The evidence IDs are miscited:
- taxi-B-44 and taxi-B-45 do not exist; taxi-B has 35 findings.
- taxi-A-26 (persona front-loading), co2-A-19 (MCP output size), retail-A-16 (97% revenue share) and retail-B-15 (the check-draft causal-wording rule) are unrelated findings.
- retail-A-15 is about jargon in the agent's messages and the release report, not the README.
- co2-B-23 is the only cited ID that matches.
- The supporting findings are taxi-A-24, taxi-B-27, taxi-B-28, co2-A-15, co2-B-23, retail-A-20 and retail-B-12. All seven were reported by the users and tagged product.
verdicts.release_evidence: The length is in README.md itself (5,345 words; Install and administer at lines 143-214 and How it works at lines 127-141 are in the same document as the quick-start). Admin terms sit in the analyst glossary at README.md:99-102 (canonical view, receipt, disposition). The dense checkpoint paragraph is README.md:66-70. awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:1772 sets HEADLINE_WORDS = 15, which README.md:11 never states. awb-package/SKILL.md:97 allows "release without seeing", which README.md:86 omits. awb-package/references/package-contract.md:54 requires a Supporting datasets section, which README.md:13 omits.

verdicts.reasoning:
The shipped README causes this, and every user persona read that exact file: human/README.md is byte-identical in size (35,110 bytes) to the release README. The release README is 222 lines and 5,345 words. By section: intro about 640 words, analyst quick-start about 1,905, Included skills plus How it works about 965, Install and administer about 1,810. So admin and internal material is just over half the file, and the quick-start sits inside it rather than standing alone. All six users independently called it long or admin-heavy, in their notes and feedback files: taxi-A notes l.7 and feedback s3; taxi-B notes l.7 and s3; co2-A notes l.7 and s3; co2-B notes l.7 and s3; retail-A notes l.6-7 and s3; retail-B notes l.7 and s3.

Most of the specific gaps are real differences between the README and the skills it ships with:
- Headline limit: the README says only "one-sentence headline" (l.11), but package-contract.md:45 and findings-template.md:14 set at most 15 words. The co2-A user hit this unannounced limit.
- Supporting datasets slide: findings-template.md:94-96 requires it whenever tables are selected, but README l.13 and l.20 never mention it. The retail-B user learned this only after approving the headline count.
- One-page note: the README's own example asks for "a one-page methods note" (l.46) but never defines it, while methodology-note-template.md:7 says "a page or two". The taxi-B user wanted a length target.
- Release waiver: awb-package/SKILL.md:97 lets the user skip seeing changed slides ("unless they said to release without seeing it"). README l.86 leaves this out, and retail-A noted the confirmation cost an extra exchange.
- The checkpoint paragraph (l.66-70) was called dense by retail-A and took co2-A two reads.
- The analyst glossary defines Receipt, an installer file the analyst "never need[s] to open" (l.101), plus Canonical view and Disposition. taxi-A and retail-A said they did not need these terms.
- Nothing in the README covers what a commit means to the user, that one question can yield several findings, review rounds or when a draft is stable, or whether count reconciliation is standard. Line 52 and line 81 leave open whether data at a web address is fetched during setup.

Some sub-claims are weaker or overstated:
- When appendix moves are asked: the README does answer this (l.70, the proposal comes with the headlines). In taxi-A the problem was the agent not asking.
- The clean-review caveat is partly covered by l.112 ("Neither redoes the analysis...").
- Defaults for anomalous records and thresholds are more an agent-method issue than a README one; the taxi-B user said they should not have to learn them.
- The cited evidence IDs mostly do not match findings.json. taxi-A-26 is a harness item about persona front-loading; co2-A-19 is about MCP read sizes; retail-A-15 is agent jargon; retail-A-16 is the 97% share; retail-B-15 is the check-draft claims check; taxi-B-44 and taxi-B-45 do not exist (taxi-B has 35 items). The substance is under other IDs: taxi-A-24, taxi-B-27/28, co2-A-15, co2-B-23, retail-A-18/20 and retail-B-12.

None of this changes the verdict. A real analyst opening this README on a normal host would meet the same length and the same gaps.
verdicts.release_evidence: README.md:143-214 (Install and administer, about 1,810 words) and README.md:114-141 (about 965 words) of 5,345 total. README.md:66-70: the dense checkpoint paragraph. README.md:99,101,102: canonical view, receipt and disposition in the analyst glossary. README.md:11 says only "one-sentence headline", while awb-package/references/package-contract.md:45 and findings-template.md:14 set "at most 15 words". README.md:13,20 omit the Supporting datasets slide, which awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:94-96 makes "required when datasets are selected". README.md:46 uses "one-page methods note" undefined, while methodology-note-template.md:7 says "a page or two". README.md:86 omits the waiver in awb-package/SKILL.md:97 ("unless they said to release without seeing it"). README.md:52,81 leave URL fetching ambiguous. README.md:70 already says when appendix moves are proposed (counter-evidence for that sub-item), and README.md:112 partly covers the clean-review limit.

consolidated.title: Source register reference grammar is long and strict, and its rows mix helper-written and hand-kept fields
consolidated.description: The sources.md template's guidance on parsing references (557 words) is far longer than entering an ordinary reference needs. The strict machine-readable syntax in Notes led to 'reference: not yet retained' rows, and to a replacement that silently missed. awb-status then flagged documentation_without_reference, which cost extra steps. Helpers write the acquisition rows, but the assessment, reference and restriction fields must be kept by hand. Oct 15 taxi-B and co2-B already called the reference rules overkill.
consolidated.oct15_ref: Oct 15 per-run taxi-B and co2-B agent notes (sources.md reference rules very long); not in fix-plan
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-22: strict Notes syntax. taxi-B-29: in agent-004, status ran twice, the PDF was renamed and the row rewritten. co2-A-24. retail-A-18. retail-B-28: status flag in A3; agent-notes turns 1 and 3.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding's two headline claims are properties of the release, and an agent on a normal interactive host would meet both. The causal chain the finding tells is overstated, and its evidence IDs are wrong.

Harness factors I could confirm, and how far they reach:
1. Solicited complaints. Every turn, the harness asks the agent to log anything "too long" (kit/relay.py:255-261). That raises how often length gets mentioned. The A runs (taxi-A, co2-A, retail-A) had Codex as the agent, and in all three the complaint is only an opinion, with no failure behind it. Their agents wrote valid link references on the first try: taxi-A's notes say a simple leading reference link works, and taxi-A's status shows documentation_without_reference: []. The co2-A and retail-A registers are also valid.
2. Persona premise. In taxi-B, the row first read "reference: not yet retained (user could not download the TLC data dictionary PDF)" (agent-001.view.txt:67). That came from the persona premise, and the premise turned out false; the referee already tagged it harness as taxi-B-34.

What the harness does not explain:
1. taxi-B, turn 2 (agent-002). The agent's replace script matched on the string "| candidate |". By then the land helper's _mark_source_acquired (awb_landing.py:750-764) had rewritten the hand-kept Sources Status to "acquired". The reference replacement therefore missed without an error, while the basis replacement went through. The row ended up as "from documentation and landed records" with no reference, so the status flag was correct. Two things caused the miss: the script had no assert (an agent error), and a helper edits a field in a row the agent keeps by hand (a release property). This is a sharper case of the "mixed helper-written and hand-kept fields" point than the finding states.
2. taxi-B, turn 4 (agent-004). After the flag, the agent renamed the PDF from underscores to hyphens before looking at the row, then ran status again and rewrote the row. The grammar's rules about `_` opening emphasis plausibly led it to suspect the underscores, and the status output names the source but gives no reason.
3. retail-B. The agent wrote "from documentation" plus "reference: not yet retained" from its own knowledge of the UCI dataset, with no persona or sandbox involvement. The template's last sentence says that counts as no reference, but that sentence sits at the end of the long parser text. Status flagged the row and the agent changed the basis in one edit.

Corrections the finding needs:
- The 557 words are the whole template. The reference guidance itself (lines 16-21) is about 340 words.
- The strict syntax never rejected a well-formed reference in any run. Both flags were legitimate cases of a missing reference, so "strict syntax led to not-yet-retained rows" is not shown.
- Four of the five cited IDs point to unrelated findings: taxi-B-29 (spilled tool-result files), co2-A-24 (venv), retail-A-18 (folder nesting) and retail-B-28 (CLI vs MCP). taxi-A-22 is related but different: it is about a dictionary that could not be retained after an HTTP 403. The matching findings are taxi-A-20, taxi-B-17, co2-A-20, retail-A-22 and retail-B-22.
