Minor severity is right.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/foundation/sources.md:16-21 (about 340 words of reference-parser rules; line 21 says 'reference: not yet retained' counts as no reference, at the end of the block); sources.md:27 (land/retain write the Acquisitions rows, the user fills Restrictions by hand); awb-init/assets/awb_landing.py:750-764 (_mark_source_acquired rewrites the Sources Status from candidate to acquired, which made taxi-B's hand replace miss); awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py:263-268 and 405-406 (flags a 'from documentation' basis without a reference and lists only the source ID, with no reason).

verdicts.reasoning:
The headline claim holds and the release causes it. The finding's chain of consequences is mostly misattributed, so the finding should be cut down to the length and opacity claim.

Supported:
- The reference rules in awb-init/assets/workbench/foundation/sources.md (lines 16-21, about 340 words) spell out parser internals in dense prose: where reading stops at raw HTML, how emphasis flanking works with `*`, `_` and `~`, and how autolinks are handled. None of that is needed to write `reference: [codebook](references/x/codebook.pdf)`. The 557-word figure counts the whole file, not just the reference rules.
- Four of the five agents independently called the rules too long: taxi-A agent.md rank 13, taxi-B agent.md item 8, retail-A agent.md item 8, retail-B agent.md.
- One concrete wasted step comes from the text being hard to follow. In taxi-B agent-004, status still listed the source. The agent guessed that underscores in the PDF name were the cause, then renamed the file and ran sed over sources.md and catalog.md. I ran the shipped `referenced()` from collect_status.py against both rows: the original underscore path already passes (True), so the rename was unnecessary, as the agent suspected.
- Helpers write the Acquisitions rows while Restrictions, assessment and references are kept by hand. That split is by design (template line 27; data.md says "Fill each new row's Restrictions yourself"), and co2-A raised it. No failure followed from it, though; it is upkeep.

Not supported or misattributed:
1. The strict syntax did not cause the 'reference: not yet retained' rows.
   - In taxi-B, the persona said the PDF could not be downloaded. In retail-B, the agent had kept no documentation and labelled an assessment made from its own knowledge as 'from documentation'.
   - The phrase itself is copied from the template, which states plainly at line 21 that such an entry "counts as no reference".
2. The replacement that silently missed was the agent's own error. In agent-002, its str.replace matched on '| candidate |'. But `land` had already returned `"source_status": "acquired"`, behaviour its help text documents. The agent itself wrote "my script lacked an assert".
3. The documentation_without_reference flag worked as designed and caught real record errors in both runs:
   - taxi-B: the failed replace, after the basis had been changed to 'from documentation and landed records'. The agent wrote "Status report was valuable here".
   - retail-B: an incorrect 'from documentation' basis, fixed with one sed.
4. The cited evidence IDs point to unrelated findings. taxi-A-22 is about a dictionary that could not be retained. taxi-B-29 is a harness finding about spilled tool-result files. co2-A-24 is about the venv interpreter, retail-A-18 about release folder nesting, and retail-B-28 about the CLI being used instead of MCP. The correct IDs are taxi-A-20, taxi-B-17, co2-A-20, retail-A-22 and retail-B-22.
5. I did not verify the Oct 15 claim.

Net: a real user's agent would read the same over-long grammar on any host, so the length and opacity are a product issue (minor). The status-flag and silent-miss costs are not defects caused by the release.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/foundation/sources.md:16-21 (reference grammar; line 21 sets out parser stop rules and says 'reference: not yet retained' counts as no reference); sources.md:27 and workbench-guides/data.md (Restrictions/assessment filled by hand); awb-init/assets/awb_landing.py:750-765 (land sets candidate->acquired, which broke taxi-B's unasserted replace); awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py:262-406 (the flag works as designed; underscore destination passes)

consolidated.title: Export sits awkwardly in awb-package's step order: it needs the draft folder and chart specs that come later
consolidated.description: Before the draft folder exists, export refuses with 'no draft at ...; create it with awb-package', even when run from within awb-package. Yet the skill wants display names set before writing, and export is what prints the display stubs and methodology_lines. Run before the chart specifications exist, export writes chart files and then exits 1 ('no specification in findings'). There is no metadata-only or dry-run export. Read-only check-draft after edits exits 1 only because the recorded inventory is stale, so preflights during a revision look like failures. All three Oct 15 B runs reported the 'no draft at' refusal, and it was not addressed. retail-A-30 was tagged unclear (the agent's own ordering); the step-order conflict itself is product.
consolidated.oct15_ref: Oct 15 per-run taxi-B, co2-B and retail-B agent.md ('no draft at ... create it with awb-package'); not in fix-plan
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-28: awb_draft.py lines 2645 and 3283. co2-B-18. retail-B-18: export error text. taxi-A-17: export and check-draft failures in agent-006 and agent-007; package-contract 'rewritten unless --verify-only'. retail-A-30: export failed for all five charts.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none. Every failure came from the agent's own choice of command order. That choice was driven by how the release lays out the steps, not by claude -p or codex exec, the sandbox, the simulated home, the relay, or the personas.

Transcripts:
- **taxi-B, retail-B, co2-B (Claude agents).** Each ran `awb.py export` before writing any draft file. Traces: taxi-B relay/agent-005 tool 15, retail-B agent-005 tool 5, co2-B agent-004 tool 5. Each got `no draft at deliveries/.../draft; create it with awb-package`. Each then guessed the fix (mkdir draft/assembly, copy deck-rules.md and m365.md) and reran.
- **retail-B explains why** (feedback/agent.md section 2). Step 3 (write) needs export's methodology_lines and display names, but export refuses until the folder exists.
- **taxi-A and retail-A (Codex agents).** Both exported before the chart specifications were written, to get methodology_lines. Export wrote six (taxi-A) and five (retail-A) chart files, then exited 1 with "chart file has no specification in findings". Both agents call the order their own mistake. retail-A says a dry-run export "would avoid the temptation".

So 5 of 6 runs, on two model families and three datasets, ran export before writing. That consistency points to the instructions, not to harness noise.

Release causes:
- **Display names.** Step 3 says to set display names "before writing", but only export's display_stub tells you which columns are missing them.
- **Methodology lines.** Step 4 has methodology_lines pasted into methodology.md, which was already written in step 3.
- **Refusal message.** When export runs early, the refusal says to "create it with awb-package", which is the skill the agent is already running. Neither the SKILL nor the contract says to create the folder. The contract says export creates the manifest, and taxi-B read that as creating the draft too.
- **No preview mode.** There is no metadata-only or dry-run export.
- **Visible failures on a real host.** The MCP layer sets isError on any nonzero exit (awb_mcp.py lines 440 and 469). A real user would see these as failed tool calls, not just the sim's telemetry.

Weaknesses in the finding as written:
1. **Wrong direction.** The draft folder and chart specs do not "come later". The SKILL puts them in step 3, before export in step 4. The real tension runs the other way: step 3 wants outputs that only export (step 4) produces.
2. **Stale-inventory point is weak.** That `check-draft` failure (taxi-A agent-006 and agent-007) is documented behaviour. The read tool's check-draft is fixed to `--verify-only`, labelled "verify a release candidate", and the error message names the fix. Using it as a mid-revision preflight was the agent's own choice, though a host where only read-only tools skip approval would push real users the same way.
3. **Wrong IDs.** Most cited finding IDs do not match the findings.json files. The matching entries are taxi-B-16, co2-B-18, retail-B-13, taxi-A-16 and retail-A-27, and retail-A-27 is tagged unclear. The "Oct 15 B runs" claim could not be checked against these folders.

Impact is minor: every agent recovered within one or two steps.
verdicts.release_evidence: release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:3282-3284 (export refuses when draft/ is missing and tells the user to create it with awb-package); awb_draft.py:3425-3426 and 3525 (export runs check_charts after writing and exits 1 when it is non-empty); awb_draft.py:2645 (the same refusal in check_draft); awb-package/SKILL.md section 3, the "Before writing, give each column ... a display name" bullet, against section 4, where export prints display_stub and the methodology_lines to paste into methodology.md; references/package-contract.md:70 (export creates the manifest, with no mention of the draft folder); awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py:12-13 and 359 (the read tool's check-draft is fixed to --verify-only) and 469 (isError on nonzero exit)

verdicts.reasoning:
The main complaint holds. The release causes it, though part of the finding overstates it.

What the release does:
(1) export() refuses when the draft folder is missing. Its message is "no draft at <path>; create it with awb-package" (awb_draft.py:3282-3284). The agent is already inside awb-package when it sees this. No instruction anywhere says to create the folder before exporting.
(2) In SKILL.md, step 3 (line 58) says "Before writing, give each column ... a display name". But the tool that reports missing names (display_stub) is export, which is step 4. Step 4 (line 68) also tells the agent to paste export's methodology_lines and questions into methodology.md, which step 3 already told it to write. The contract (package-contract.md:21) says export runs "before the narratives ... are final". The skill never says that step 3 is a first pass.

The behaviour was consistent across runs. All three B runs set up display.toml, then ran export before writing findings.md, and got the "no draft at" refusal:
- taxi-B relay agent-005, tool call 15
- co2-B relay agent-004, tool call 5
- retail-B relay agent-005, tool call 5
Each agent recovered by running mkdir. retail-B's agent stated the conflict directly: methodology.md needs export's methodology_lines and display names. taxi-A and retail-A also exported before their chart specifications were complete. Five of six runs exported early, all on the same model and with no harness involvement. That suggests the skill's wording invites it, and a real user's agent would likely do the same. The harm is small: one wasted call and a misleading message.

Parts of the finding that do not hold:
(a) "Chart specs that come later" misreads the skill. Its Sequence puts Write (step 3, with every Chart N specification) before Export (step 4). An agent following it exactly has the folder and the specifications in place before it exports.
(b) Exit 1 when specifications are missing is documented: export's help text says it exits 0 only when files were written and check_charts is empty. retail-A's agent called the ordering its own mistake.
(c) The read-only check-draft that failed on a stale inventory is the MCP read tool's variant. awb_mcp.py:125 describes it as "verify a release candidate, writing nothing", and SKILL.md step 6 says to run the writing check-draft. Using it as a mid-revision preflight was the agent's misuse; taxi-A's agent itself called those failures expected.
(d) "No dry-run export" is a feature request. If the draft folder exists but findings.md does not, export writes its files and exits 0, so creating the folder first already works as a preview.

The cited IDs are also off. The matching findings are taxi-B-16, retail-B-13, taxi-A-16 and retail-A-27; taxi-B-28, retail-B-18, taxi-A-17 and retail-A-30 are unrelated findings. Only co2-B-18 matches. The evidence itself is real.

Verdict: product (minor). The causes are the circular refusal message and the step-3/step-4 dependency in the text. The check-draft and dry-run parts are not product issues.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:3282-3284 (export refuses with "no draft at ...; create it with awb-package"); awb-package/SKILL.md:58 ("Before writing, give each column ... a display name") versus SKILL.md:68 (export's display_stub, plus "Paste its methodology_lines into methodology.md"); awb-package/references/package-contract.md:21 (export runs before the narratives are final). Contradicting the sub-claims: SKILL.md:14-15 (Write comes before Export); awb_draft.py:3479 ("Exit 0 only when written and check_charts is empty"); awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py:125 (read-tool check-draft is "verify a release candidate, writing nothing").

consolidated.title: Agents' own tool and shell slips
consolidated.description: These are generic agent errors that neither the release nor the harness caused: apply_patch mismatches and double operations; shadowing a functions.exec helper; backticks breaking a JavaScript template string; a guessed file name; a Unicode mismatch in a patch; zsh not word-splitting a command variable; 'echo =====' read as a =command expansion, repeatedly in reviewer subagents; a blocked 'cat > /dev/null' killed with pkill -f '^cat$'; a regex edit that garbled a methodology sentence; pip installing to the user site through a resolved venv symlink; and string slicing at the first literal '[parameters]', which also appears in the settings.toml template's header comment (Oct 15 taxi-B made the same slip). All were recovered, mostly without user impact.
consolidated.oct15_ref: new (retail-B-39 repeats Oct 15 taxi-B's settings.toml slicing error)
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-38: apply_patch failures in agent-003 and agent-006 .err. co2-A-34. co2-B-40: exit 127; pkill; '0.13 Mt).15 Mt tolerance'. retail-A-31. retail-A-32: 'SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier state'. retail-B-39: prepared-statement error at agent-002 call 37; settings.toml template lines 1 and 4. retail-B-45: repeated 'Exit code 1' on 'echo ======'.

verdicts.reasoning:
Every slip listed did happen, and none was caused by the release, so this does not count against the product. I checked each one against the logs or the agents' own friction notes.

- **taxi-A:** the Codex apply_patch errors appear in relay/agent-003.err (the expected text did not match the file) and agent-006.err (two operations targeted findings.md). Shadowing text() in functions.exec ("TypeError: text is not a function") is in the agent's notes, written in agent-003.
- **co2-A:** agent-notes lines 26 and 58 record a Delete plus Add on one settings.toml and a mismatched patch. Line 78 records the guessed file name src/packaging/outline.py, line 79 the NFKC mismatch, and line 82 the backtick SyntaxError.
- **retail-A:** agent-notes line 15 records the venv symlink resolved to base python3, so pip installed into the user site. Line 51 records "SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'state'".
- **co2-B:** in agent-002, zsh did not split $R and the command exited 127. In agent-004, the stray `cat > /dev/null` was followed by `pkill -f "^cat$"`. In agent-007, the garbled "0.13 Mt).15 Mt tolerance" was repaired.
- **retail-B:** in agent-002, the agent sliced settings.toml at the first "[parameters]" and DuckDB then reported missing prepared-statement parameters. In agent-005, 006 and 007, reviewer subagents repeatedly hit "(eval):1: ===== not found" with exit 1. I reproduced that zsh =word behaviour locally.

None of these comes from the skills, helpers or MCP server.
- apply_patch and functions.exec are Codex host tools.
- Word splitting and =expansion are zsh behaviour, the same as on a normal macOS host.
- The stray cat, the regex garble, the guessed path and the symlink resolution are the model's own mistakes.

Some slips are tied directly to how the simulation was run:
- Both backtick SyntaxErrors (co2-A, retail-A) happened while the agent was writing the friction log the harness asked for (feedback/agent-notes.md).
- The pip user-site fallback happened because base site-packages was not writable under the sandbox and the simulated home. A normal Homebrew Python would refuse the install under PEP 668 instead.

Since nothing points to the release and part of it is harness-shaped, the lens's default of harness applies. It is not a strict harness artifact: most of these are model slips that could happen on any host.

One exception touches the release. The investigation settings.toml template uses the literal "[parameters]" in its header comments (lines 1 and 4) before the real table (line 6). That made the retail-B agent's string slicing fragile, and the finding says Oct 15 taxi-B made the same slip. The agent still owns the slicing, and the run already tracks this separately as retail-B-20 (tagged unclear). It is not a reason to call C-28 a product finding.

Caveats:
- The evidence IDs the finding cites don't match the findings files. taxi-A-38, co2-A-34, co2-B-40 and retail-B-45 are beyond the highest IDs in those findings.json files. retail-A-31 and retail-A-32 there are about reviewer logging and the persona front-loading answers. Only the underlying evidence in the logs and notes supports the claims.
- The functions.exec errors are known only from the agents' own notes. The failed JS never reached a tool call, so it left nothing in the Codex JSON logs.
verdicts.release_evidence: release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/settings.toml:1 and :4 put the literal "[parameters]" in comments before the real table at :6. That is the only release involvement, a minor one, in the retail-B slicing slip, which is already tracked as retail-B-20. Nothing in the release causes the other slips.

verdicts.reasoning:
The slips all happened, but the release does not cause any of them, so the finding is not a product defect.

Each slip I checked against the raw evidence:
- **taxi-A:** relay/agent-003.err logs an apply_patch "Failed to find expected lines" error on documentation-notes.md. relay/agent-006.err logs an apply_patch "multiple operations target ...findings.md" error. "text is not a function" appears in relay/agent-003.jsonl and agent-009.jsonl, from the agent shadowing the functions.exec text() helper.
- **co2-A:** feedback/agent.md:67-95 records three slips:
  - a delete-plus-add apply_patch on settings.toml;
  - an rg on src/packaging/outline.py, a guessed file name (the function lives in draft.py);
  - a first fix that compared raw Unicode against NFKC-normalised text, plus the JS template-string "Unexpected identifier 'assert'".
- **co2-B:**
  - relay/agent-002.jsonl line 97: "Exit code 127 ... no such file or directory: .venv/bin/python src/awb.py sql". The command was stored in R="..." and called as $R, which zsh does not word-split.
  - relay/agent-004.jsonl line 40: the agent itself wrote a stray `cat > /dev/null;`. Line 53 kills it with `pkill -f "^cat$"`.
  - relay/agent-007.jsonl line 179: methodology.md:26 reads "(largest gap, rounded, 0.13 Mt).15 Mt tolerance." The reviewer subagent caught it and line 231 fixed it before delivery.
- **retail-A:** relay/agent-001.jsonl has `Path(".venv/bin/python3").resolve()` followed by "Defaulting to user installation". The agent uninstalled and reinstalled into the venv. relay/agent-003.jsonl and agent-008.jsonl have "SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'state'" from backticks in a JS template string.
- **retail-B:**
  - relay/agent-002.jsonl, tool call 38 by my count (the finding says 37): `i=t.index("[parameters]"); head=t[:i]`. This puts the agent's new `[parameters]` header on the end of the template's first comment line, which comments out the table. DuckDB then reports "Values were not provided for the following prepared statement parameters: end, meaningful_sales, start".
  - In relay/agent-005/006/007.jsonl, reviewer subagents ran `echo ======` 12 times. Every run failed with "(eval):1: ===== not found", Exit code 1. This is zsh's `=cmd` expansion, and I reproduced it locally.

Release side: no shipped file tells agents to use `echo =====`, `cat > /dev/null`, pkill, apply_patch, `Path.resolve()` on the venv interpreter, a command stored in a shell variable, or string slicing of settings.toml. A grep of the release for these patterns found nothing.

The only release-adjacent item is the settings.toml template. Its header comment names the `[parameters]` table in prose on lines 1 and 4. awb-scope/SKILL.md:55 only says to copy run.py with its settings.toml and populate them. Either of these would have worked on the same template:
- editing the file normally;
- a line-anchored match on "\n[parameters]";
- a TOML parser.

Naming a table in a config comment is ordinary. The cause is the agent's substring slice, and the same slip in an earlier run (Oct 15 taxi-B) does not change that. Rewording the comment would be cheap optional hardening, not a fix.

None of this is caused by the harness either. All the slips are generic agent errors, recovered within the same turn. The one with a visible effect, the garbled methodology sentence, was caught by review before delivery.

The cited ids taxi-A-38, co2-B-40 and retail-B-45 are not in those runs' findings.json files. retail-A-31 and -32 are in its findings.json but describe other issues: reviewer logging and persona front-loading. I found the evidence directly in the relay logs and feedback notes instead.

Verdict: the slips are real, but the claim that the release causes them is unsupported. They belong in an agent-error bucket, not in release fixes.
verdicts.release_evidence: No release file instructs or causes the slips. release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/settings.toml:1 and :4 mention "[parameters]" in prose comments; this is only an incidental trap for the agent's substring slice in retail-B relay/agent-002.jsonl call 38 (`t.index("[parameters]")`). awb-scope/SKILL.md:55 says only to copy and populate settings.toml. Nothing in the release prescribes echo =====, cat > /dev/null, pkill, apply_patch, venv symlink resolution, or a command stored in a variable.

consolidated.title: Commit suggestions break the once-per-session rule: repeated, unclear, or missing
consolidated.description: The README and AGENTS.md promise at most one commit suggestion per session (#62 change 9), but the awb-status 'Commit the current work' row and the awb-package and awb-release provenance reports raise it again. co2-B mentioned commits in five replies and explicitly invited one in two of them; retail-B suggested a commit three times. co2-A's single suggestion ('The setup is ready for an initial commit') did not read as a request. retail-A never suggested one, so its release shipped without a packaging commit, and the user saw that only as a jargon provenance line (see C-56).
consolidated.evidence: co2-B-10: README.md:109; A2 'I'd suggest committing now'; A4 'Say commit the current work'. retail-B-10: A2, A3 and A5. co2-A-18: A1. retail-A-34: A4 'work remains uncommitted'; A7 'No packaging Git commit exists'.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none for the main claim, which is that commit reminders repeat.

Harness causes I ruled out:
- **Session continuity and memory.** relay.py resumes the same Claude session on every turn (`--resume` with a session id fixed at the start; relay.py:137-143), and none of the agent logs in co2-B or retail-B shows a context compaction. Each agent therefore had its earlier replies in view, so the repeats are not memory loss.
- **The agent system prompt.** It says nothing about commits.
- **The personas.** The user never asked for commit reminders. In retail-B the user gave commit permission only in message 6, after the repeats.
- **The required status call.** The harness requires at least one awb-status call (kit/human-rules.md:31). That makes the problem more likely to show up, but the README itself suggests that request, and these runs had about 8 to 9 user messages each. A real user working in one sitting would hit the same path.

The repeats come from release text that has no once-per-session guard:
- **retail-B A3.** The "You can ask for: 'Commit the current work'" line comes word for word from the awb-status/SKILL.md:65 row, which fires whenever `git.uncommitted_paths` is above zero. retail-B A2 had already offered a commit ("I can commit it whenever you'd like").
- **co2-B A4 and retail-B A5.** These came from the awb-package report rule (SKILL.md:91), which says to report an unrecorded packaging commit as a provenance gap. Its only exemption is a project without Git. The co2-B agent read `producing_commit` from the manifest in order to report it (relay/agent-004.jsonl). It then added the invitation "Say 'commit the current work'", borrowing the awb-status request phrase. That came after its own A2 line, "I'd suggest committing now".
- **co2-B A8.** awb-release/SKILL.md:55 applies the same gap rule, which produced the provenance line in this reply.

The release is inconsistent on this point. workbench-guides/data.md:11 and analysis.md:17 both carry the guard "unless you already suggested a commit this session". awb-status, awb-package and awb-release do not. Yet README.md:109 tells the user the agent "reminds you at most once a session", and AGENTS.md:48 says the same.

Weak parts of the finding:
- **co2-A.** The wording "The setup is ready for an initial commit" is Codex's own; the release does not prescribe it. The user still understood it well enough to answer "Hold off on commits for now".
- **retail-A.** Making no suggestion at all does not break an "at most once" rule. That run's jargon provenance line is C-56's issue.

The main claim, repeated reminders that contradict the README promise and come from release text, would reach a real user on a normal interactive host.
verdicts.release_evidence:
Paths are relative to the release folder.
- Promise, with no exceptions: README.md:109 and awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:48.
- Sources of the repeats, none with a once-per-session guard:
  - awb-status/SKILL.md:65: the "Commit the current work" row fires whenever `git.uncommitted_paths` is above zero.
  - awb-package/SKILL.md:91 and awb-release/SKILL.md:55: report an unrecorded packaging commit as a provenance gap, exempting only projects without Git.
- The guard exists elsewhere, which shows the inconsistency: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/data.md:11 and analysis.md:17 ("unless you already suggested a commit this session").

verdicts.reasoning:
The main claim holds and the release causes it: a user can get the commit reminder more than once in a session. The finding overreaches on co2-A and retail-A, and those parts should be cut.

The promise: README.md:109 ("reminds you at most once a session") and the shipped AGENTS.md:48 ("suggest one at most once a session while analytical code is uncommitted"). Several guides enforce this with an explicit guard, "unless you already suggested a commit this session": workbench-guides/data.md:11, data.md:33 and analysis.md:17. Three other places in the release have no such guard.

1. awb-status/SKILL.md:65. Its "You can ask for" table adds "Commit the current work" to every status report while git.uncommitted_paths > 0, and nothing checks whether a commit was already suggested. Separately, SKILL.md:26 has every status report include git.commit_comparison ("no commits yet; all work uncommitted").
2. awb-package/SKILL.md:91 and awb-release/SKILL.md:55. Both say to report every provenance gap. The only exception is an unrecorded packaging commit "in a project without Git". In a Git repository that has no commit yet, awb_draft.py:2895-2897 records packaging_commit as {"unknown": "the checkout has no commit yet"}, and provenance_gaps() (awb_draft.py:3955) reports it. So every package and release report raises the missing commit again.

The run evidence holds up. co2-B and retail-B each ran as one continuous session (the same session_id in every agent-NNN.jsonl), so "once per session" applies across the whole run.

- **co2-B:** commits come up in A1, A2, A3, A4 and A8.
  - A2 is the one allowed suggestion: "I'd suggest committing now ... Tell me if you want that."
  - A4 is the package report. It turns the provenance gap into a second invitation, "Say 'commit the current work'", reusing the request wording from the awb-status table.
  - A8 is the release report repeating the gap.
  - The simulated user complained (feedback/human.md:19, 31).
- **retail-B:** suggestions in A2, A3 and A5.
  - A2: "I can commit it whenever you'd like".
  - A3: the status table's "Commit the current work". The agent's own notes say "suggested a commit once (last turn), not repeating" (agent-notes.md:40), yet the status table still produced the line. This is the clearest case of the release causing a repeat against what the agent intended.
  - A5: the package provenance gap, "A commit before release would make the release traceable".
  - The user called the repeats a distraction (human.md:60).

The co2-A and retail-A parts do not show a release defect.

- **co2-A:** its A1 line "The setup is ready for an initial commit" was a single suggestion, which the rule allows. Nothing in awb-init tells the agent to say this or how to word it, so the unclear wording comes from the agent (Codex).
- **retail-A:**
  - Making no suggestion at all fits "at most once".
  - Its A4 status reply left out the "You can ask for" list that would have offered a commit. That is the agent departing from awb-status, not the release.
  - Releasing with no commit is how the on-request mode is designed to work.
  - The confusing A7 line ("No packaging Git commit exists") comes from the awb-release provenance-gap requirement, and finding C-56 already covers it.

Fix the release in three places:
- give the awb-status row the same "unless already suggested this session" guard the guides use;
- in package and release reports, stop treating a missing first commit in a Git project as a gap that needs restating, or tie that report to the single reminder;
- drop the co2-A and retail-A sub-claims from the finding.
verdicts.release_evidence: Causes it: awb-status/SKILL.md:65 (a "Commit the current work" row whenever git.uncommitted_paths > 0, no once-per-session guard); awb-status/SKILL.md:26 (git.commit_comparison in every report); awb-package/SKILL.md:91 and awb-release/SKILL.md:55 (report every provenance gap; the only exception is a project without Git); awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:2895-2897 (packaging_commit unknown, "the checkout has no commit yet") and awb_draft.py:3955 provenance_gaps(). The rule they break: README.md:109 and awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:48. Guides that do carry the guard: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/data.md:11, data.md:33 and analysis.md:17.

consolidated.title: awb-status reports a cryptic 'state_status: indeterminate at date precision'
consolidated.description: When the latest state and commit share a date, or the project has no commits, the collector reports state freshness as 'indeterminate at date precision', even when evidence checks show every finding current. awb-status gives no plain translation, so agents dropped the line or puzzled over it. Oct 15 taxi-B reported the same line.
consolidated.oct15_ref: Oct 15 per-run taxi-B agent-notes ('indeterminate at date precision' unclear to report); not in fix-plan
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-22. taxi-B-43: status output in agent-004. co2-A-25: A5, all 11 findings current. co2-B-37: collect_status.py:884.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to pin this on the harness and couldn't. The trigger condition is in the release, it is the normal result for any project whose state record is kept up to date, and the skill gives no wording for it.

1. **The release produces it whenever two dates match.** `git_status()` compares two calendar dates. One is the state's `Last updated` date. The other is the newest of the uncommitted file modification dates and the latest investigation commit date. When the difference is 0 days it returns 'indeterminate at date precision'. The state helper writes `Last updated: {today}` on every state write (awb_provenance.py:1129), and agents write the state at the end of each task. So the newest change and the state almost always share a date. Running status on a later day without new work does not help, because both dates are still the earlier day. 'up to date' needs a state write on a strictly later day than every change, which is rare in normal use. A real user on an interactive host would see this value most of the time.

2. **The harness's compressed timeline doesn't explain it.** Every run happened on 2026-10-16, but per point 1 the same-day match is the normal case anyway. The simulated home folder and timezone don't matter either: both dates came out as 2026-10-16.

3. **The no-commit persona preference doesn't explain it.** taxi-A had commits and a clean tree (`has_commits:true`, `uncommitted_paths:0`, `latest_commit_date` 2026-10-16) and still got 'indeterminate at date precision'. taxi-B, co2-A and co2-B had no commits and got the same value, with `days_after_state:0` in each.

4. **The skill gives no plain-language translation.** awb-status/SKILL.md line 26 tells the agent to report `git.state_status` using the collector's values without its keys. It explains only `out of date`. Nothing in the release tells the agent what 'indeterminate at date precision' means or how to put it to a user.

5. **The agents' handling matches the finding.** co2-B's notes say the line is "unclear for user; omitted". taxi-B's notes call it "fine but cryptic". taxi-A's notes explain the date tie and say not to read the field as proof of order. retail-A and co2-A worked around it, retail-A by not calling the state current on the same calendar day. None of the user-facing replies I checked passed the line on. That shows agents dropping or working around it, not a relay or role mistake.

**One harness effect, which doesn't change the verdict:** the agents were told to log friction, so they wrote more about this than a real user's agent would. But the output and the missing guidance both come from the release.

**Minor gap:** the evidence IDs in the finding (taxi-A-22, taxi-B-43, co2-A-25, co2-B-37) don't appear in the runs' findings.json files, which use taxi-A-20 and co2-A-21, or in the grading folder. I checked the raw transcripts and notes directly instead, and they support the finding.
verdicts.release_evidence: The value comes from awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py:884, which sets `state_status` to "indeterminate at date precision" when `difference == 0`. The two dates it compares are `state_date`, the state's `Last updated` date read at collect_status.py:209-210, and the newest change date, built at collect_status.py:860-878 from uncommitted file modification dates and `git log -1 --format=%cs`. awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py:1129 writes `Last updated: {today}` on every state write. awb-status/SKILL.md:26 says to report `git.state_status` but explains only `out of date`, and nothing in the release explains the indeterminate value.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release is the cause. collect_status.py:884 sets state_status to "indeterminate at date precision" whenever the newest dated change has the same date as the state's last_updated. The newest dated change is either the mtime of an uncommitted investigation file or the latest investigation commit, which excludes state.md and the question ledger. awb-status/SKILL.md:26 tells the agent to report git.state_status, but it only says how to expand the `out of date` value. It never explains "indeterminate" in plain terms or says what to tell the user. The CHANGELOG (line 71) documents only `out of date` / `up to date`. No other file in the release mentions the value.

The run evidence holds up. I read the collector output directly in all four runs, and each shows days_after_state 0 with state_status "indeterminate at date precision":
- **taxi-A:** relay/agent-004 shows has_commits true, uncommitted_paths 0, and latest_change "latest investigation commit". So even a clean, fully committed tree gets the non-answer when the state was written and committed on the same day.
- **taxi-B, co2-A, co2-B:** has_commits false; the latest change is an investigation file's mtime from that day.

The agent notes match the finding:
- **taxi-A notes, line 61:** the agent reasoned it through and reported the date and the committed state instead of the value.
- **taxi-B notes, line 44:** "fine but cryptic"; its reply dropped the line.
- **co2-B notes, line 32:** "unclear for user; omitted".
- **co2-A notes, line 84, and agent.md item 12:** the agent found the value inconclusive, fell back on the evidence checks, and reported "All 11 findings are current" in A5.

So agents either dropped a line the skill tells them to report or had to work out what it meant themselves.

A real user would hit this. Status is often requested on a day the state was updated and work continued. Updating the state and committing the same day also triggers it, so it is not just an artifact of the sims running in one day. The one-day sims only made it happen every time.

Caveats:
- No user ever saw the cryptic string, because agents filtered it out. The real impact is a freshness signal that gets silently dropped, plus agent confusion, which fits "minor".
- The evidence IDs in the finding are mislabelled. taxi-A-22 is about the data dictionary, and co2-A-25 is about the sandbox. The matching records are taxi-A-20 and co2-A-21. taxi-B and co2-B have no findings.json entry; the issue appears only in their agent-notes.
- I could not check the "Oct 15 taxi-B" claim from these folders.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py:884 emits "indeterminate at date precision" when difference == 0; awb-status/SKILL.md:26 says to report git.state_status but only explains `out of date`, with no plain-language wording for indeterminate; CHANGELOG.md:71 lists only `out of date` / `up to date`.

consolidated.title: awb-status stays read-only even when the same message asks for edits
consolidated.description: Users combined a status request with edits: headline changes, a caveat edit, definitions. awb-status says 'Stay read-only' and gives no guidance for mixed requests, and the README says nothing about it. retail-A put the edits off for a whole turn, then told the user they were 'pending in the package files' when they existed only in chat. retail-B edited foundation/sources.md during the status turn anyway. taxi-A and co2-B flagged the tension. Oct 15 retail-A and taxi-B noted the same tension. retail-B-42 was tagged unclear because it happened once.
consolidated.oct15_ref: Oct 15 per-run retail-A and taxi-B agent notes ('awb-status says stay read-only'); not in fix-plan
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-23: transcript lines 165-167. retail-A-05: A4 'I'll record your headline changes' then 'pending in the package files'; U5. co2-B-22. retail-B-42: sed on sources.md after read status; A3 'I've changed it to say that'.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked hard for a harness cause and found only one harness factor: it inflated how often the problem showed up, but it did not cause the behaviour.

Harness factor that inflated frequency: the persona brief makes "ask where things stand at least once" an end-point criterion and suggests the README wording "Use awb-status — where are we?". In all six runs the simulated user tacked that line onto a message that also asked for work. Examples: co2-B U3 opens with it and then lists four analysis requests; retail-B U3 and taxi-A U4 add it after edit requests. That is box-ticking inside one continuous session, so mixed status-plus-edit requests come up far more often than they would for real users. The agents flagging the "tension" (taxi-A agent-notes line 59, co2-B agent-notes line 31) were writing in the friction log the harness asked them to keep.

The one run with a visible effect has nothing to do with harness mechanics. In retail-A turn 4 the Codex agent's log shows it read awb-status/SKILL.md, ran only MCP status and stale reads, and wrote nothing to the workbench. Its notes and reply say it held back the user's headline edits because of the skill's "Stay read-only" line. It was not blocked by:
- sandbox or approval limits (the same agent wrote files in other turns)
- non-interactive exec
- auto-approved MCP tools
- the simulated home
- a relay error (agent-004.jsonl matches the transcript)

A real user on an interactive Codex host who bundles an edit with "where are we?" can get the same deferral. The README's step 6 wording makes that bundling natural, and the README calls awb-status a "read-only report" without saying edits in the same message will wait.

Where the finding overstates:
1. The "whole turn" cost is doubtful. The retail-A user wrote "Before you write the full draft: use awb-status", so asking for the draft separately (U5) followed from their own ordering.
2. "Pending in the package files" is a model wording slip. The agent's own notes say "Do not misreport them as saved."
3. retail-B's sed on foundation/sources.md is not a user-requested edit. The agent fixed a flag the status report raised (documentation_without_reference), which breaks the skill's explicit "turn every fix into a next request". That is the model not following a clear rule, not missing guidance for mixed requests.
4. Five of six agents (taxi-A, taxi-B, co2-A, co2-B, retail-B) handled the mixed request without user-visible harm, either by doing the work and then reporting status, or the reverse.

Net: the release text (unscoped read-only, no guidance for mixed requests) caused the retail-A deferral and the ambiguity three agents reported. It is real but minor, and the harness inflated how often it appeared.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-status/SKILL.md:8 says "Stay *read-only*: report what the records say, and turn every fix into a next request." It is unscoped, with no guidance for a message that also asks for edits. README.md:84 suggests "Use awb-status — where are we?" and README.md:123 calls awb-status a "read-only report", with nothing on edits sent in the same message. Run evidence: retail-A relay/agent-004.jsonl (status and stale reads only, no workbench writes) and transcript line 302.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release causes this. awb-status/SKILL.md opens with one sentence that has no stated scope: "Stay *read-only*: report what the records say, and turn every fix into a next request." It does not say whether this covers the whole turn or only the status step, and it gives no guidance for a message that also asks for edits. The README calls status a "read-only report" (lines 84, 123) and is also silent on mixed requests. Yet it does explain the same-message case for awb-release (line 86, "If you ask for a change in the same message, you see the changed slides first"), so the gap is specific to status. The project AGENTS.md template (line 50) sends package corrections only through awb-package on the user's request. That pushes a literal-minded agent further toward deferring edits when the user named only awb-status.

What the run evidence shows:
- **retail-A (the only case a user could see).** In U4 the user sent five headline edits, then "Before you write the full draft: use awb-status". A4 opens "I'll record your headline changes", then makes no file changes; agent-notes confirm "no changes made". It ends with "This status pass stayed read-only under ... 'Stay read-only' instruction; your latest edits are pending in the package files". That wording is misleading, because the edits existed only in chat (the draft held only headline files). The simulated user raised it in human.md pain point 3, and the agent rated it Major in agent.md. One correction: the claim that it "cost a turn" is overstated. The user had asked for status before the full draft, so the U5 draft request was needed anyway. The real harm is that the edits went unrecorded and the agent described their state confusingly.
- **taxi-A (transcript lines 165-167 are accurate).** The user asked for a holiday caveat and status in one message. The agent made the edit and then ran status. It flagged the tension in agent-notes line 59 and agent.md line 28. No impact on the user.
- **co2-B.** The agent ran status and then the requested work, and recorded the ambiguity in agent.md line 24. No impact on the user.
- **retail-B.** I confirmed the sed edit on foundation/sources.md in relay agent-003.jsonl, and A3 says "I've changed it to say that". However, the user never asked for that edit. The agent was fixing an item the status report itself had flagged, which breaks the skill's "turn every fix into a next request". That is the agent ignoring the instruction once, not the mixed-request problem, so it only weakly supports this finding.

Two citations are wrong. The finding cites taxi-A-23, but the matching entry in taxi-A's findings.json is taxi-A-21 (taxi-A-23 is about the deck format). retail-B-42 does not exist: retail-B's findings.json runs only to retail-B-35.

Net: a real user who naturally writes "make these edits, then where are we?" hits wording that leaves the agent to guess. One of four agents deferred the edits and misdescribed where they stood; the other three worked around it. The release is the cause and the severity is minor. Confidence is medium because the only user-visible harm comes from one run.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-status/SKILL.md:8 "Stay *read-only*: report what the records say, and turn every fix into a next request." (no scope, no mixed-request guidance); README.md:84 and :123 describe status as read-only with no mixed-request note, while README.md:86 does give same-message-change guidance, but only for awb-release; awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:50 routes package corrections only through awb-package.

consolidated.title: No review pass for audience wording, definitions or display precision
consolidated.description: First full drafts carried wording and precision unsuited to a board: 'other located trips', an unexplained 'occupied hour', labels like $106.28, and arrow-heavy headlines. They also left terms undefined ('territorial', a repeat-buyer metric), used technical control-group wording, and wrote How we know bullets as instructions. Neither check-draft nor the review flagged these. Review repairs made for consistency spread misleading labels: 'largest buyers' for growth contributors, and pooled orders without a customer ID that 'count as one buyer'. findings-template sets a translation rule, but review step 3 checks rules and provenance, not readability. This matches Oct 15, where taxi-A's first deck needed five user corrections. retail-A-24 was tagged unclear because it is largely the agent's drafting.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-32: msg 7 corrections 2-5. retail-B-17: passes 5, 7, 9 and 10; U6; R-growth-contribution-001 and R-unidentified-orders-001. co2-A-16: U5 item 2. retail-A-24: U6 items 4-6.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none. Checked against the run folders:

1. **The problems were in the drafts themselves, not introduced by the relay.**
   - taxi-A: the draft turn's Codex stream (relay/agent-006.jsonl) contains "other located trips", "occupied hour" left undefined, and a display rounding of 2 decimal places that produced $106.28.
   - The agent then reported "The full review and final package checks passed".
   - The audience had been recorded in the brief as "The Lab board, nontechnical", so the template's translation rule applied and the draft still broke it.
   - human-007.out.md items 2-5 match the finding.
   - co2-A U5 item 2 ("territorial" undefined) matches.
   - retail-A U6 items 4-6 (control-group wording, How we know bullets written as instructions, undefined repeat-buyer metric) match.
   - retail-B U6 matches.

2. **It happened with both agent models and both persona models.**
   - Codex was the agent in taxi-A, co2-A and retail-A. Claude (claude -p) was the agent in retail-B.
   - So it is not one model's role behaviour.
   - Running non-interactively, the Codex sandbox, MCP auto-approval and the simulated home folder have no plausible bearing on draft wording or on what the reviewer checks.

3. **The personas were not set up to hunt for these problems.**
   - The four BRIEF.md files only say "review the deck draft like a real user ... ask for any corrections you would genuinely want (wording, a chart, an emphasis, a caveat)".
   - There is no script telling them to look for jargon or precision.
   - Front-loading facts at intake does not affect slide wording.
   - taxi-A human/notes.md shows the persona reacting to what it read: "$106.28. Too precise for the board" and "arrows reads like a spreadsheet".

4. **The retail-B claim about review repairs holds.** In relay/agent-005.jsonl, 12 Plan reviewer subagents ran.
   - The pass labelled "fifth pass" raised R-concentration-001 errors against "France's growth came from many buyers". The agent's fix became "France's three largest buyers supplied 32.9% of its growth", which uses "largest buyers" for growth contributors.
   - The passes labelled seventh, ninth and tenth flagged consistency gaps around no-ID revenue being "pooled as one buyer". The fixes put "orders without a customer ID count as one buyer" into findings.md:118.
   - The final pass was clean. The user then had to correct both labels (U6), and R-growth-contribution-001 and R-unidentified-orders-001 were recorded as a result.

5. **The release causes the gap.**
   - findings-template.md:5-7 sets the audience-language rule.
   - The only automated enforcement it names is check-draft flagging names "spelled the way the workbench spells" them.
   - Step 3 of review.md, the reviewer's own judgment pass, checks only: matching qualifications, claim strength, revalidation caveats, tracing to methodology.md, and citations for "checked/verified" claims.
   - Neither covers undefined terms, readability or display precision for the audience.
   - SKILL.md:58 asks the agent to choose decimal places, with no audience-precision guidance.

A real user on a normal host would get the same first draft past check-draft and the review.

One caveat: the wording is the drafting model's own, so how bad a first draft is will vary by model. That does not make it a harness artifact.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/references/review.md:22 (step 3 lists only qualifications, claim strength, revalidation caveats, tracing to methodology.md and citations for checked/verified claims, with no audience readability, definitions or precision check); awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:5-7 (sets the audience-words rule, but the only enforcement named is check-draft flagging workbench-spelled names); awb-package/SKILL.md:58 (agent sets decimal places in display.toml with no audience-precision guidance). Run evidence: taxi-A/relay/agent-006.jsonl (draft holds "other located trips", "occupied hour", rounding to 2 decimal places; agent-006.out.md:11 "full review and final package checks passed"); retail-B/relay/agent-005.jsonl reviewer passes labelled fifth, seventh, ninth and tenth (repairs introduce "three largest buyers supplied ... growth" and "count as one buyer"), retail-B/project/foundation/review-rules.md:31-44

verdicts.reasoning:
The cited finding IDs (taxi-A-32, retail-B-17, co2-A-16, retail-A-24) do not match the findings.json files. Those files stop at taxi-A-29, and retail-B-17, co2-A-16 and retail-A-24 there are unrelated findings. Every piece of evidence the finding describes does hold up when I read the transcripts and logs directly.

taxi-A: two fresh reviews passed the first full draft (project/.tmp/package-review-1 and -2, findings.md). That draft says "other located trips". It shows "$106.28 / $98.99" with "two-decimal labels" in the axis line. It names "occupied hour" without the plain explanation the user later asked for. Its headline is the arrow-heavy "Exclusions fell 4.9%→2.5% for one provider and rose 3.1%→4.1% for another", and it says "with zero-record tolerance". In transcript msg 7 the user corrects items 2-5 (plus 6).

retail-B: I pulled the reviewer reports from relay/agent-005.jsonl. Pass 2 demanded that the filter tolerances (50%, 3%) be added to findings.md and the note. In U6 the user had them removed. The repair after the agent's "fifth pass" (R-concentration-001) turned the headline into "France's three largest buyers supplied 32.9% of its growth". The "seventh", "ninth" and "tenth" passes made the agent spread "no-ID revenue is pooled as one buyer" across the narratives for consistency, ending in the slide caveat "orders without a customer ID count as one buyer". In U6 the user replaced both labels, which became R-growth-contribution and R-unidentified-orders.

co2-A: in U5 item 2 the user asks to define "territorial". retail-A: U6 items 4-6 cover the technical control-group wording, How we know bullets written as instructions, and an undefined repeat-buyer metric. In every run, check-draft and the full review had passed before the user stepped in.

The release causes this:
- **Reviewer scope.** review.md step 3 lists exactly what the reviewer judges: matching qualifications, claim strength, flags, tracing to methodology, and citations for "checked" claims. Step 4 says "Report exactly this, and nothing else". So the reviewer is never asked to judge undefined terms, audience-unsuitable labels, imperative voice or display precision, and is told not to report anything outside its list.
- **Tolerance rule.** Step 3 requires "the check in plain words, with its tolerance" in findings.md and the note. That rule pushed technical wording into audience text: taxi-A's "zero-record tolerance" and retail-B's filter thresholds.
- **Translation rule has no check.** findings-template.md:7 sets the translation rule, but its only enforcement is check-draft's names check, which matches workbench-spelled names. awb_draft.py:2484 states its "Known limits: this compares rendered text, not paraphrases or audience suitability."
- **No precision guidance.** SKILL.md:58 has the agent pick [round] places with no guidance on what precision suits the audience.

The translation rule is a general instruction, and it does not cover definitions, voice or precision. So the release does not prevent the problem: it leaves readability to the user's own review pass. A real user on a normal host would get the same first drafts and would have to make these corrections themselves. Minor severity is fair.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/references/review.md:22 (step 3 lists the only non-command checks: no audience wording, definitions, voice or precision check, and it requires "with its tolerance" in findings.md and the note); review.md:23 ("Report exactly this, and nothing else"); awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:7 (translation rule, enforced only by check-draft's names check); awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:2484-2485 ("Known limits: this compares rendered text, not paraphrases or audience suitability"); awb-package/SKILL.md:58 (agent picks [round] decimal places with no audience-precision guidance)

consolidated.title: Causal-wording check flags sentences that deny causation
consolidated.description: check-draft's phrase list refuses negated or harmless phrasings: 'attributable to' inside a negated sentence; 'does not test what caused them'; the user's own caveats 'the effect on repeat rates is unknown' and 'causes cannot be inferred'; and 'not trends or causes' and 'waiting and driving'. Agents paraphrased instead. In retail-B the agent then told the user a definition was 'in your wording' when it was not. Oct 15 kept this fail-safe behavior by design (5.7).
consolidated.oct15_ref: fix-plan 5.7 (I, negated causal wording kept by design)
consolidated.evidence: co2-A-22: methodology-note.md line 36. retail-B-20: package-contract.md line 49; A5 vs A7 text. co2-B-21: 'does not test what caused them'. taxi-B-33: claim-word false positives.

verdicts.reasoning:
The harness did not cause this. The flags come from a fixed regex in the release's check-draft code. The same draft text gives the same refusal on any host, with or without a sandbox, and whether the MCP tools are approved by hand or automatically.

I checked the actual check-draft results in the relay logs for all four runs:
- co2-A (Codex agent), relay/agent-004.jsonl item_30: claims row {file: methodology-note.md, line 36, section "Other limitations", phrase "attributable to", claim descriptive}. The agent then said it was "removing a phrase the checker reads as causal despite its qualification." The original sentence is gone, because the Codex file_change records hold no diff. So "negated" rests on the agent's notes, but the flagged line was in a limitations section either way.
- co2-B (Claude agent), relay/agent-004.jsonl line 105: claims row line 15, section Answer, phrase "caused". The source text was "The deck reports observed changes; it does not test what caused them." The agent changed it to "the reasons behind them".
- taxi-B, relay/agent-005.jsonl line 214: three rows were flagged:
  - "causes" in "Two months describe differences, not trends or causes" (Answer slide)
  - "causes" in the same sentence in methodology-note.md Limitations
  - "driving" in "not what drivers earn per hour, since waiting and driving between trips are not counted". Here "driving" is literal driving, not a causal word.
- retail-B, relay/agent-005.jsonl line 66: "effect on" (line 75) and "causes" (line 101) were flagged in caveats reading "the effect on repeat rates is unknown" and "causes cannot be inferred". The agent rewrote them at line 101.

The cause is in the release, and the documented rule produces it:
- `_CAUSAL` is a plain whole-word regex with no handling of negation or context.
- methodology-note.md is read whole at the deck's claim strength, with no exemption for its Limitations section. In findings.md, by contrast, the "Limitations and open caveats" slide is exempt. That mismatch is what caught the co2-A and taxi-B methodology-note lines.
- package-contract.md:49 states the refusal with no exception for negation.
- The Oct 15 fix plan (docs/ux-simulation-2026-10-15/fix-plan.md:106, item 5.7) records negated causal wording as an intended fail-safe that is kept.

The finding repeats across both agent models: Codex in co2-A, Claude in co2-B, taxi-B and retail-B. That rules out a quirk of one model.

Possible harness explanations, and why they fail:
1. Persona front-loading. In retail-B, the Codex-played user wrote "the effect on repeat rates is unknown" (transcript msg 4). That is ordinary caveat wording a real analyst would write, though, and in co2-A, co2-B and taxi-B the flagged phrases were the agent's own.
2. Model behavior. In retail-B the agent told the user the first-observed definition was "in your wording" (transcript ~line 393) after it had paraphrased the user's caveat to pass the check. That misstatement is the agent's honesty slip, so that part can be blamed on the model rather than the release. The release is still what forced the paraphrase, and the main finding (the check refuses sentences that deny causation) stands without it.
3. Non-interactive runs, the sandbox, the simulated home folder, relay mistakes. None of these touches a deterministic regex run on the draft text.

Severity is minor. Every agent cleared the flags by rewording. The behavior is intentional by design, but it is the release that causes it, and real users would hit it.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:1145-1150 (_CAUSAL whole-word regex including caus(?:es|ed|ing), driv(?:e|es|en|ing), effects?\s+(?:of|on), attributable\s+to; no negation handling); awb_draft.py:1286-1289 (methodology-note.md read whole at the deck's strongest claim, no exemption for its Limitations section); awb_draft.py:1296-1305 (_wording emits a row for every regex match below causal); awb-package/references/package-contract.md:49 (documents the refusal; exempts only the findings.md 'How we know', 'Limitations and open caveats', 'What changed since the last version' and 'Supporting datasets' slides).

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding holds up, and the release causes it. check-draft's claims check is a plain whole-word regex (_CAUSAL in awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py). It has no handling for negation, and it treats the verb "causes" and the noun "causes" the same way. Below causal strength, every match is refused. package-contract.md line 49 states the rule as "wording such as drives, causes ... is refused: reword it". helpers.md line 37 points to the phrase list and offers no override. The helper's own comment drops bare "cause" and "because" because "they also ... state disclaimers". It still matches "causes", "caused", "effect on" and "attributable to" in disclaimers.

I ran the release regex on each cited sentence and it matched every one. I then checked each run's actual check-draft output:
- co2-A: relay/agent-004.jsonl has a claims row for methodology-note.md line 36, section "Other limitations", phrase "attributable to". The review-copy snapshot (agent-home/.cache/awb-reviews/donor-roundtable/001/methodology-note.md:36) shows the sentence: "the emissions comparison does not quantify the exact share attributable to war." This example is the weakest of the four. The sentence assumes some share is caused by war, and the same line says "affected by war", which the checker does not catch ("affected" is left off the list).
- co2-B: relay/agent-004.jsonl has a claims row at Answer line 15, phrase "caused", for "The deck reports observed changes; it does not test what caused them." The agent changed it to "the reasons behind them".
- retail-B: relay/agent-005.jsonl has claims rows for "effect on" (line 75) and "causes" (line 101). The user's message 4 asked word for word for "the effect on repeat rates is unknown" and said cancellation causes can't be inferred. The agent's reply 4 used that wording. The released findings.md reads "how much that changes their repeat rates is unknown" (line 61) and "why orders were cancelled cannot be inferred" (line 80). Yet the agent's reply 5 (transcript line 393) told the user the caveat was "in your wording".
- taxi-B: relay/agent-005.jsonl has claims rows for "causes" in "Two months describe differences, not trends or causes" (Answer and methodology-note) and "driving" in "waiting and driving between trips". The agent changed them to "reasons" and "cruising".

A real user on a normal interactive host gets the same refusals, and the retail-B user had their own caveat wording overridden. That makes this a product issue. It is minor: each case cost one reword, and the strict rule is apparently a deliberate fail-safe.

Two problems with the finding's citations, not its substance:
- Some evidence IDs do not match the runs' findings.json. The actual entries are co2-A-18, retail-B-15 and taxi-B-21. retail-B-20 is about the settings.toml template, and taxi-B-33 is about the simulated user's calendar mistake.
- I could not trace the "Oct 15 by design (5.7)" note to any file. Even if accurate, it only says the behavior is intended; the release still causes it.
