Also findings-template.md:16 and methodology-note-template.md:9.

consolidated.title: Preview-and-wait has no defined artifact, location or status
consolidated.description: #61 added the preview-and-wait checkpoint, but neither the package contract nor awb-status defines a preview file or state. Agents improvised preview-plan.md or headline-preview.md in the draft folder, plus a headline-only findings.md that cannot pass the final checks. co2-A's headline-preview.md, with Q- and result IDs in it, shipped in frozen release 001: the inventory freezes every file in the draft folder, and START-HERE does not classify it. Status showed the missing manifest and narratives, expected at that stage, as gaps.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-04: transcript line 223. co2-A-14: storage/releases/co2-country-priorities/donor-roundtable/001/headline-preview.md. retail-A-19: A4.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to pin this on the harness and could not. Every part of the finding checks out against the run files and the release code.

1. **The release defines no preview artifact.** awb-package step 3 says only to write the title slide and every headline and "show them". It names no location. The contract's draft layout (package-contract.md:9-19) lists no preview file. In all three Codex-agent runs the agent made its own. taxi-A wrote preview-plan.md plus a findings.md holding only headlines (agent-005 log; agent-notes say "Created headline-only findings.md and preview-plan.md under the standard draft path"). co2-A and retail-A each wrote headline-preview.md. taxi-A happened to move its file out of the draft before release (agent-006 log), and retail-A's released/001 does not contain one either. co2-A's shipped.

2. **The shipping path is in the release code and would work the same on any host.** inventory() scans every file in the draft (awb_draft.py:1660-1694). check-draft rewrites the inventory, and no check flags unknown files. start_here() lists only the files it knows (awb_draft.py:2580-2614). So co2-A's draft/headline-preview.md went into released/001, into its manifest inventory (manifest.json line 1981), and into storage/releases/.../001. Its contents are byte-identical to the draft. It holds Q- and result IDs, and START-HERE never mentions it. The co2-A user noticed this unprompted (human.md line 45; notes line 51).

3. **The status gap is in the release.** collect_status.py:422-423 reports a draft with no manifest as an uncertainty ("Draft lacks manifest.json"). The awb-status table routes uncertainties that name a missing standard record to "Bring the workbench up to date (awb-init)", and no row covers the preview stage. In retail-A's status turn (A4) the collector returned exactly that uncertainty, and the agent had to explain it away by hand.

**Harness explanations, checked one by one:**
- **Non-interactive exec.** It did not force a file onto disk. The relay resumes the same Codex session every turn (`codex exec resume <id>`, agent-005.err and agent-006.err), so the agent kept its context and did not need to save the preview to remember it.
- **Sandbox, auto-approved MCP, simulated home.** None of these played any part in creating or shipping the file.
- **Personas front-loading "preview-and-wait".** This does not matter, because preview-and-wait is the release's default mode anyway. No user ever asked for a saved file.
- **Model behavior.** This is the one real mitigation: only Codex agents improvised a preview file. The variant-B Claude agents wrote only findings.md, methodology.md and methodology-note.md. But the README (line 5) names OpenAI Codex as a supported host, and the release leaves the location unspecified, so a real Codex user can hit this. Once any agent puts a stray file in the draft, the release freezes it with no warning.

**Evidence citation errors in the finding.** Two cited IDs point to unrelated findings:
- co2-A-14 is about the initial-commit wording. The preview-file finding is co2-A-12.
- retail-A-19 is about START-HERE listing methodology.md twice. The status finding is retail-A-23.

Neither error affects the verdict. Minor severity fits.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/SKILL.md:47 (preview-and-wait says "write ... show them" but names no location); awb-package/references/package-contract.md:9-19 (the draft layout has no preview file); awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:1660-1694 (inventory freezes every file in the draft); awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:2580-2614 (START-HERE lists only known files); awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py:422-423 (a draft with no manifest is reported as an uncertainty); awb-status/SKILL.md:50 and :60 (that uncertainty routes to awb-init, and a draft with no release prompts "mark delivered")

verdicts.reasoning:
The release defines preview-and-wait only as a step, with no artifact, location or state. awb-package/SKILL.md:47 says to "write the title slide and every slide headline ... show them". It never says where to write them. package-contract.md:39 repeats the mode rules and also names no file. The draft layout at package-contract.md:7-19 lists no preview file, and nothing says what to do with a partial draft before approval.

All three A-run agents read "write" as "write a file in the draft folder":
- taxi-A wrote preview-plan.md plus a headline-only findings.md (transcript line 223 links draft/preview-plan.md; agent-009 notes say so). Later, in agent-006, it moved the file to .tmp/ itself.
- retail-A wrote headline-preview.md plus a headline-only findings.md (agent-008 notes). In agent-005 it moved the preview to investigations/.../headline-checkpoint.md.
- co2-A wrote headline-preview.md and never removed it, believing "the package contract requires headline preview before full slides" (agent-004/007 notes).

Nothing in the release catches a leftover file:
- inventory() in awb_draft.py:1690 scans every file in the draft folder.
- check-draft reads only the narratives (_narratives, awb_draft.py:1117).
- start_here() (awb_draft.py:2581) lists only the files it knows about.
- release copies the verified draft as it stands.

As a result, co2-A's release 001 holds headline-preview.md, which contains Q-001..Q-005 and result IDs such as territorial-change, ranking-groups and ukraine-timing. The file is in the release's manifest inventory, and START-HERE.md does not mention it. The simulated user flagged this in co2-A/feedback/human.md:45.

On status: collect_status.py:422-423 records "Draft lacks manifest.json; awb-package rewrites it on the next revision" as an uncertainty whenever a draft folder has no manifest. The retail-A A4 collector output shows exactly this at the preview stage, and the agent had to explain it by hand. Nothing in the release describes a preview or awaiting-approval state.

One overstatement: the status collector does not itself flag missing narratives. Only the missing manifest shows up as an uncertainty; the agent's notes mention the narratives. Every other part of the finding is supported.

A real user on a normal interactive host would hit the same unclear instruction and the same unguarded freeze-everything inventory. Nothing here depends on the harness.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/SKILL.md:47 ("write the title slide and every slide headline ... show them", no file or location named); awb-package/references/package-contract.md:7-19 (draft layout, no preview file, no rule about extra files) and :39; awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:1690-1694 (inventory scans every draft file), :1117-1123 (checks read only the narratives), :2581-2620 (START-HERE lists only known files); awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py:422-423 ("Draft lacks manifest.json" uncertainty, no preview state). Shipped result: co2-A/storage/releases/co2-country-priorities/donor-roundtable/001/headline-preview.md, listed in that release's manifest.json inventory.

consolidated.title: awb-init's interview-before-creation rule leaves no place to record a detailed first message
consolidated.description: #62 made awb-init run awb-scope's first interview round before the investigation exists. When the first message already supplies questions, sources, audience, storage locations and checkpoint mode, as the README recommends, there is no pending-intake record to hold them. Agents parked those facts in an improvised README 'Scope intake' section, and taxi-A's agent felt it had to justify the pause. The underlying Oct 15 problem, no interview at all, is fixed.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-19: README append 'Scope intake — awaiting first interview answers'; awb-init step 4. co2-A-27: README line 94 recommends a complete first message. retail-A-10: agent-notes initial setup entry.

verdicts.reasoning:
The rule the finding describes is real. awb-init step 4 runs awb-scope's first interview round before the investigation exists, and the brief, where audience, length and checkpoint mode belong, is created only after that round. But the friction comes from the agent model, its host prompt and the harness, not from the release.

1. **Only Codex agents did it.** The three runs where Codex played the agent (taxi-A, co2-A, retail-A) each added a temporary README section and logged the missing record as friction. The three runs where Claude played the agent (taxi-B, co2-B, retail-B) ran the same release on equally detailed first messages. None of them added an intake record. They kept the facts in the conversation and created the investigation on the next turn. co2-B's log calls the rule "clear enough" (co2-B/feedback/agent-notes.md:8), and retail-B's calls it "clear" (retail-B/feedback/agent-notes.md:13). taxi-B wrote the storage paths into README lines the template already has.

2. **No information was at risk.** Every later turn resumed the same session by id (`codex exec resume <id>`, `claude -p --resume <id>`), so the first message stayed in context. The improvised section was removed in turn 2 (taxi-A/relay/agent-002.jsonl cuts README at "## Scope intake"), and no final README still has one. No fact was lost and nothing was asked twice. All three simulated users rated the scoping round good or excellent and said putting everything in the first message saved turns.

3. **The "justify the pause" part comes from Codex's own base instructions.** In the taxi-A rollout's session_meta, those instructions tell the model to explain why it stops to ask, naming the source, such as a SKILL.md, in a separate paragraph at the end. Codex's Default collaboration mode also says to "strongly prefer ... executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask". retail-A's log names this tension: "developer says prefer execution and avoid confirmation". The same quoting of skill files shows up in awb-package and awb-status turns too, so it is not specific to init.

4. **The complaint came from a log the harness asked for.** The harness note told the agent to record anything "missing", and the claim that the facts needed a durable record is the Codex agent's guess in that log. It is not a failure anyone saw.

5. **The release expects these facts to live in the session.** README.md:64 says naming storage folders in the first message "usually saves the question within that session". The storage paths already have README lines, and brief.md:19 holds length and checkpoint mode once the investigation exists.

Front-loaded first messages are not a harness artifact, since README.md:44 and README.md:94 recommend them. But they caused no failure here.

**What remains real:** a session that ends before the interview is answered would lose the first-message facts. No run showed that, so nothing here shows that a user on a normal interactive host would hit it because of the release.

**Why confidence is medium, not high:** a real Codex CLI user gets the same base prompt and might see the same improvised section and skill-quoting paragraph. Those behaviors come from the host and model, not the release.
verdicts.release_evidence: The rule is real: awb-init/SKILL.md:46 runs awb-scope's first interview round before the investigation exists. The release's own records point against the finding: README.md:64 expects first-message facts to be reused within the same session; brief.md:19 is where length and checkpoint mode go once the investigation exists; storage locations already have README template lines. The Claude-agent runs under the same release found the rule clear (co2-B/feedback/agent-notes.md:8, retail-B/feedback/agent-notes.md:13). The pause justification follows Codex's base instructions in the taxi-A rollout session_meta, not the release.

verdicts.reasoning:
What the finding gets right: the release has no holding record for a detailed first message. awb-init/SKILL.md:24 and :46 tell the agent to ask awb-scope's first interview round before the investigation exists. awb-scope/SKILL.md:42 writes the records only after that round. All three Codex runs (variant A) then wrote first-message facts into the project README. taxi-A appended a '## Scope intake — awaiting first interview answers' section (relay/agent-001.jsonl item_24; agent-notes.md:9). co2-A wrote a 'temporary README handoff' (agent-notes.md:16; agent.md item 10). retail-A preserved the intake in the README (agent-notes.md:6,8; agent.md item 5).

Why the cause looks like the harness and not the release:
(1) The same release ran on Claude Code (variant B), the more representative interactive host, and all three runs handled it cleanly. They kept the facts in the conversation, asked the round and said they would create the records from the answers. taxi-B reply 1 says 'Investigation records: none yet. I'll create them from your answers.' co2-B agent-notes.md:8 calls the instruction 'clear enough', and retail-B agent-notes.md:13 calls it 'clear'. None of them improvised a record or justified the pause.
(2) The Codex agents' stated motive was keeping the facts across turns ('so a future turn does not lose the five user questions'; 'otherwise the rich initial request would not have durable records'). retail-A also cites Codex developer instructions that 'favored continuing authorized work'. Both fit the non-interactive `codex exec` relay, not the release. On a normal interactive host the conversation carries those facts to the next turn, where awb-scope writes the brief.
(3) Justifying the pause is the agent ignoring a clear instruction. The shipped AGENTS.md template line 30 says 'never send them to a skill or instruction file'. All three Codex agents broke this repeatedly, also later in awb-package and awb-release turns (human feedback in taxi-A, co2-A and retail-A). The Claude agents never did.
(4) No user-visible harm is shown. The simulated users praised the scoping round, and the README sections were later replaced.

Corrections to the finding:
- The cited IDs point to unrelated findings. taxi-A-19 is about producer imports, co2-A-27 about a relay logging gap and retail-A-10 about slide count. The matching findings are taxi-A-17, co2-A-23 and retail-A-09.
- README.md:94 observes that a shorter first message means more questions; it does not recommend a complete one. README.md:64 does encourage naming storage folders early, but those already have homes on the template README's 'Landed data is kept at' and 'Released packages are kept at' lines (assets/workbench/README.md:9,11).

What a real user could still hit: if the session is lost between the setup turn and the answers, the first message's facts are gone. No run shows that, which is why confidence is medium rather than high.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/SKILL.md:46 (run awb-scope's first interview round before it creates the investigation); awb-scope/SKILL.md:42 (records written after the interview); awb-init/assets/workbench/README.md:9,11 (storage locations already have record lines); awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:30 (never send the user to a skill or instruction file, which the Codex agents broke when justifying the pause); README.md:64,94 (encourages a detailed first message but does not require a holding record). Contrast: Claude agents running the same release kept the facts in conversation without improvising (taxi-B reply 1; co2-B agent-notes.md:8; retail-B agent-notes.md:13).

consolidated.title: Chart-spec wording leads to blank lines that make check-draft count spec fields as bullets
consolidated.description: findings-template says to 'leave a blank line between them and the slide's next bullet'. Agents read that as blank lines between the Data, Highlight and Axis fields, and check-draft then counted the fields as bullets ('10 bullets; keep it to 5'). All three Opus agents hit it. helpers.md explains that a blank line ends the fields.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-27. co2-B-17: findings-template.md:19; outline failure in A4. retail-B-19: two regex repair passes.

verdicts.reasoning:
Every harness explanation I tested fails.

1. The agents read the release's own words. In all three B runs, the agent read package-format/findings-template.md from the project copy installed by the release's helper, and cmp shows each copy is byte-identical to the release template.

2. Nothing in the harness touches Markdown formatting. kit/claude-agent-system.md says nothing about blank lines, bullets or Markdown.

3. Interactivity, relay, sandbox and MCP approval play no part. The agent wrote findings.md, ran check-draft and repaired the file itself, all inside one agent turn (taxi-B agent-005, co2-B agent-004, retail-B agent-005). B runs use Claude, so there is no Codex sandbox. The simulated home only changes paths. Personas are irrelevant.

4. The blank lines come from the template prose, not a general model habit. In both co2-B and retail-B, the first findings.md write has tight slide bullets but a blank line between every chart field, which matches a reading of "leave a blank line between them and the slide's next bullet". taxi-B put one blank line after **Data:** only. Each time, the fields after the blank line counted as slide bullets, and check-draft reported "10 bullets; keep it to 5" or "11 bullets" on every finding slide. The outline message never mentions the chart specification, so the agents had to work out the cause themselves.

5. All three agents independently blame the same sentence, findings-template.md:19, in their notes and feedback (taxi-B, co2-B and retail-B agent-notes.md and agent.md). The fixes cost one regex pass in co2-B and two in retail-B (retail-B agent-005 lines 17 and 20).

6. helpers.md:11 does state the rule that a blank line before the next field ends the fields. But the agents had read helpers.md and were still misled by the template prose.

What argues against: the Codex agents in the A runs did not hit this. Their specs are tight, and co2-A's "bullets; keep" match is only the agent reading source code. So the misreading depends on the model. Claude Code is a host the release supports, though, and 3 of 3 Opus agents hit it. A real Claude Code user's agent would read the same sentence the same way.

Corrections to the finding as written:
- Two of its evidence IDs point to the wrong entries. taxi-B-27 is the README-length issue and retail-B-19 is the awb.py sql parameter issue. The matching entries are taxi-B-15 and retail-B-14; co2-B-17 is correct.
- taxi-B's form was a single blank line after Data, not blank lines between all fields. The mechanism is the same.

Severity minor is right: each agent fixed it itself within the turn.
verdicts.release_evidence: release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:19 ("The specification's fields are the bullets directly under its line, each one paragraph with nothing nested under it, so leave a blank line between them and the slide's next bullet"). The rule it collides with is at awb-package/references/helpers.md:11 ("a blank line before the next one at that depth, or any other block, ends them"). check-draft's outline row is in awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py: it says only "N bullets; keep it to 5" and never names the chart fields.

verdicts.reasoning:
The shipped template wording is ambiguous, and all three runs show the failure in their transcripts.

Release cause: findings-template.md:19 says the fields are "each one paragraph with nothing nested under it, so leave a blank line between them and the slide's next bullet". "Each one paragraph" and "a blank line between them" can easily be read as "separate each field with a blank line". The parser enforces the opposite. In awb_draft.py:1853, `not (block["gap"] and chart["fields"])` ends the fields at the first blank line that follows a field, so the remaining fields become slide bullets. The outline message at awb_draft.py:2023 then says only "N bullets; keep it to 5". It never mentions the chart specification, which makes the fault harder to trace.

Raw relay evidence (I checked it directly, not only the feedback summaries):
- taxi-B relay/agent-005.jsonl, line 175: the Write puts a blank line after **Data:**. The check-draft result at line 214 reports 9 to 11 bullets on all 10 finding slides. The agent's notes at line 1375 call it a misreading of that template sentence.
- co2-B relay/agent-004.jsonl, line 84: blank lines after the Chart line and between every field. The result at line 105 reports 10 to 11 bullets. A first fix (line 112) still fails, and a second regex pass (line 117) repairs it.
- retail-B relay/agent-005.jsonl, line 50: blank lines between every field. The result at line 66 reports 10 to 11 bullets. After the first regex at line 101, the result at line 107 still reports 9 to 10. A second regex at line 117 makes it pass.

All three agents raise it on their own in feedback/agent.md (taxi-B §1.6, co2-B §1.8, retail-B §1.5).

What already prevents it, and why it didn't:
- The template's example block (findings-template.md:21-30) shows the fields with no blank lines between them.
- helpers.md:11 says a blank line ends the fields. taxi-B read helpers.md (relay line 71) before drafting. But that rule sits inside a very dense paragraph of the reference, while the drafting prose in the template is what agents follow. No agent repeated the mistake after check-draft flagged it; each one repaired it. So this is not an agent ignoring a clear instruction again and again.

The Codex agents in the A runs wrote the fields with no blank lines between them and did not hit this. So the misreading depends on the model, but it hit 3 of 3 Opus runs, which is what a Claude-hosted user would run.

Severity minor is right: check-draft catches it, and it costs one or two repair cycles.

Citation errors in the finding: taxi-B-27 is the README finding; the relevant one is taxi-B-15. retail-B-19 is the `awb.py sql` finding; the relevant one is retail-B-14. co2-B-17 is correct. The "two regex repair passes" happened in both co2-B and retail-B.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:19 ("each one paragraph with nothing nested under it, so leave a blank line between them and the slide's next bullet"). awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:1853 (a blank line after a field ends the fields) and awb_draft.py:2023 (the bullet-count message does not mention the chart). Mitigations that did not prevent it: the template example at findings-template.md:21-30 and the rule at awb-package/references/helpers.md:11.

consolidated.title: Default ledger storyline misplaces supporting-question slides, and presentation_order is maintained by hand
consolidated.description: #61's presentation_order lets the user's order stand, but several frictions remain. The ledger-derived default put slides citing a child or supporting question (EU reconciliation, Q-006) out of narrative order. Agents proposed the user's order at the headline step without seeing the derived one, so check-draft failed on storyline rows until presentation_order was written. The field then had to be edited by hand in manifest.json whenever a heading changed. No tool previews the derived order.
consolidated.evidence: co2-A-21: check-draft 'move it to finding position 5'. co2-B-20: manifest edits in A4-A7. retail-A-21: concentration expected at position 3, products at 5.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not tie any part of this to the harness. Here is what I checked.

1. **co2-A: the default order really did move the slides.** In agent-004.jsonl, check-draft's storyline row says to move the GDP slide (Q-002) "to finding position 5".
   - In questions.json, the agent made Q-006 (eligibility and the EU-27 reconciliation) a `must` child of Q-001.
   - The consumption and history slides cite that reconciliation result in methodology.md.
   - The release ranks a slide by the best-ranked question among all the results it cites. Supporting results count the same as the main one. So both slides take Q-006's place right after Q-001 and land ahead of GDP.

2. **co2-B: the priority sort did it.** Q-006 is a `should` child of Q-002. The release sorts by priority before tree position, so that slide goes after every `must` root.
   - The Claude agent did see the default order and told the user so ("The default would put it last"). The user approved the agent's reorder.
   - In agent-005 to agent-007, the agent ran Python snippets that rewrote presentation_order entries every time a heading changed.

3. **retail-A: the release counted ordinary words as citations.** Check-draft in agent-005 wanted concentration at position 3 and products at 5.
   - I recomputed the citations. Common words in the prose, such as "monthly" in the repeat slide's "the full-year monthly range", match result IDs. The release counts a result ID found anywhere in a methodology section as a citation.
   - That ties the repeat and international slides to Q-001 and Q-002 results, which moves them earlier.

4. **No harness cause.**
   - The persona briefs say nothing about slide order.
   - The users only said "Order is fine" to the order the agent proposed.
   - The harness note just asks for a friction log.
   - Nothing about non-interactive exec, the sandbox, auto-approval, the simulated home folder or the relay affects how the order is derived or checked.

5. **The release's own design produces the remaining friction.**
   - Its only package commands are export, review-rules check and check-draft. None of them lists the derived order.
   - The derived order depends on methodology citations, and those don't exist yet at a preview-and-wait headline step. So the agent has to derive it by hand.
   - By design, presentation_order is written only by hand, only after export has written the manifest, and it must be reworded by hand whenever a heading changes.

A real user on a normal interactive host, with the same agent, would hit all of this.

**Caveats on the finding's wording:**
- Two evidence IDs point to unrelated findings. co2-A-21 is about awb-status freshness and retail-A-21 is about setup and DuckDB. The right entries are co2-A-17 and retail-A-25. The quoted check-draft text is still real.
- "Agents proposed the user's order without seeing the derived one" applies only to co2-A and retail-A. In co2-B the agent saw the default order and explained it.
- Hand-editing presentation_order is documented behaviour rather than a bug, but it is still friction caused by the release.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:2390-2405 (storyline_problems: priority sorts before walk position, and each slide takes the best-ranked question among all its cited results, supporting ones included); awb_draft.py:1186-1190 with 702-709 (_cited counts any whole-token mention of a result ID in a methodology section, e.g. the word 'monthly'); awb-package/references/package-contract.md:33-35 (ledger order is the default; presentation_order overrides it) and :50 (commands write every manifest field except presentation_order); awb-package/assets/package-format/manifest-template.md:49 (rewording a heading means rewording its presentation_order entry); awb-package/SKILL.md:52 (propose the ledger-derived order; record presentation_order only once export has written the manifest); package-contract.md:70-72 (only export, review-rules check and check-draft exist, so no command previews the order)

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked each part of the finding against the shipped files and the run logs. All four parts hold up, with two corrections to the details.

1) The default order puts supporting or child-question slides out of narrative order. The release causes this.
- storyline_problems ranks each slide by the earliest question that any cited result answers: `min(questions, key=ranks)`. The rank is priority first, then position in a depth-first walk of the question tree. The package contract's Ledger storyline section says the same.
- co2-A: methodology cites `eu-reconciliation` as "supported by" on the consumption and cumulative-shares slides. That result answers Q-006, a must-priority child of Q-001. Both slides therefore rank ahead of the GDP slide (Q-002). check-draft (relay agent-004.jsonl) reported: GDP slide at position 3, expected 5, "move it to finding position 5".
- co2-B: Q-006 is a should-priority child of Q-002. Because priority is compared before tree position, its slide sorts after every must-priority root.
- retail-A: check-draft (relay agent-005.jsonl) reported concentration at position 2, expected 3, and products at 4, expected 5. The cause there is different. The result-ID matcher (`_name_pattern`/`_cited`) treats plain words in methodology prose as citations. "the full-year monthly range" in the cohorts section cited result `monthly` (Q-001). "customer concentration" in the Australia section cited `concentration` (Q-002). With correct citations, the ledger order would have matched the user's Q1–Q5 order. The docstring records this as a known limit, but the user-facing docs never explain it. So in retail-A the release mis-derived the order, rather than ordering a real supporting citation badly.

2) Proposing at the headline step without seeing the derived order, and the check-draft failures.
- The skill says "Propose the ledger-derived finding order". No command computes it: the CLI table has no such command, and `questions list` prints the question tree, not the slide order.
- The derived order depends on which results each methodology section cites. In preview-and-wait mode those sections are written after the headlines are approved.
- co2-A: the agent's headline-preview.md said "All findings follow the ledger-derived order". It was true for the citations planned then. The order changed once the full methodology cited eu-reconciliation, and check-draft failed until presentation_order was written. This is a correction to the finding: the co2-A agent did try to propose the derived order. It did not simply propose the user's order.
- retail-A: check-draft failed once, then presentation_order was written.
- co2-B: no failure, because the agent wrote presentation_order before running check-draft.

3) presentation_order is edited by hand whenever a heading changes.
- The manifest template says "You record it and `export` keeps it", and "A revision that rewords a finding heading rewords its entry here too."
- co2-B relay logs show hand-written Python updating the manifest's presentation_order alongside every heading change: agent-004 line 104, agent-005 lines 31 and 491, agent-006 line 54.

4) No tool previews the derived order. Confirmed. The storyline rows give only the moved slide's own question, so the agent cannot see why other slides jumped ahead. The retail-A agent said it could not tell whether the order was wrong.

Nothing here depends on the simulation harness; a real user on a normal interactive host would hit the same thing. Severity minor is fair: each case cost one failed check plus the manual edits.

The finding's evidence IDs are mislabeled. co2-A-21 and retail-A-21 in findings.json are unrelated items (state freshness, and interpreter setup). The matching items are co2-A-17 and retail-A-25. The quoted check-draft outputs are real.
