One citation in the finding is wrong. The retail-B finding is retail-B-17, not retail-B-22, which is about the sources.md template. The underlying retail-B evidence is still sound.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/awb_validate.py:124 (join["left_rows"] read with no check; compare _judgment at lines 158-163, which raises a clear ValueError); awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/settings.toml:33 (comment says "left_rows usually from a producer" and never says it is required); awb-init/references/validation.md:11,15 (says producers supply joins.left_rows; gives a default only for keys_unique); awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/run.py:168-170 (prints the traceback for each result and continues)

consolidated.title: Scan helpers' generic heuristics miss panel-data issues and cannot express per-file rules
consolidated.description: eda_scan.py casts the date column to DATE, so it fails on an integer year column ('Unimplemented type for cast (INTEGER -> DATE)'), and it does not report coverage years per measure. The clean scan missed the mix of countries and aggregates and Kosovo's missing ISO code, and flagged aggregates as IQR extremes instead. clean-scan --range takes one global range per column, so a per-file month rule had to become an exclusion local to the investigation. Oct 15 co2-A reported the same scanner miss on aggregates; the recorder side of that complaint was fixed by 9.3.
consolidated.oct15_ref: Oct 15 per-run co2-A agent.md item 8 (scanner side; recorder side fixed by fix-plan 9.3, #65)
consolidated.evidence: co2-B-13: eda_scan.py lines 337-342, 417 and 454. co2-B-14: issue added as 'new' in foundation/quality.md. taxi-B-42: awb-clean SKILL section 1 '--range COL=MIN:MAX'.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not find a harness cause. Both runs used scripts that are byte-identical to the release: diff -q found no difference for co2-B's agent-home eda_scan.py or taxi-B's scan_dataset.py. Every behavior in the finding comes from the released code acting on the dataset, so a real user would see the same thing on an interactive host.

1) Integer year column (co2-B, relay/agent-002.jsonl lines 126-131). The agent did what awb-explore SKILL step 2 says: pass "its date column as --date-column (with --start and --end ...)". For the OWID panel that column is `year`, stored as INTEGER. The release then failed with a ScanError: "scope filter failed on owid_co2: Conversion Error: Unimplemented type for cast (INTEGER -> DATE) ... pass --where or --no-scope". The agent recovered 4 seconds later by moving the year filter into --where. On the rescan, `year` is not of temporal kind, so the scan leaves out coverage, null rates by period and over-time output. That is why no per-measure coverage years appear. Nothing here depends on the sandbox, the relay, approvals or the persona. Two qualifications:
- The finding cites the wrong lines. Lines 337-342, 417 and 454 only run for columns of temporal kind, and pick_date never hands them an integer column. The cast that actually fails is at line 755 in scope_filters.
- The help text does say "date or timestamp column", so this is a documented limit hit by following the SKILL, not a crash.

2) Clean scan missed aggregates and Kosovo (co2-B). The generic checks in checks.md have no rule for mixed entity types, and they list heavy-tailed quantities as a common `extreme` false positive. The scan output matches that: DQ-002 flagged co2 extremes that turned out to be aggregates, and the agent recorded the aggregates issue as `new` DQ-004. This is the gap the finding describes. However, awb-clean SKILL section 2 plans for it: "An in-scope problem the scan missed ... recorded as a `new` issue." The persona's front-loading told the agent about aggregates early, but it did not change what the scan printed.

3) Global --range (taxi-B). The agent passed `tpep_pickup_datetime=2024-01-01:2024-08-01` through the MCP clean-scan call, and agent-notes.md line 21 records the per-file complaint. Three things weaken this part:
- The cited id taxi-B-42 does not exist. taxi-B findings.json has only taxi-B-01 to taxi-B-35, and none of them mention range.
- The agent itself wrote "fine as investigation-local".
- The SKILL classes a `range` used as the reporting period as an investigation-local choice. scan_dataset.py also accepts a single data file as its target, so each monthly file could have been scanned with its own range.

Overall: the cause is the release's generic scan design, not the harness. Severity minor is right. Parts of the finding are documented by-design limits, and its line and id citations are partly wrong.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-explore/scripts/eda_scan.py:755. scope_filters always builds `CAST(<date_column> AS DATE) >= CAST(<start> AS DATE)`, which is the INTEGER -> DATE failure. eda_scan.py:651-658 give coverage and by-period output only to temporal-kind columns, so an integer year gets none. awb-clean/references/checks.md lists heavy-tailed quantities as an `extreme` false positive and has no aggregate check. awb-clean/SKILL.md section 1 has `--range COL=MIN:MAX` with one range per spec; section 2 classes a period `range` as investigation-local and says a missed problem is recorded as a `new` issue. awb-clean/scripts/scan_dataset.py:803 accepts a data file as the target.

verdicts.reasoning:
Only one part of this bundled finding holds up: the integer-year limitation in eda_scan.py. The other two parts describe cases the release already plans for, and the agents treated them that way.

1) Integer year column (CONFIRMED, release-caused, minor). awb-explore/SKILL.md:22 tells the agent to pass the brief's date column as --date-column, adding --start and --end when settings hold no period. co2-B did exactly that (relay/agent-002.jsonl): `eda_scan.py ... --date-column year --start 1850 --end 2024`. It failed with "scope filter failed on owid_co2: Conversion Error: Unimplemented type for cast (INTEGER -> DATE) ... pass --where or --no-scope". The crash comes from scope_filters at eda_scan.py:755, which always emits `CAST(col AS DATE) >= CAST('1850' AS DATE)`. The cited lines 337-342, 417 and 454 are not the crash site. They are the coverage, null-by-period and trend queries, and they show the related design limit: TEMPORAL (line 35) and pick_date (lines 760-767) accept only DATE/TIMESTAMP. So even after the agent recovered with `--where "... AND year >= 1850"`, the date column was None and the scan gave no per-year coverage or trend. The agent had wanted per-year coverage for each measure. The --help text does say "date or timestamp column", but the SKILL instruction gives no caveat for annual panel data such as OWID or World Bank. A real user on a normal host would hit this. Mitigating factors: the error is clean (exit 2), it names the fix, and recovery took one retry, so the severity is minor.

2) Clean scan missed the mix of countries and aggregates, and Kosovo's missing ISO code (NOT a release defect). The checks are generic by design (checks.md lists `extreme` with heavy-tailed false positives). awb-clean/SKILL.md:33 explicitly says: "An in-scope problem the scan missed, such as one a saved query shows, is decided the same way and recorded as a `new` issue." The agent followed that path without trouble. DQ-004 in co2-B/project/foundation/quality.md records the mix, with reconciliation-query evidence and an is_country view fix. DQ-002 classifies the aggregate extremes correctly. Asking a generic scanner to detect rows that are sums of other rows, or to know that Kosovo is a country, is a feature request rather than something the release broke.

3) clean-scan --range is one global range per column (NOT a real problem). The taxi-B evidence is only a note in agent-notes.md:21: "can only express one global range ... fine as investigation-local". The user's own brief defines "pickup outside the month the file covers" as a screening rule for this investigation. awb-clean/SKILL.md:28 classes a reporting-period `range` as an investigation-local choice anyway, so a per-file range option would not have changed where the rule landed. DQ-007 records it consistently. No user-visible harm occurred.

Net: the verdict is product, limited to the eda_scan integer-year limitation (failed cast plus no per-year coverage). The aggregate-detection and per-file-range parts should be dropped or downgraded to enhancement suggestions.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-explore/scripts/eda_scan.py:755 (scope_filters builds CAST(col AS DATE) for --start/--end); eda_scan.py:35 and 760-767 (TEMPORAL regex and pick_date accept only DATE/TIMESTAMP, so an integer year column gets no coverage or trend, which affects lines 337-342, 417 and 454); awb-explore/SKILL.md:22 (tells the agent to pass the date column with --date-column/--start/--end). Contradicts the other subclaims: awb-clean/SKILL.md:33 (scan misses are recorded as `new` issues) and awb-clean/SKILL.md:28 (a reporting-period range is an investigation-local choice).

consolidated.title: display.toml feedback gaps: label warnings cannot be resolved, boolean value keys silently miss
consolidated.description: #64's collision warning repeats a label_warnings entry on every export for a display name several results share ('Month' across five), with no way to mark it confirmed. Boolean value keys (true = 'Yes') silently match nothing, because the saved CSV holds 'True'.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-33: awb-package SKILL step 4 'For each label_warnings column, confirm its name suits every result'. co2-B-19: display.toml edit in A4.

verdicts.reasoning:
I found no harness cause for either half. Both come from deterministic code paths in the release, and a real user on a normal interactive host would hit them the same way.

**Boolean value keys (co2-B):**
- The co2-B agent was Claude Opus running under claude -p. In relay/agent-004.jsonl it wrote `[values.large] true = "Yes" / false = "No"` and ran a full export with no error or warning. It then rewrote the keys as `"True"`/`"False"` and noted "silently didn't map. No warning."
- The text `True` comes from the release itself. The investigation template shipped with awb-init saves result tables with pandas `frame.to_csv`, and pandas writes booleans as `True`/`False`.
- In TOML, a bare key `true` is the lowercase string "true". `_display_cell` looks labels up by exact match (`if text in labels`), so the key never matches.
- `_shape` and `export` never report a value key that matches no cell. `@where` treats a value no row holds as an error, so the gap is inconsistent within the same command.
- None of the documentation (helpers.md:45, the export help text, the glossary template) says value keys must match the saved CSV text exactly, case included.
- The sandbox, auto-approved tools, simulated home folder, relay and persona played no part. Any agent writing display.toml for a pandas boolean column on any host would get the same silent miss.

**Label warnings (taxi-A):**
- `label_collisions` recomputes the warning from display.toml and the recorded questions on every full export, with no acknowledged state.
- taxi-A's relay shows the same `source_month`/"Month" entry for five results in agent-006 and agent-007, across exports triggered by normal user revisions such as whole-dollar rounding. A real user's revisions would trigger the same repeats.
- awb-package SKILL.md:68 says to "confirm its name suits every result". After confirming, the warning stays, so the agent has to re-confirm after every export.
- The same "Month" meaning fits all five results here, so the warning is effectively a false positive with no way to dismiss it. That is release design, not harness.

**Where the finding overstates:**
- "Cannot be resolved" goes too far. The warning drops if the column is named under `[results."<id>".columns]` for all but one of the colliding results. The taxi-A agent already used that mechanism for tip-code-sensitivity.
- That workaround means copying the same name into four tables, not marking the warning confirmed. The SKILL's "or name it for one result" does not clear a five-way collision. So the friction is real but small, and the minor severity fits.
verdicts.release_evidence: Boolean keys: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:3104-3107 (`_display_cell`, exact `text in labels` lookup); awb_draft.py:3226-3231 (`used` keeps only matched codes; nothing reports unmatched keys) versus awb_draft.py:3184-3190 (`@where` with a value no row holds is an error); awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/run.py:120 (`frame.to_csv(table, index=False)`, so pandas writes booleans as True/False). Label warnings: awb_draft.py:3251-3265 (`label_collisions`, recomputed and returned on every full export, no acknowledged state); awb_draft.py:3338-3340; awb-package/SKILL.md:68 ("confirm its name suits every result it labels, or name it for one result"). Counterpoint: awb_draft.py:3261 skips any column named under the result's own columns table, so per-result names do silence the warning.

verdicts.reasoning:
Both parts of the finding hold up, and in both the shipped helper and docs cause the behaviour.

Part 1: label warnings cannot be marked confirmed.
- label_collisions (awb_draft.py:3251-3265) runs on every full export. It skips a result only when that result names the column under its own [results."<id>".columns] table. It warns whenever the results that share a column have more than one distinct recorded question, and separate results almost always do.
- display.toml cannot record an acknowledgement. display_names (awb_draft.py:3013-3016) rejects any key outside the five allowed tables, so there is nowhere to write "confirmed".
- The skill and the warning offer two ways out: "confirm it fits each, or name the column for one result" (_COLLISION at awb_draft.py:2969-2970, SKILL.md:68). Confirming changes nothing, so the warning comes back on the next export. Naming the column for one result does not clear it either when three or more results share the name: the rest still have different questions. In taxi-A five results share it.
- The only way to silence it is to repeat the same name under each result's own columns table (all but one result is enough). Nothing in the release presents that as a way to confirm a shared name.
- Run evidence: taxi-A relay logs agent-006.jsonl and agent-007.jsonl contain the same entry several times: source_month / "Month" across airport-comparison, tipping-patterns, trip-volume, zone-ranking and quality-counts. taxi-A feedback/agent.md item 17 says the agent confirmed the meaning in methodology, but "repeated confirm warnings have no recorded resolved state". Any real user whose charts share a common column (month, country) across results would hit this.

Part 2: boolean value keys silently match nothing.
- The workbench's own run.py template saves results with pandas frame.to_csv (run.py:120), which writes booleans as "True" and "False".
- In TOML, a bare key `true` is the string "true"; parsing `true = "Yes"` gives {'true': 'Yes'}.
- _display_cell (awb_draft.py:3104-3107) needs an exact `text in labels` match. The labels-used collection (awb_draft.py:3224) records only keys that matched, and nothing warns about a key that matched no cell.
- The docs (helpers.md:45, glossary.md:8) describe the values table only as "coded value = label". They never say the key must match the saved text exactly. That rule is stated only for @where row selection.
- Run evidence: co2-B relay agent-004.jsonl line 27 writes `[values.large] true = "Yes" / false = "No"`. The export at line 31 succeeded with no warning, and the dataset file still showed True (line 36). The agent found this only by reading the output, then changed the keys to "True" and "False" (line 40). co2-B feedback/agent.md item 10 and agent-notes.md line 43 confirm it.

Severity minor is right for both: they add noise and need manual output checks, but they do not corrupt anything. The release, not the harness, causes both.
verdicts.release_evidence: Part 1: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:3251-3265 (label_collisions skips only results that name the column themselves; no acknowledgement state); awb_draft.py:2969-2970 (the "confirm it fits each, or name the column for one result" warning text); awb_draft.py:3013-3016 (display.toml rejects any other key, so a confirmation cannot be stored); awb-package/SKILL.md:68 ("For each label_warnings column, confirm its name suits every result it labels, or name it for one result"). Part 2: awb_draft.py:3104-3107 (_display_cell needs an exact `text in labels` match); awb_draft.py:3224 (records only matched labels; no warning for an unmatched key); awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/run.py:120 (frame.to_csv writes pandas booleans as True/False); awb-package/references/helpers.md:45 (describes values only as "coded value = label", never that keys must match the saved text)

consolidated.title: Releases can ship from uncommitted code, and repairing provenance takes commit, rerun, re-export and commit
consolidated.description: co2-B's release 001 was frozen from a repository with no commits, so producing_commit is 'uncommitted' and the only provenance is file checksums. Results run before the first commit stay 'uncommitted' until they are rerun after a commit. In retail-B, fixing that took a commit, a rerun, a re-export and another commit, and nothing told the agent this was needed. With commits made on request and at most one reminder per session (C-30), this cost is easy to miss.
consolidated.evidence: co2-B-11: released/001/manifest.json; no commits in the project git log. retail-B-21: A6 commits 6fb0cc2 and c18e2e7.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none.

co2-B:
- The project has no commits.
- Release 001's manifest records producing_commit "uncommitted" and packaging_commit {"unknown": "the checkout has no commit yet"}.
- Nothing in the harness stopped the agent from committing:
  - The appended system prompt (prompts/claude-agent-system.md) sets no git limits.
  - agent-home/.gitconfig holds a git identity.
  - git commands were allowed.
- The release's own defaults are the cause:
  - awb-init creates a repository "with no commit or remote".
  - The project README template sets "Commits: on request", and AGENTS.md says to commit only when asked.
  - awb-package's export step says "Commit nothing on the user's behalf to make provenance look clean."
  - awb-release still releases without a commit.
- The agent suggested a commit several times (transcript lines 157, 187, 353, 578). The Codex user never asked for one; its notes call the suggestion optional. That is ordinary user behavior and the README allows it, not a role or relay artifact. A real user who never says "commit" ends up in the same state on any host.

retail-B:
- The persona allowed commits in message 6. The agent then committed 6fb0cc2 and edited two results.
- It committed again (c18e2e7) and reran all eight results so their evidence would record that commit. Six of the eight had unchanged tables and were rerun only for provenance.
- It re-exported, then made a third commit (c1e1393, "Record result evidence produced at c18e2e7") because the rerun had changed the evidence files.
- The agent's notes and feedback (agent.md §1.4) say nothing warned it; it noticed only from the manifest.

The release code shows why nothing warns:
- awb_provenance.py writes producing_commit "uncommitted" when there is no HEAD, and records the commit plus file checksums when there are uncommitted changes. That value is only replaced by a rerun.
- collect_status.py reports only has_commits and uncommitted_paths. Once everything is committed, status shows a clean tree even though the evidence still says "uncommitted".
- awb_draft.provenance_gaps flags only {"unknown": ...} objects, so the string "uncommitted" never appears as a gap at release.
- export prints producing_commit but never says to rerun after committing.

Harness quirks I found, none of which caused the finding:
- The retail-B agent set commit authorship with git -c, using the real user's identity. This affected only the author field.
- The persona volunteered the commit permission. This only triggered the commit chain; it did not cause it.

One small correction: the finding cites "retail-B-21", but the matching finding is retail-B-16. The evidence it gives (commits 6fb0cc2 and c18e2e7) is correct. Minor severity fits.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/SKILL.md:16 (initialize a local repository "with no commit or remote"); awb-init/assets/workbench/README.md:13 ("Commits: on request") and :56; awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:48 (commit only when asked, suggest at most once a session); awb-package/SKILL.md:68 ("Commit nothing on the user's behalf to make provenance look clean"); awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py:779-781 (producing_commit "uncommitted" plus file checksums when there is no HEAD, fixed in the evidence until a rerun); awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py:847-849 (reports only has_commits and uncommitted_paths, nothing about evidence recorded before a commit); awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:3955-3980 (provenance_gaps flags only {"unknown": ...} values, so "uncommitted" is never reported); awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:3417-3420 (export prints producing_commit with no rerun advice)

verdicts.reasoning:
The core mechanism is real and comes from the release. Two parts of the finding overreach.

What the evidence shows:
- co2-B: the project has no commits ("does not have any commits yet"). released/001/manifest.json records producing_commit "uncommitted", per-file sha256 values in producing_uncommitted_changes, and packaging_commit {"unknown": "the checkout has no commit yet"}.
- retail-B: the history matches the claimed repair: 6fb0cc2, then code commit c18e2e7, then "Record result evidence produced at c18e2e7" (c1e1393). The agent's notes say it reran unchanged results ("kept supported") and re-exported to get a SHA, and that it noticed "only from manifest producing_commit".

The release causes this and does not prevent it:
- awb_provenance.py:779 fixes producing_commit as "uncommitted" when the result is produced.
- compare_evidence (awb_provenance.py:861, 941) checks such evidence by checksum only. Once the code is committed it still counts as current, so `stale` never asks for a rerun.
- awb-status/collect_status.py:847-849 reports only uncommitted paths and has_commits. It never says which results were produced before any commit.
- No skill, reference or README says that committing alone leaves earlier results "uncommitted", or that the fix is commit, then rerun, then re-export.
- With the default "Commits: on request" (AGENTS.md:48, README.md:56), a real user who commits only before release will hit this.
- The gap also misleads the agent: in co2-B it offered "commit the current work" to save the analysis as a version before release. Under this tooling that would not have changed the manifest without a rerun.

Where the finding overreaches:
1. "Releases can ship from uncommitted code" is documented behavior, not a defect. manifest-template.md:16 allows producing_commit `uncommitted` with recorded checksums. In co2-B the user was told at A2, A3, A4 and A8 and went ahead.
2. The "easy to miss" point, tied to the one-reminder limit (C-30), is contradicted. Both runs repeated the reminder, and both simulated users complained it was too frequent.
3. In retail-B, much of the rerun and re-export was needed anyway for the user's requested changes (new reconciliation and identified-contributor checks, renamed Chart 6 columns). The extra cost that comes from provenance alone is putting the rerun after the commit, plus one evidence commit.

The real defect is narrower: the commit-then-rerun step is undocumented and nothing reports it. Minor severity is right.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py:779 (producing_commit "uncommitted" fixed when the result is produced); awb_provenance.py:861 and :941 (uncommitted evidence compared by checksum only, so it stays current after a commit and nothing asks for a rerun); awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py:847-849 (reports uncommitted paths only, not results produced before any commit); no commit-then-rerun guidance in awb-release/SKILL.md, awb-package/SKILL.md, awb-init/references/provenance.md or workbench/AGENTS.md:48. Against the finding: awb-package/assets/package-format/manifest-template.md:16 explicitly allows producing_commit `uncommitted` with checksums, so co2-B's release from uncommitted code is documented behavior.

consolidated.title: Headline previews need substantial user correction
consolidated.description: First previews had several kinds of gap. Answer headlines did not state the answer. Slides described one country instead of the top-ten groups. A denominator counted countries without data (27 of 45 instead of 27 of 39). A subtitle period did not cover the 1850 analysis. One slide named 2 of 4 entities, and the coal slide lacked its threshold and its definition of 'fastest'. In co2-A the user rewrote five headlines. check-draft cannot detect a headline that does not answer its question, and the 15-word cap squeezes executive answers.
consolidated.evidence: co2-A-15: A2 headlines 2-4; U3. co2-B-35: A3; U4.

verdicts.reasoning:
I found no harness cause. The relay passed the headlines through unchanged: co2-A relay/agent-002.out.md and agent-002.jsonl match the transcript, and the co2-B agent-003.out.md lines match too. Headline wording does not depend on the sandbox, the auto-approved tools, the simulated home folder or non-interactive mode. The same Codex or Claude agent would draft the same previews for a real user. The persona briefs never mention headlines. The co2-B front-loading (co2-B-29) only touched the scoping facts. On the release side, the agent's own notes link the co2-A Answer squeeze to a release rule. Its A2 notes say "All main headlines are at most 15 words". Its A3 notes say slashes were used "to fit all three requested evidence clauses into one sentence within the 15-word package rule". In A5 it said the user's 21-word headline "exceeds the template's word limit". The template's one-key-number-per-headline rule plausibly also pushed slides 3 and 4 to name only China and the US for top-ten questions. A real user on an interactive host would get these same previews. So a narrower version of the finding is a product issue.

The finding overstates the problem, though:
1. co2-A original slide 6 already named all four entities in both directions ("raises US and EU-27... lowers China's and India's"). The user's own U3 edit caused that wording to be dropped, and U4 had to restore it. That is persona churn, not a gap in the preview.
2. co2-A original slide 5 ("45 of 164 countries cut...") already stated an answer with a number. Naming the US, Japan and Germany was a preference.
3. co2-B's Answer headline did state an answer ("China and India added the most CO2...; 45 countries cut emissions while growing").
4. The preview shows only headlines. The co2-B "2 of 4 entities" and "coal slide lacked threshold/definition" points are about slide bodies the user never saw. The co2-B persona says so itself: "The initial headline alone would not have covered all four, but the draft did."
5. The co2-B "27 of 45" headline already said "6 lack data". Changing the denominator was a framing preference, not a miscount.

Both personas said the preview checkpoint worked or was useful. Neither listed headline correction as a pain point beyond the word cap. What holds up:
- The co2-A Answer headline was vague and squeezed by the 15-word cap.
- co2-A slides 3 and 4 named one country for top-ten questions.
- The co2-B subtitle period did not cover the 1850 analysis.
- Nothing checks whether a headline answers its question before the preview. check-draft and the reviewer run only on the full draft.

The 15-word-cap part duplicates co2-A-01 (major).
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:14 sets a hard cap: one sentence, at most 15 words, stating the slide's point "with its key number". findings-template.md:36 says the Answer headline is "<the answer to the question, with its key number>". awb-package/references/helpers.md:28 shows the outline check enforces only the word count (over 15 words fails), with no semantic check. awb-package/SKILL.md:47 says preview-and-wait shows the headlines with no review pass. The reviewer in references/review.md:22 runs only on the full narratives.

verdicts.reasoning:
The cited turns do show users editing headlines. In co2-A U3, the user asked for changes to slides 2 to 6. The second clause of the Answer headline was vague ("other measures reveal different country priorities"). Slides 3 and 4 were framed on China and the US instead of the top-ten groups, slide 5 did not name the US, Japan and Germany, and slide 6 had no numbers. In co2-B U4, the user asked for "27 of 39 with consumption data" instead of "27 of those 45; 12 did not, 6 lack data", all four per-person comparisons on slide 6, the 50 Mt threshold and the definition of "fastest" on slide 8, and a subtitle that also covers the 1850 analysis.

The release does not cause these edits, and part of it already guards against them:
- findings-template.md:14 says a headline is "one sentence... stating its point with its key number, never a topic label".
- findings-template.md:36 says the Answer headline is "the answer to the question, with its key number". The vague Answer clause is the agent falling short of that instruction.
- findings-template.md:11 says the subtitle names "audience, population, and period". Leaving out 1850 was an agent oversight.
- The other edits are editorial preferences: group framing instead of the top country, and a preferred denominator, although the agent's 45-based wording was complete and accurate. Some were requests for slide content (thresholds, all four entities) that a headline-only preview, as designed, leaves to the user.

SKILL.md:47 and README.md:66-68 set up preview-and-wait so the user can review the headlines before the full slides. Users correcting headlines there is that step working, and each correction was settled in one turn. The users said as much:
- co2-A feedback: "The headline checkpoint (preview-and-wait) worked as the README described."
- co2-B feedback: "The headline preview was useful". The co2-B user lists no headline problem among their pain points.

"check-draft cannot detect a headline that does not answer its question" is true but no defect. awb_draft.py:2015-2020 checks only that a headline is not empty and has at most 15 words. check-draft does not run at the preview stage, and no word-count check could catch that kind of failure. The release makes the user that check at the checkpoint, and the reviewer subagent on the full draft.

The one part that holds is that the 15-word cap squeezes executive answers. It plausibly made the first co2-A Answer headline vaguer (13 words covering three points). It also forced the trims in co2-A A4 and co2-B A5. That is already a separate finding, co2-A-01 (major, product), and it shows up after the first preview, not in it.

The cited IDs do not match the run files. "co2-A-15" in co2-A/feedback/findings.json is a README finding, and "co2-B-35" does not exist (that file has 31 entries). The turn citations do check out in the transcripts.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:14 (headline must state its point with its key number, never a topic label, at most 15 words) and :36 (Answer headline = the answer with its key number), which already instruct against the vague Answer clause. findings-template.md:11 (subtitle names the period). awb-package/SKILL.md:47 and README.md:66-68 (preview-and-wait is the designed approve/reorder step). awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:1772 HEADLINE_WORDS = 15 and :2015-2020 (check-draft checks only empty or over-15-word headlines). The cap part duplicates co2-A-01.

consolidated.title: awb-scope's four-decision cap forces unrelated choices into one question
consolidated.description: awb-scope allows at most four decisions per round, so agents bundled unrelated method choices into one question: the global total, EU-27 history and the definition of 'fastest' in co2-B; three revenue thresholds in retail-B. That bundle left 'full two years' ambiguous against the incomplete December 2011. Users still followed it. Oct 15 retail-B said the same cap cost a round.
consolidated.oct15_ref: Oct 15 per-run retail-B agent.md (interview batching against a deadline); fix-plan 8
consolidated.evidence: co2-B-36: awb-scope SKILL:25; A1 question 4. retail-B-16: A1 decision 4; agent-notes turn 1.

verdicts.reasoning:
The core claim holds up and I found no harness cause. Two parts of the finding go further than the evidence, covered at the end.

What the runs show:
- **co2-B, first agent reply:** the agent asked four numbered questions. Item 4 put three separate definitions under one heading: the Q4 global total, EU-27 history, and Q5 "fastest". Item 2 also packed several choices together: the end years for Q1, Q2 and Q5, plus the rule for which countries count in Q2.
- **retail-B, first agent reply:** item 4, "The cut-offs", put thresholds for Q2, Q4 and Q5 into one question.
- **Both agents blamed the skill at the time.** Each wrote in its first-turn friction log that awb-scope's "at most four" rule made it bundle:
  - co2-B: "had to squeeze into 4 bundled questions"
  - retail-B: "forced bundling five questions' definitional choices"
- **Both simulated users noticed the bundling.** In co2-B the user said the bundled choices "remained understandable".

Harness checks:
- **Sandbox, auto-approved MCP tools, home folder, relay:** none of these affect how many decisions the agent puts in a scoping message. Both messages are the agent's first reply, written before the simulated user had answered anything.
- **Non-interactive `claude -p`:** the agent had no AskUserQuestion tool. That tool is also limited to four questions per call. And `awb-init` step 4 says to put the first scoping round in the setup report as text, so a normal interactive host would see the same pressure. The skills also target Codex and Copilot, which ask in text.
- **Personas front-loading:** both users gave five questions and their storage folders in the first message. The product README tells real users to do exactly that ("The more you put in the first message, the fewer questions follow"), so this is realistic, not an artifact.
- **The model choosing to bundle instead of asking a second round:** this is partly model behaviour. But the release text pushes it that way:
  - SKILL.md:25 sets the cap of four and says nothing about what to do when more than four decisions are at the same level.
  - SKILL.md:42 says to ask every open decision before writing the records, with no separate confirmation round.
  - awb-init/SKILL.md:46 puts the first round in the setup report, and that report is limited to five items (line 50).

  A real user running the same model would get the same result.

Where the finding goes too far:
1. **The "full two years" ambiguity was not caused by bundling.** It came from the agent's wording. The retail-B user's own notes ("'full two years' is ambiguous given incomplete December 2011") and feedback ("also left...") list it as a separate problem.
2. **"Users still followed it" is only partly true.** The retail-B user corrected two of the bundled choices: one 24-month window for every analysis, and small or new markets shown separately instead of left out.
3. **The Oct 15 "cost a round" claim** is not in these run folders, so I could not check it.

Harm was minor in both runs. The cap-driven bundling is a real product behaviour, so the verdict is product, but the finding's description should be narrowed.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-scope/SKILL.md:25 ("ask decisions at the same level together, at most four"); awb-scope/SKILL.md:42 (ask every open decision before writing records, no separate confirmation round); awb-init/SKILL.md:46 (first interview round goes in the setup report) and :50 (report limited to five items); README.md:62 ("They come up to four at a time")

verdicts.reasoning:
The release causes the bundling, and the evidence shows it. Part of the finding overreaches.

What the release says. awb-scope/SKILL.md:25 tells the agent to ask same-level decisions together, "at most four", each with a recommendation. SKILL.md:42 adds that the agent must ask every decision the user can answer, method choices included, before it writes any records. When a brief has more than four same-level method choices, these two rules leave two options: spend extra rounds, or nest several decisions under one numbered item. Nothing in the release stops nesting or warns against it, and awb-init:46 puts this first round inside the setup report.

What the runs show:
- **co2-B** (transcript.md:53, item 4 "Q4 and Q5 definitions"): three separate choices sit under one number: the Q4 global denominator, EU-27 history (stated, with no alternative offered) and how to define Q5 "fastest".
- **retail-B** (transcript.md:38-42, item 4 "The cut-offs"): three thresholds for three different questions sit under one number.
- **The agents name the cap as the cause.** co2-B feedback/agent-notes.md:9 says it "had to squeeze into 4 bundled questions". retail-B feedback/agent-notes.md:13 says the cap "forced bundling".
- **Both simulated users noticed.** co2-B human/feedback.md:35 found the bundle understandable. retail-B human.md:38 said "The fourth question bundled several different thresholds."
- **The same pressure shows up elsewhere.** The taxi-B agent (agent-notes.md:10) had to pick which four to ask. The Oct 15 retail-B agent said the cap cost an extra round (docs/ux-simulation-2026-10-15/retail-B/agent.md:23 in commit 842582e). So the cap produces either an extra round or a bundle, and this is not a harness artifact.

Where the finding overreaches:
- **The "full two years" ambiguity is a wording problem, not a bundling one.** The phrase "over the full two years" at retail-B transcript.md:39 would be just as ambiguous if asked alone. The data had not been downloaded yet, and the user fixed it in U2.
- **Harm was low.** Both users answered in one reply with no wrong numbers.
- **The cap is a deliberate trade-off.** The Oct 15 fix plan (fix-plan.md:314) kept it on purpose to stop the first exchange getting too long.
- **The cited evidence IDs are wrong, though the evidence exists.** co2-B's findings.json stops at co2-B-31, so co2-B-36 does not exist. retail-B-16 is about uncommitted provenance, not the cap. The underlying evidence is real anyway: the A1 transcripts, the agent notes and the human feedback.

Conclusion: a real user would get these bundled questions, and the shipped instruction causes them. The finding is real but minor.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-scope/SKILL.md:25 ("ask decisions at the same level together, at most four, each with a recommended answer") together with awb-scope/SKILL.md:42 (ask every user-answerable decision, method choices included, before writing records); awb-init/SKILL.md:46 puts that first round inside the setup report. Agents cite the cap at co2-B/feedback/agent-notes.md:9 and retail-B/feedback/agent-notes.md:13; bundles at co2-B/transcript.md:53 and retail-B/transcript.md:38-42.

consolidated.title: Review independence rests on the brief and the agent's discipline
consolidated.description: In Codex, the read-only reviewer subagent inherits the session's full tools, so review.md's read-only limit rests on the brief alone, as review.md itself says, and the parent has to manage snapshots. In retail-A, the agent edited three passages while a review was running and asked the same reviewer to reread them, blurring the separation between writer and reviewer. retail-A-33 was tagged unclear because it happened once.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-37: review.md 'Launch', Codex branch: 'the brief's instruction alone'. retail-A-33: agent-notes full draft entry.

verdicts.reasoning:
The simulation did not cause this. Both of its claims hold up in the primary sources, and the harness settings had nothing to do with either.

1) Tool inheritance in Codex. The Codex multi-agent developer message in the retail-A parent rollout (agent-home/.codex/sessions/.../rollout-...01a14625...jsonl, line 4) says every agent in the team has "access to the same set of tools" and shares one filesystem. That is how Codex itself works, not something codex exec or the sim config adds. The config uses approval_policy=never with workspace-write. An interactive Codex session in workspace-write would let a subagent write in the workspace just the same. The release's Codex branch says the read-only limit is "the brief's instruction alone" (review.md:11 and :14). So a real Codex user gets exactly this setup.

2) The mid-review edit in retail-A is real and came from the agent, not the harness. In the parent rollout:
- 19:54:51 spawn_agent package_review_final, with fork_turns "all".
- 19:55:29 an exec edits findings.md, methodology-note.md and methodology.md, prints "Clarified independent chart rounding before full review finishes", and overwrites the review-2 snapshot.
- 19:55:33 send_message to the same reviewer.
In the reviewer's rollout (...01a14648...), it read findings.md and methodology.md at 19:55:11–19:55:20, before the edit. After the message it grepped the lines containing "round" and returned "review: clean". No persona, relay or sandbox factor played a part. The model chose to keep editing while it waited on 10-second wait_agent polls, which can happen just the same on an interactive host.

Where the release is the cause:
- review.md asks for "a fresh subagent" (line 7) but gives Codex no way to make one. Codex's default spawn (fork_turns omitted, or "all") copies the writer's full history into the subagent. retail-A spawned all four reviewers with fork_turns "all". taxi-A used "none" every time, and co2-A used both. So whether the reviewer is actually independent comes down to the agent's discretion, which fits the finding.
- The staleness and snapshot rules (review.md:35, :37) do not forbid editing narratives while a review is running, and they do not forbid sending the reviewer new instructions mid-review. The rereading workaround is not sanctioned by the release, but nothing in it rules the workaround out either.

Caveats that keep this minor:
- Codex's tool inheritance is a host limitation, and the release documents it accurately. The fixable parts are the missing rules: no edits during a running review, and a no-history spawn (fork_turns "none") for the reviewer.
- There was no harm to the result. Two later full reviews (release_revision_review, release_001_review) passed before the release was made.
- The snapshot burden in the finding applies on every host (review.md:37), not only in Codex.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/references/review.md:11 (Codex: "the limit to read tools is then the brief's instruction alone"); review.md:14 ("Codex inherits tools, so those limits are conventions"); review.md:7 ("Start a fresh subagent", with no Codex instruction to avoid a full-history fork); review.md:35 and :37 (staleness and snapshot rules do not forbid edits or new instructions while a review is running)

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding's premise is accurate, but no run shows the harm it describes.

1. The premise holds. review.md:11 says Codex subagents "inherit the session's sandbox and tools" and that the read-tools limit is "the brief's instruction alone". review.md:14 says the same again. The reviewer rollouts confirm it: retail-A review 2 (agent-home/.codex/sessions/2026/10/16/rollout-...15-54-51-01a14648...jsonl, line 36) ran under a workspace-write sandbox with the project writable.

2. No reviewer broke the brief. I scanned all eight reviewer rollouts (four in taxi-A, four in retail-A) and found no write operations. They ran only cat, nl, sed, rg, Python reads and awb/read. The one bad call was a read-only CLI command with a wrong `--project` flag, which is a separate finding (retail-A-28). taxi-A-37 is only a quote of the release text and describes no incident.

3. The retail-A episode is a single choice the agent made, not something the release told it to do. It also does not blur who wrote and who reviewed. Relay agent-005.jsonl item 85 shows the writer adding a rounding clarification to findings.md, methodology-note.md and methodology.md while review 2 was running. It updated the snapshot at the same time. Rollout line 105 is the writer's mid-review message to the reviewer. At line 106 the reviewer then re-grepped every 'round' line in all three narratives, and its output contains the new text ('Chart pound values', 'computed before rounding'). The final 'review: clean' therefore covers the edited text. The writer never judged its own draft, and the reviewer never edited.

4. Nothing in the release causes this behaviour. review.md defines the review as a fixed input: a snapshot is copied "for every review awb-package launches" (line 37), and "a stale review is run again" (line 35). The staleness rule is worded "after it", so the release does not explicitly cover edits made during a review. At most that is a small wording gap, and it is not tied to tool inheritance. The parent agent holds its own edit tools on every host, so this has nothing to do with the reviewer inheriting tools.

5. "The parent has to manage snapshots" applies on every host (review.md:37), not just Codex. It is a deliberate design choice, not a failure.

Side observation, not part of C-59 as written: Codex's spawn_agent forks the parent's conversation by default (fork_turns defaults to 'all'). The review-2 reviewer's context carried the writer's earlier user-facing replies (rollout lines 8–25). review.md:7 asks for a "fresh subagent" but never says fork_turns "none" for Codex. That is a separate, real gap in reviewer independence and would need its own finding.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/references/review.md:11 and :14 say Codex reviewer limits rest on the brief and offer the mitigation. review.md:35 and :37 set the snapshot-per-launch and stale-review-is-rerun rules, which the retail-A agent worked around once. None of these causes a mid-review edit. Contradicting run evidence: in retail-A/agent-home/.codex/sessions/2026/10/16/rollout-2026-10-16T15-54-51-01a14648-1459-7b33-ae97-26dcf6ab13e8.jsonl the reviewer re-reads the edited lines after the writer's message (lines 105-106) before giving 'review: clean' (line 123), and none of the eight reviewer rollouts contains a write.

consolidated.title: Skill scaffolding steps produce compound shell commands that need approval
consolidated.description: Following the skills' template-copy steps produced compound Bash commands (cd, cp from the skill folder, sed on README lines, heredoc appends, uv venv). These raised a permission prompt even though Bash was pre-allowed. A host with default permissions, or Copilot, would prompt for many more.
consolidated.evidence: co2-B-26: relay/permission-prompts.jsonl at 19:20:48Z. retail-B-38: permission-prompts.jsonl at 19:19:53Z.

verdicts.reasoning:
Each run logged exactly one permission prompt. Both came from the approver MCP that the harness passed to headless `claude -p` as --permission-prompt-tool. The same launch carried a blanket `--allowedTools Bash` and `--add-dir agent-home` (kit/relay.py:146-153). Under that setup a prompt only appears when one of Claude Code's own command-safety checks fires on a particular command. The evidence ties that to how the model wrote the command and to the harness, not to the release.

1) The release does not prescribe shell commands. awb-init says to "Adapt asset files to the target" (orientation, ignore rules, AGENTS, ledgers). No skill tells the agent to use cp, sed, heredocs or `uv venv`. The work could have been done with the Read and Write file tools. Choosing compound Bash was the model's decision.

2) The harness shaped the commands that prompted. kit/claude-agent-system.md tells the agent to "set HOME={SIMDIR}/agent-home" in shell commands that touch the home folder. It also puts the skills under a long simulation path, so the agent defined path variables to shorten them. The retail-B command that prompted contains `P=<simdir>; A=$P/agent-home/.claude/skills/...; cd $P/project` and `HOME=$P/agent-home uv venv`. Both come straight from the harness instructions. The co2-B command starts with `cd <simdir>/project;` (a redundant cd to the working directory) and copies from `<simdir>/agent-home/.claude/skills/...` by absolute path.

3) The trigger is inconsistent, so it is not a reliable result of the skill steps:
- **retail-B:** a near-identical command ran without a prompt. It was `cp ../agent-home/.../glossary.md foundation/glossary.md && cat >> foundation/glossary.md <<'EOF'` with markdown tables, backticks and non-ASCII characters, and so was `sed ... catalog.md > foundation/catalog.md && cat >> ... <<'EOF'`.
- **co2-B:** `cd <sim>/project; cp <skill>/quality.md foundation/quality.md` and many `cd ...; cat > file <<'EOF'` commands passed.
- **co2-B, closest match:** `B=<sim>; cd $B/project && HOME=$B/agent-home uv pip install ...` passed.
- **taxi-B:** same release, same agent model and the same scaffolding shape (`cd`, path variables, `cp` from the skill folder, `sed > README.md`, `HOME=... uv venv`). The run logged zero prompts and has no permission-prompts.jsonl at all.

Out of dozens of comparable commands per run, one prompted. That points to an edge case in Claude Code's parser, hit by the model's particular phrasing under the harness configuration.

4) The release already expects host approvals. README.md:110-111 says the host may ask the user to approve commands, that this is the host's own prompt, and that registering the awb MCP server reduces approvals.

5) The finding's wider claim, that a host with default permissions or Copilot "would prompt for many more", is an extrapolation. No run tested it. On a default-permission host, prompts for file writes and shell commands are general host behavior that any skill writing files would trigger. They are not a release defect shown by this evidence.

The referee rated both as product only because its playbook counts every logged prompt as product friction (retail-B-30 tag_reason). It did not analyse the cause.

Why confidence is medium: the exact Claude Code heuristic that fired could not be pinned down. A real host might also prompt on a copy from `~/.claude/skills` outside the project, since in the harness the skill folder was an added directory and that case was hidden. Even so, the release is not shown to be the cause.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/SKILL.md:28-30 ("Adapt asset files to the target"; no shell commands prescribed). README.md:110-111 (host approval prompts are the host's own; MCP registration reduces them). In the harness: kit/claude-agent-system.md (tells the agent to set HOME={SIMDIR}/agent-home and puts the skills under the simulation folder), kit/relay.py:146-153 (blanket --allowedTools Bash, --add-dir agent-home, approver as --permission-prompt-tool).

verdicts.reasoning:
The cited prompts are real, but the evidence does not show that the release causes them.

1. What the logs show. Each run logged exactly one prompt in relay/permission-prompts.jsonl.
   - co2-B, 19:20:48Z, turn A2: `cd project; cp <skill>/assets/workbench/foundation/catalog.md foundation/catalog.md; cat >> foundation/catalog.md <<'EOF' ... EOF; tail | cut`.
   - retail-B, 19:19:53Z, turn A1: `P=..; A=$P/agent-home/...; cd $P/project; cp $A/.gitignore $A/AGENTS.md .; sed ... $A/README.md > README.md; HOME=... uv venv`.
   - Those are 2 prompts out of 689 Bash calls in co2-B and 328 in retail-B. taxi-B, the third Claude-agent run on the same release, has no permission-prompts file at all.

2. The prompt does not follow the scaffolding steps. Commands of the same shape ran without a prompt:
   - co2-B turn A1 did the full init the same way (`cd $P; cp` the templates; a python heredoc to edit README; `HOME=... uv venv`; installer) with no prompt.
   - co2-B turn A2 ran `cd project; cat > src/preparation/owid_co2.sql <<'EOF'` and `cd project; echo ... > foundation/views/010_owid_co2.sql` with no prompt.
   - About 30 co2-B and 23 retail-B commands combined `cd` with an output redirect, and only one in each run prompted.
   - So the prompt depends on details of how the agent wrote the command, which set off a narrow Claude Code safety check. It does not come from following the skills' steps.

3. The release does not prescribe this command shape.
   - awb-init/SKILL.md (step 3.1, lines 28-30; step 3.4, line 39) and awb-scope/SKILL.md (line 55) only say to "adapt" or "copy" the templates.
   - The only shell command the init skill gives is `python3 <skill-directory>/scripts/install_helpers.py <project-root>`, which the MCP `setup` tool also wraps.
   - Searching every release file for `cp `, `sed -`, heredoc, `cat >`, `uv venv` and `cd` finds no scaffolding instruction. The only hit is the read-only `sed -n` in awb-package/references/review.md.
   - The `cd`, the variable-expanded paths, `sed` with a redirect, the heredoc appends and the `HOME=` prefix were all the agent's choices. In this harness the agent's Write and Edit tools were pre-allowed and would have done the same work without a prompt.

4. The claim about other hosts is speculation. That a host with default permissions, or Copilot, "would prompt for many more" applies to every terminal command and file write any agent makes, whatever the skill. The release already says so: README.md line 110 says the host may ask for approvals, and line 111 says registering the awb MCP server cuts them down.

The one gap in the release that is real: the MCP `setup` tool refuses a folder without workbench markers (awb_mcp.py lines 191-195), so the agent must create the root files by hand. That is a design gap, not evidence that the steps produce prompting compound shell commands.

The run evidence is co2-B-26 and retail-B-30. retail-B-38, the ID the task cites, is not in retail-B's findings.json, but the 19:19:53Z prompt it points to is the one retail-B-30 describes.
verdicts.release_evidence: none found. Nothing in the release tells the agent to use shell to copy or edit templates. awb-init/SKILL.md:28-30 and :39 and awb-scope/SKILL.md:55 say only to "adapt" or "copy" templates. The only command given is install_helpers.py (awb-init/SKILL.md:34-36). README.md:110-111 already says the host may ask for approvals and that registering the MCP server reduces them. The gap closest to the claim is that awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py:191-195 (setup tool) needs workbench markers that already exist, so the root files are written by hand, but it does not cause compound shell commands.

consolidated.title: Helper output is verbose and easy to misread
consolidated.description: Helper JSON carries long absolute paths and large payloads: a 17,385-token manifest read and a 36,108-token search of the helper truncated output and once hid an installer refusal. An export of results only returns an empty charts list while keeping the existing chart files. co2-A-23 was tagged unclear because the largest outputs came from the agent's own broad cat and rg commands. retail-A-20's point about the helper output format is product.
consolidated.evidence: retail-A-20: A5, A6. co2-A-23: agent-notes init and full-draft entries.

verdicts.reasoning:
The large outputs did not come from the helpers. The cluster cites retail-A-20 and co2-A-23, but those IDs belong to unrelated findings. The findings that actually match are retail-A-24 and co2-A-19.

co2-A, checked in the Codex rollout (agent-home/.codex/sessions/.../rollout-...986f-7ac2-81f3-f0e2a4c27055.jsonl):
(1) The 17,385-token read was the agent's own exec_command `cat .../draft/manifest.json` with max_output_tokens 6000 (rollout line ~848). The "original token count" label is Codex's truncation notice. No awb MCP tool produced it.
(2) The 36,108-token read was the agent's own `rg -n -A 28 -B 3 '...' methodology.md package-contract.md deck-rules.md findings-template.md src/packaging/draft.py` (line ~913). That is a broad search over the 4,190-line helper source. The agent itself calls these "agent query-sizing errors".
(3) The hidden installer refusal (an interpreter mismatch, not an installer bug) happened because the agent packed several calls into one functions.exec Promise.allSettled batch: a 15,000-token `cat` of data.md plus package-contract.md, the install_helpers.py run, an MCP state read and a web fetch (line 45). Codex cut the combined script output from 14,622 tokens down to head and tail, and the installer's message sat in the dropped middle (line 51). A later standalone `--check` showed it plainly. This is Codex exec batching and truncation, not helper output.
Across co2-A, the largest real awb MCP outputs are about 13-14k characters (roughly 3.5k tokens): read/state, which prints brief.md and state.md by design, and read/sql.

retail-A, checked in the relay JSONL for A5 and A6: the largest MCP output is read/state at 14,210 characters, with zero absolute paths. Absolute paths appear in only about 11 small outputs (setup, retain, status, release), one to three each. They look long only because the simulation's project root is a ~150-character scratchpad path (<scratch>). A normal user's root such as ~/work/retail would be short. The agent's in-session notes never mention verbosity; it shows up only in the requested retrospective.

The result-only export returning `"charts": []` while leaving the chart files in place is real release behavior, and it is documented. The awb_draft.py export help says that with only --result it "records provenance and leaves exported files untouched", and package-contract.md:70 says the same; `report["charts"]` lists only files written in that call. The agent read `help export` and interpreted the result correctly during the session (agent-notes line 85: "refreshed provenance while retaining charts"). So nothing shows it was actually misread.

What remains on the product side is a cosmetic report-field naming nit and a 70KB manifest. The release asks agents to hand-edit two of the manifest's fields (allowed_numbers, presentation_order), but it never asks them to read the whole file. Neither caused harm in these runs.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:3438-3440 (export help: with only --result it records provenance and leaves exported files untouched) and :3371 (report charts lists only files written in this call); awb-package/references/package-contract.md:70 (same behavior documented). Contradicting the "verbose helper" claim: co2-A Codex rollout line ~848 (the agent's own `cat manifest.json`, max_output_tokens 6000, "original token count: 17385"), line ~913 (the agent's own `rg -A 28 -B 3` over draft.py, 36108 tokens), lines 45/51 (batched exec output truncated, which hid the install_helpers interpreter refusal). retail-A relay agent-005/006: largest MCP output 14,210 characters, 0 absolute paths.

verdicts.reasoning:
Note on IDs: the finding cites retail-A-20 and co2-A-23, but those IDs are about the README and init ordering. The findings it actually describes are retail-A-24 and co2-A-19. I checked the logs for both runs.

1) Large payloads and truncation (co2-A). The 17,385-token read was the agent running `cat deliveries/.../draft/manifest.json` itself (A4, 69,537 characters). The 36,108-token result was the agent's own `rg -n -A 28 -B 3` across five files, including the 4,190-line draft.py (A5, 144,351 characters). Neither was helper output. No awb MCP result in either run was very large. The biggest was about 14k characters in co2-A (read sql, read state at about 13k) and 8.3k in retail-A (status).

2) The "hidden installer refusal" (co2-A A1). The installer printed 570 characters of JSON with a clear "error" field and exited 1 (item_12). It ran in the same parallel batch as the agent's 25k-character `cat` of data.md and package-contract.md. Codex truncated the combined batch result, and a later `--check` showed the refusal. The agent itself calls these "agent query-sizing errors amplified by verbose provenance, not silent data loss" (co2-A/feedback/agent.md line 97).

3) "Long absolute paths". The helpers write relative paths through `_rel` (awb_draft.py:70). Export output shows `charts/chart-1.csv`, `package-format/...` and so on. Absolute paths appear only where expected: the project root in setup, storage roots in retain, status and release, one or two per result. They look long only because the simulation's scratchpad path is deep, which is a harness artifact.

4) Result-only export returns `"charts": []`. This one is real. awb_draft.py:3281 starts the report with an empty charts list, and the list is filled (line 3371) only on a full export. It is documented, though: the help text says "With only --result it records provenance and leaves exported files untouched" (awb_draft.py:3439-3440), and package-contract.md:70 says the same. In retail-A A5 and A6 the agent read it correctly: agent-notes line 99 says "Result-only package export preserved existing five chart exports". Nothing was misread. It is also an agent-facing JSON field, not something the user sees.

Partial product kernel: the manifest is about 70KB of helper-written provenance (analytical_settings about 16k characters, producing_uncommitted_changes about 10.7k, export_checks about 8.5k). awb-package/SKILL.md lines 32-33 tell the agent to read the existing manifest, and there is no field-level manifest read. The 17k-token read still came from the agent choosing to cat the whole file.

In short, the cited evidence does not show helper output causing truncation or misreading. The truncation came from the agent's own broad commands and batching. The one product-caused quirk is documented and was handled correctly, so the finding as stated is not supported.
verdicts.release_evidence: The empty charts list is real but documented: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:3281 starts the report with `"charts": []` and fills it at :3371 only on a full export; :3439-3440 (help text) and awb-package/references/package-contract.md:70 say a --result-only export leaves the files untouched. Paths are relative via _rel (awb_draft.py:70). The large manifest comes from export provenance, and awb-package/SKILL.md:32-33 says to read the manifest. The 17k and 36k-token outputs were the agent's own `cat manifest.json` (co2-A relay/agent-004.jsonl) and broad `rg` (agent-005.jsonl). The installer refusal was a 570-character JSON error (agent-001.jsonl item_12) truncated in a batch with a 25k-character cat (item_11).

consolidated.title: Project records drift from what was released or decided
consolidated.description: No step brings corrected claims back into the investigation records. taxi-B's findings still say each month 'includes one holiday', 'Monday to Wednesday', and that rc99 trips 'all record zero tips', while the release says MLK Day and 'almost all'. Scaffold guidance text stays in the live state.md. A README line the agent wrote ('No release is authorized') went stale and had to be fixed by hand at release. retail-A-35 was tagged unclear because the agent wrote that text itself.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-12: findings.json lines 66 and 131; state.md lines 13 and 17; history.md line 177. retail-A-22: state.md lines 22-37 match the template. retail-A-35: A7.

verdicts.reasoning:
The main claim holds up, and I could not tie it to anything in how the simulation was run.

1. **taxi-B finding text drift is real.** The investigation's findings.json (lines 66 and 131), rendered into state.md (rows 13 and 17), still says each month "includes one holiday", that July was higher "Monday to Wednesday", and that rc99 trips "all record zero tips". Unresolved-issues line 36 also still says "all record zero tips". Release 001 (findings.md:21, :32, :118) says Sunday to Wednesday, adds MLK Day, and says "almost all".
2. **The corrections came from the release's own process, not the harness.** The awb-package draft reviewer caught them (transcript lines 387 and 430-431; history.md:177). The persona's wrong calendar objection (taxi-B-33) did not cause them.
3. **The agent followed the release's instruction, and that instruction is the gap.** It recorded the MLK fact in history.md, which is all awb-package/SKILL.md:64 asks for ("record them in the investigation's history.md"). It even ran `state finding` to change the tips-by-borough caveat cell from "all" to "almost all", but left the finding text unchanged.
4. **Nothing in the release reconciles finding text with corrected package claims.** No step tells the agent to correct a recorded finding with `state finding --text` when review shows the record is wrong. review.md:22 compares findings.md only with methodology.md. check-draft compares numbers, not wording, with the record.
5. **This matters for a real user.** A later bounded revision reads "current findings ... in state.md" (SKILL.md:33), so the stale wording can come back into a future draft.
6. **No harness factor explains it.** Headless `claude -p`, auto-approved permissions, the simulated home and persona front-loading play no part. The harness note sets no limit on maintaining records.

The two smaller sub-claims are weaker:

- **Scaffold guidance in state.md is caused by the release, not the harness.** The template's guidance prose (state.md template lines 10-22) is kept by the release's own list writer (`edit_list` docstring: "Only list-item lines change"). It shows up in both the Claude-agent run (taxi-B) and the Codex-agent run (retail-A). It may be intended as standing guidance, though, so it is cosmetic at most.
- **The retail-A README line is agent-authored and does not count as product evidence.** The agent itself wrote the "No release is authorized" line in a README section of its own making (agent-002 log). No release template or instruction prompts it, and the agent fixed it itself at release.

Net: product, minor. Confidence is medium rather than high because part of the drift is the agent's partial use of `state finding`, and two of the four examples are weak.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/SKILL.md:64 (the only record step is adding new facts to history.md; nothing corrects recorded finding text); awb-package/references/review.md:22 (review checks findings.md against methodology.md, not state.md/findings.json); awb-package/SKILL.md:33 (a later revision reads current findings in state.md, so stale text can come back); awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py:1794-1800 (edit_list: "Only list-item lines change", which keeps template guidance); awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/state.md:10-22 (the guidance prose). Contradicting the README sub-claim: awb-init/assets/workbench/README.md has no investigation-status section; the agent wrote that text (retail-A relay/agent-002.jsonl).

verdicts.reasoning:
The main claim holds, and the release causes it. Two of the three retail-A pieces do not.

The cited IDs are off. The taxi-B issue is taxi-B-05 in that run's findings.json, and the retail-A issue is retail-A-26. No retail-A-35 exists among that run's 32 findings. The cited file lines are right.

What the taxi-B evidence shows:
- investigations/airport-trips-and-tipping/findings.json:66 still says July was higher "on Monday to Wednesday" and that "each includes one holiday (New Year's Day, Independence Day)". In the result table Sunday was also higher in July (81,564 to 85,104), and January 2024 also had MLK Day.
- findings.json:131 still says rate code 99 trips "all record zero tips".
- state.md:13 and state.md:17 render these stale texts. The Unresolved issues item at state.md:36 still says "all record zero tips".
- The released findings.md says "Sunday to Wednesday", names MLK Day and says "almost all".

The agent did some record upkeep. It wrote the MLK correction to history.md (line 177). In agent-005 it ran `state finding tips-by-borough --caveat ... --reason "'all' corrected to 'almost all'"`, which changed only the caveat. It never used `--text`, so the finding wording stayed wrong.

Why the release is the cause:
- awb-package/SKILL.md:64 sends facts a revision adds only to history.md, "so no narrative states more than the records". No step covers the reverse case, where records still state a claim that review corrected in the package.
- review.md:22 and package-contract.md:48 check the narratives against each other, and numbers against results. Nothing compares package claims with the state.md finding text.
- awb-release adds no record-maintenance step.
- AGENTS.md:46 says how to reword a finding but never says when review corrections require it. No clear instruction was ignored.

This matters to a real user: awb-package:33 starts later revisions from "current findings and flags in state.md". The wrong wording can come back in a later revision, and status keeps showing it.

Retail-A pieces that do not hold:
- The stale "No release is authorized" line is in a README section the agent wrote itself (relay/agent-002.jsonl, replacing its own "Pending scope handoff" block). The README template has no such text. The agent also fixed it itself at release, not the user.
- The guidance text left in state.md (retail-A state.md lines 22-37) is there by design, not drift. edit_list only adds or drops list items. CHANGELOG.md:104 removed sentences from AGENTS.md because the state template states them.

So the verdict rests on taxi-B alone.
verdicts.release_evidence: Causes it: awb-package/SKILL.md:64 sends facts a revision adds only to history.md, and nothing covers stale claims already in the records. awb-package/references/review.md:22 and awb-package/references/package-contract.md:48 compare narratives with each other and numbers with results, never with the state.md finding text. awb-release/SKILL.md has no step that brings corrections back into the records. Contradicts the retail-A pieces: awb-init/assets/workbench/README.md:1-58 has no release-authorization line (the agent wrote it in retail-A relay/agent-002.jsonl). awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/state.md:10-22 keeps its guidance by design: awb_provenance.py:1794 edit_list changes only list items, and CHANGELOG.md:104 relies on the template stating it.

consolidated.title: Scoping interviews missed a question the persona then volunteered
consolidated.description: The interview did not ask what 'countries' means (sovereign countries versus aggregates and the EU-27 bloc) or how to treat non-product stock codes. The personas volunteered both, so these runs cannot show whether the agent would have raised them later.
consolidated.evidence: co2-A-29: A1; U2 'countries means...'. retail-A-26: U2 'One thing you didn't ask about'.

verdicts.reasoning:
The omission itself is real and the harness did not cause it. In co2-A reply 1, Codex asked four scope questions (program focus, measures, comparison years, donor files) and said "Four choices will finish scoping." None of them asked what "countries" means. In retail-A reply 1, Codex asked four questions and none covered non-product stock codes. The harness note added to message 1 only asks for a friction log, and non-interactive codex exec did not stop the agent from asking questions. So the miss is not a sandbox, relay or MCP artifact.

The finding still does not show a release defect that a real user would hit:

1. **The personas front-loaded the answers.** Both briefs list these facts under "Things you can tell the agent if it asks" (co2-A BRIEF line 19; retail-A BRIEF line 18). The co2-A persona's notes show a deliberate choice: "Not yet: whether 'countries' excludes aggregates wasn't asked; I'll say it." Because the personas volunteered, the runs cannot show what would have happened next, as the finding itself admits. Whether the agent would have raised the point later, or chosen a sensible definition and disclosed it, is unobserved.

2. **The release already tells the agent to probe this.** awb-scope/SKILL.md line 31 says to dig into "the definition of the measure and of each population term, tested ... against source data." Lines 23 and 42 also require covering the population and asking every open decision before writing records. The release has the instruction; the gap is the Codex model not applying it in one round.

3. **Other runs on the same release handle it.**
   - retail-B (Claude as agent) asked about non-product lines (bank charges, Amazon fees, manual adjustments) in its first scope round.
   - co2-B (Claude agent, a Codex persona that did not volunteer) also skipped the countries definition in scope. Its awb-clean step then flagged countries versus aggregates and told the user it set countries to mean "the 219 entities with a code, plus Kosovo." So the release's later stages caught it unprompted.

4. **The retail case is partly by design.** In retail-A, the scope interview ran before any data was landed; the agent had read only the UCI page, which does not describe the non-product codes. awb-init's data guide (workbench-guides/data.md:43) puts exclusions in preparation and exploration, after scope. The original findings.json already tagged retail-A's version "unclear" for this reason.

The run evidence shows one model's interview skipping a question in its first round. It does not show a user-facing consequence, and the release text does not cause the miss. Any real-user impact is hidden by the personas front-loading the answers.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-scope/SKILL.md:31 (requires "the definition of the measure and of each population term"), awb-scope/SKILL.md:23 and :42 (cover the population; ask every open decision before writing records). These contradict a missing instruction. awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/data.md:43 puts exclusions in preparation and EDA, after scope. Cross-run on the same release: retail-B reply 1 asked about non-product lines; co2-B reply 2 settled the countries-versus-aggregates definition in awb-clean without being asked.

verdicts.reasoning:
The transcripts back up what the finding observed. In co2-A, the agent's first round (A1) asked four questions: program focus, measures, comparison years, and donor files. None asked what "countries" means. The persona then volunteered "'countries' means sovereign countries and territories, not regions or income groups... Treat the EU-27 as one bloc only where a question names it" (U2). In retail-A, A1 asked about success criteria, customer and repeat-purchase definitions, the product threshold, and the market ranking. The persona's U2 opens "One thing you didn't ask about: some stock codes aren't products...". The cited IDs do not match the run files, though. co2-A/feedback/findings.json has only 28 entries, so there is no co2-A-29, and retail-A-26 there is about stale lifecycle text. The A1/U2 transcript references are correct.

The release does not cause the miss. It tells the agent to do the opposite. awb-scope/SKILL.md:31 tells the interviewer to push on "the definition of the measure and of each population term, tested with a concrete example". "Countries" and "products" are exactly such terms. Line 27 adds "Leave no answer recorded in a form two analysts could read differently". The cap of four questions per round at line 25 does not force the omission. Both agents spent a slot on lower-value items: donor files in co2-A, and in retail-A a product-threshold question where "what counts as a product" fit naturally. Multiple rounds are allowed.

The B runs use the same release with a different agent, and they show the release surfaces both issues:
- **retail-B (A1):** the agent raised non-product lines on its own in the first interview round, recommending excluding "bank charges, Amazon fees, manual adjustments and bad-debt write-offs".
- **co2-B:** the persona never volunteered the countries definition. The release's clean and explore steps caught it anyway. co2-B/project/foundation/quality.md DQ-004 records that OWID mixes countries with aggregates, the EU-27 and World, and that Kosovo has no ISO code. The agent added an is_country flag and reported its definition to the user.

So the finding's open question, whether the agent would have raised these later, is answered for this release: yes, it would. The two misses come from one agent's first-round choices against a clear instruction, once per run, not from anything in the shipped files. The persona front-loading the answer is a study-design limit, and no real user harm is shown.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-scope/SKILL.md:31 ("the definition of the measure and of each population term, tested with a concrete example and against source data...") and :27 ("Leave no answer recorded in a form two analysts could read differently") instruct the interviewer to raise these definitions, so the release prevents this rather than causing it. Same-release counterevidence: retail-B transcript A1 asks about non-trading lines unprompted; co2-B/project/foundation/quality.md DQ-004 catches countries vs aggregates through awb-clean without the persona volunteering it.

consolidated.title: File links switch between absolute and project-relative paths
consolidated.description: Within a session, replies switched from absolute to project-relative file links, which may not open as links for the user. AGENTS.md says only 'giving file paths'.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-31: absolute paths at transcript lines 51-223, relative at 260-334. co2-A-17: relative links in A4.

verdicts.reasoning:
The switch did happen: taxi-A replies 6-7 and co2-A reply 4 used links like `deliveries/.../draft/findings.md`, while the other replies used absolute targets. The relay copies Codex agent_message text verbatim (kit/relay.py _codex_reply), so the harness did not rewrite anything. Even so, the evidence does not show that the release causes this, or that users are harmed by it.

1. The host already sets the rule. The Codex rollout's base_instructions (agent-home/.codex/sessions/.../rollout-...01a14625...jsonl, session_meta) say clickable file links should use a "plain label, absolute target". The release's AGENTS.md line 28 ("Answer in chat, giving file paths") does not contradict that. The relative links break the host's own formatting rule, not a gap left by the release.

2. Release priming is not the cause. In taxi-A turn 6 and co2-A turn 4, the check-draft helper returned a project-relative `"draft": "deliveries/..."`, and awb-package SKILL.md:91 asks the agent to report "the draft path", so priming is a possible contributor. But retail-A, the third Codex run, rules it out as the driver. Its reply 5 got the same relative check-draft output three times and still used absolute links. Its replies 1 and 4 used relative links (`README.md`, `../agent-home/.agents/skills/awb-init/SKILL.md`) with no helper involved at all.

3. The pattern follows the Codex model. All three Codex-agent runs mix the two styles, at different steps. The Claude-agent runs (taxi-B, co2-B, retail-B) consistently use project-relative paths in backticks. This is the Codex model drifting from its host instruction, not something the skills produce.

4. The harm is untested. Codex's cwd was the project root (session_meta cwd), so the relative targets are workspace-relative. No one tried to open a link. The simulated humans read the files directly and called it a "minor inconsistency" (taxi-A notes turn 7) and "fine in an IDE, awkward in a terminal" (co2-A notes turn 4).

The harness did not cause it either.
