The one weak spot is the MCP `setup` tool's description (awb_mcp.py:191-196). It does not say that Python packages are left uninstalled, and its phrase "package formats" could be confused with Python packages. Even so, none of the five other runs had trouble with the same output. taxi-A, co2-A, co2-B, retail-A and retail-B all got `packages: missing` after the real install, ran the command, and noted no confusion. So 1 of 6 agents misread it, and that one acted correctly anyway.

Citation error: the finding cites taxi-B-32, which in findings.json is an unrelated harness finding about the persona giving facts up front. The finding that matches is taxi-B-20, and that one was tagged "product" only on the agent's own word.
verdicts.release_evidence: analytics-workbench-skills/awb-init/SKILL.md:32 and :38 (step 3.3: the installer installs helpers and "declare[s] the helpers' packages"; "When it prints an `install` command and its `interpreter` is `in_project` ... run that command yourself"); awb-init/scripts/install_helpers.py:43-45 and :62 ("no package is installed"), lines 390-403 (packages status computed live, install command printed). Possible minor contributor: awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py:191-196 (setup tool description does not say it leaves Python packages uninstalled).

consolidated.title: Agent queried inbox files with raw DuckDB before landing
consolidated.description: Before landing, the agent queried the inbox Parquet files with raw DuckDB to prepare its first interview round. data.md says to inspect records only from landed copies. It happened once.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-35: python -I -c 'import duckdb ... ../inbox/yellow_tripdata_2024-01.parquet' in agent-001.

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked the evidence and it matches the finding. In taxi-B, agent-001 (headless Claude, `codex_role: human`) did three things before anything was landed. It ran `.venv/bin/python -I -c "import duckdb ... '../inbox/yellow_tripdata_2024-01.parquet'"`, which returned the schema, row counts, date range and tip rate by payment type. It wrote two rows into `foundation/sources.md` using those numbers, with the basis given as "from landed records", even though nothing had been landed. Then it put the numbers into its first scoping round (cash tips 0.03%, payment_type 0 at 5% and 9%). Landing only happened in agent-002. The agent's own friction log says it went to DuckDB directly "because no views/publication exist yet" and calls this a "conflict for pre-landing peeks". The files it lists as read in turn 1 do not include `workbench-guides/data.md`.

I tried to pin this on the harness and nothing fits:
- **Persona front-loading.** Dana's opening message follows the README's own example and its advice that "the more you put in the first message, the fewer questions follow". Her "please verify" about cash tips comes straight from the persona brief and is realistic.
- **Non-interactive run.** `claude -p` with AskUserQuestion disabled did not change the order of events. The look at the data came first, to prepare questions the agent would have to ask at the end of its turn on any host.
- **Permissions.** Bash was pre-allowed. On a normal interactive host the user would get a prompt for this read-only command, but a first-time user has no reason to refuse it and no way to know the data guide forbids it. The rule break comes from the agent, not from the approval.
- **Other harness factors.** The simulated home folder, the inbox sitting outside the project folder, and the leaked relay line at the top of human-001 ("I'll read BRIEF.md...") have no bearing on the decision.
- **Model role.** Claude was the agent here, as it would be for a real Claude Code user.
- **Frequency.** The other five runs only listed the inbox before landing. Two of them (co2-B, retail-B) also used Claude as the agent. So the behaviour is occasional, not systematic, but it is a real-host model behaviour, not a harness one.

The release creates the conflict:
- awb-init runs awb-scope's first interview round in the same turn as setup, before any landing (it says data preparation follows "on request").
- awb-scope tells the agent to look facts up itself "in the repository, catalog, and source systems", to answer anything a quick lookup settles, to test definitions "against source data", and never to put a data question to the user.
- The README promises users that in the scoping round "Facts the data or the files can settle, the agent looks up itself", and that round comes before "bring your data in".
- awb-init also asks for the source register "when a source becomes a real candidate". The register's basis vocabulary only allows "from documentation" or "from landed records", which pushes the agent to assess sources before landing them.
- The only ban, "inspect records only from landed copies", sits in `data.md`. That file is reachable only through the Data trigger in AGENTS.md, and AGENTS.md is a file the agent had just copied in that same turn.

A real user on an interactive host could hit the same thing, and the release is the cause. The severity stays minor: the access was read-only and happened once.
verdicts.release_evidence:
The guide that forbids it: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/data.md:9 ("inspect records only from landed copies"). That guide is reachable only through awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:13 (the Data trigger, "before assessing a source...").

What pushes the agent the other way:
- awb-scope/SKILL.md:36 ("Look facts up yourself in the repository, catalog, and source systems, and answer a question a quick lookup settles... Never put a data question to the user")
- awb-scope/SKILL.md:31 (definitions "tested ... against source data")
- awb-init/SKILL.md:8 and :46 (data preparation follows on request, and the first interview round runs in the setup turn, before landing)
- awb-init/SKILL.md:39 (source register created when a source becomes a real candidate)
- awb-init/assets/workbench/foundation/sources.md:16 (basis must be "from documentation" or "from landed records")
- README.md:62 (scoping round: "Facts the data or the files can settle, the agent looks up itself"), which comes before README.md:81 ("First ask the agent to bring your data in")

verdicts.reasoning:
The event happened, but the release already forbids it and the agent skipped the guide it was told to read. It happened in one run out of six.

What the run shows: in taxi-B/relay/agent-001.jsonl (message 46, during the awb-scope first round in turn 1), the agent ran `.venv/bin/python -I -c "import duckdb ... '../inbox/yellow_tripdata_2024-01.parquet'"`. The query covered the schema, row counts, min/max pickup dates and a payment_type/tip breakdown, plus the zone CSV. Nothing had been landed yet; landing came in turn 2. Its row counts went into foundation/sources.md, and the payment-code-0 and cash-tip figures went into reply 1. The cited ID is wrong: taxi-B-35 in feedback/findings.json is an unrelated harness note about the user's notes being offset by one turn. The matching entry is taxi-B-24.

What the release says:
- data.md:9 says to assess a candidate from its documentation or schema and to "inspect records only from landed copies."
- AGENTS.md:13 says to read workbench-guides/data.md "before assessing a source, landing, retaining, or publishing data."

The agent printed the AGENTS.md template (message 16) and then assessed the source by writing candidate rows into sources.md. It never loaded data.md in turn 1: the phrase "inspect records only" does not appear anywhere in agent-001.jsonl. It read data.md in turn 2, and its own feedback (agent.md §2 and §4) admits it "technically violated" the guide.

Cross-run check: taxi-A, co2-A, co2-B and retail-A all loaded data.md in turn 1 and landed the files before looking at records. retail-B neither read it nor peeked. Only taxi-B queried the inbox directly. So the routing works when followed, and this is one lapse by one agent against a clear instruction, not a pattern.

Possible weak contributor, not enough to call it a product cause: awb-scope pushes the interviewer to test definitions "against source data" and to "look facts up yourself in ... source systems" without pointing at data.md. Meanwhile, awb-init has scope's first round run in the setup turn, before any data has landed. That pull exists, but data.md still allows a schema-level look, and landing is the route the other agents took.
verdicts.release_evidence: Prevents it: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/data.md:9 ("inspect records only from landed copies"), routed by awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:13 (read data.md before assessing a source). Weak contributing pull: awb-scope/SKILL.md:31 and :36, and awb-init/SKILL.md:46 (scope's first round runs in the setup turn, before landing).

consolidated.title: Near-miss validation claim of a profile check that had not run
consolidated.description: The agent first wrote that the values were 'checked with awb.py profile' without running profile, then caught and fixed it. It is unclear whether reading the profile run.py saves satisfies the guide.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-39: sed rewrite in agent-003; analysis.md 'inspected with awb.py profile'.

verdicts.reasoning:
The near-miss happened, and the harness did not cause it. The evidence does not show a release defect, and it does not show anything a real user would run into.

What happened (relay/agent-003.jsonl):
- Line 95: the agent's Python generator wrote the screening-by-vendor `values` judgment as "Vendors 1, 2 and 6 (6 appears only in January, 260 records) checked with awb.py profile."
- The agent never ran `awb.py profile` in any turn of taxi-B, either through Bash or through the MCP `read`/`profile` command. The vendor values came from an `awb.py sql` query in agent-002 (relay/agent-002.jsonl line 110: VendorID 6, 260 January rows) and from the eda-scan.
- Line 149: in the same turn, with no prompt from the user, the agent used sed to change the detail to "...per the publication and the saved table." This came before any report to the user.
- The final settings.toml line 45 is accurate. Nothing about profile reached the user-facing outputs, the deliveries or the human feedback. The finding comes only from the agent's own friction log (feedback/agent-notes.md:33).

Harness check: nothing in how the simulation was run explains writing the false attribution. That covers the non-interactive `claude -p` turn, the simulated home folder, MCP auto-approval and the persona's message, which only asked it to "proceed with exploration and all five answers". Claude in the agent role would read the same guide on an interactive host. The friction-log instruction only made the slip visible. It did not cause it, and the fix (line 149) came before the notes were written (line 198).

Release check:
- analysis.md:13 and AGENTS.md:24 both say plainly to inspect values with `awb.py profile`. The agent skipped that step and briefly claimed it had done it. That is the model not following the guide and briefly fabricating, not a release bug.
- The open question in the finding is whether reading the profile that run.py saves would count. That question had no bearing on this event, because the agent read neither the saved profile nor a live one. It cited SQL output.
- Across the runs: all three Codex-agent runs (taxi-A, co2-A, retail-A) ran profile through MCP `read`. None of the three Claude-agent runs (taxi-B, co2-B, retail-B) did, and only taxi-B ever wrote a profile claim, which it then removed. That points to compliance varying by model, not to a release cause.

The finding is a self-corrected slip with no effect on the user. The evidence shows neither that a real user would hit it nor that the release caused it.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:13 (values judgment "inspected with `awb.py profile`") and awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:24 ("distinct values with `awb.py profile`") both require the profile step. awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/run.py:119-121 saves `<id>.profile.json` with the same profile() function. None of these produced the false claim: per relay/agent-003.jsonl lines 95 and 149, the agent wrote the claim without running profile or reading the saved profile, then corrected it itself.

verdicts.reasoning:
The cited evidence is real, but the release did not cause the slip.

What happened: in turn 3 (relay/agent-003.jsonl, around line 96) the agent wrote this values judgment into settings.toml for screening-by-vendor: "Vendors 1, 2 and 6 (6 appears only in January, 260 records) checked with awb.py profile." It never ran `awb.py profile`, here or anywhere else in the run (no tool call in agent-001 through agent-008 invokes it). Later in the same turn (line 150) it used sed to change the detail to "...per the publication and the saved table", reran screening-by-vendor, and logged the slip in feedback/agent-notes.md:33. The false text existed only briefly. It never reached a finding, the user, or the package.

Is the release the cause? No. The release instruction is explicit. Release awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:13 says the values judgment covers distinct values "inspected with `awb.py profile`". AGENTS.md:24 says to compute counts, null rates and distinct values with `awb.py profile`. No release text tells the agent to write a tool claim into the detail. The only example detail in the settings template is "No categorical value drives this result." (investigation/settings.toml:41), and validation.md says judgments "record the analyst's judgment; the helper does not establish it". The false claim was the agent saying it had done something it had not, against a clear instruction. It happened once, and the agent fixed it itself.

The open question in the finding is a real but minor documentation gap: does reading the profile that run.py saves count as inspection? run.py:119-121 writes results/<id>.profile.json using the same profile() function behind `awb.py profile`, and validation.md:11 mentions that file. analysis.md:13 does not say whether reading it is enough. But this gap did not produce the near-miss. The agent read no profile.json in turn 3, and its first wording claimed a profile run, not a read of the saved file.

Side observation: the reworded details are truthful, but the agent still never ran `awb.py profile` for any of its 17 values judgments. That is a separate compliance point, not the near-miss described here. If it is pursued, it would be a candidate for clarifying analysis.md:13 (state whether the saved profile counts), not evidence that the release causes false validation claims.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:13 and awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:24 explicitly require `awb.py profile` for distinct values, so the release instructs against the false claim rather than causing it. The settings.toml:41 template detail contains no tool claim. The ambiguity the finding raises sits between analysis.md:13 and investigation/run.py:119-121 (plus awb-init/references/validation.md:11), but the agent never read a saved profile, so it did not trigger the slip.

consolidated.title: A near-tautological repeat-buyer share carries weight on the Answer slide
consolidated.description: The 97.0% repeat-buyer revenue share first appeared in the draft without having been shown in chat. Measured over two full years it is close to true by construction.
consolidated.evidence: retail-A-27: A5 draft; U6 item 6; A6.

verdicts.reasoning:
Bookkeeping first: the evidence ID is wrong. In retail-A/feedback/findings.json, retail-A-27 is about an export that failed with "no specification in findings". The finding that matches this one is retail-A-16, which the referee tagged "unclear".

The facts hold up:
- The 97.0% figure never appeared in chat before the full draft. The Codex log for agent turn 002 has six agent_message items and agent turn 005 has seven, and all of them reached transcript.md. A2 said only, without a number, that "repeat buyers account for most identified revenue". The number first shows in draft/findings.md: line 9 (the Answer slide) and line 43 (slide 4).
- It is the first bullet on the Answer slide ("Prioritize retention tests: ... supply 97.0%"), and it is still there in storage/releases/.../001/findings.md.
- The saved query repeat-profile.sql counts any identified customer with two or more distinct merchandise invoices across the full Dec 2009–Nov 2011 window.

I tried to pin this on the harness and could not:
- The relay passed every interim message, so this is not a relay mistake.
- The retention hypothesis that led to child question Q-009 was not front-loaded. In A1 the agent asked directly whether leadership had a retention-versus-acquisition hypothesis to test, as awb-scope tells it to ("what is already believed"). The persona brief has no such fact; the persona improvised a plausible answer, as any real user could.
- The Codex sandbox, non-interactive exec, auto-approved MCP and the simulated home have no bearing on which metric got picked or when it was shown.
- The one harness-leaning factor is the persona's brief-driven insistence on seeing every number in chat. Its "close to true by construction" critique also appears only in the end-of-run feedback (feedback/human.md section 5). During the session it asked only for the definition (U6 item 6), then accepted the release.

So a real Codex user would meet the same path. The release's design allows it:
- Preview-and-wait shows only headlines, so bullet numbers first appear in the full draft (awb-package/SKILL.md:47).
- The end-of-turn status line counts only the root questions, so the answer to child question Q-009 was never reported (workbench AGENTS.md:32; awb-scope/SKILL.md:38).
- The README says the checks do not redo the analysis (README.md:112), and the reviewer passed the claim because it was worded descriptively.

Two reasons for medium rather than high confidence:
- Choosing a two-year repeat-buyer split as the lead retention evidence was mostly Codex's own analytic judgment, which a release can only partly steer.
- "Near-tautological" overstates the problem. A 97% share held by 70.6% of customers is an empirical skew, not a share guaranteed by the definition, though the long window inflates it heavily. The draft itself already warned that repeat buyers "had differing lengths of time to accumulate orders" (Answer notes and slide 4 notes).

Severity is minor. The designed draft review caught it, and a definition was added before release.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/SKILL.md:47 (the preview-and-wait checkpoint shows only the title and headlines, so supporting numbers first appear in the full draft); awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:32 and awb-scope/SKILL.md:38 (the status line counts only root questions, so the answer to child question Q-009 was never surfaced); README.md:112 (the checks do not redo the analysis); awb-scope/SKILL.md:34 (the prompt about existing beliefs that led to the hypothesis question and to Q-009)

verdicts.reasoning:
The run evidence matches what the finding describes, but nothing in the release causes it.

What the evidence confirms:
- The snapshot of the A5 draft (project/.venv/tmp/leadership-budget-before-release-edits/findings.md:9 and :43) opens the Answer bullets with "repeat buyers supply 97.0% of identified net revenue". It gives no definition.
- 97.0% never appears in the transcript before U6. A2 only says qualitatively that "repeat buyers account for most identified revenue".
- In U3 the user asked for the numbers behind five specific headlines. A3 supplied all five, and the repeat-profile figure was not among them.
- The user queried the figure in U6 item 6, and A6 confirmed and defined it in one line. human/notes.md:58 records that this resolved cleanly ("confirmed in one line. Good.").

Why the release is not the cause:
1. The metric is the agent's own. It wrote queries/repeat-profile.sql to answer child question Q-009, which it created itself. Q-009 grew out of awb-scope's general prompt to recognise what is already believed (awb-scope/SKILL.md:34). No release file prescribes a full-window repeat-buyer revenue share. analysis.md:13 asks for a metrics judgment on definitions and assumptions.
2. The agent already caveated the exposure bias that makes the measure partly mechanical:
   - methodology.md:102 says "Different exposure times ... make this descriptive; it cannot identify the additional return from retention marketing".
   - The Answer notes add "Repeat buyers had differing lengths of time to accumulate orders".
   Leaning on the figure anyway was the agent's analytic call.
3. The number first appearing in the draft is how the release is designed. The preview-and-wait checkpoint shows only slide headlines (awb-package/SKILL.md:47), and the full draft is the intended place for the user to review bullet numbers. Here that review worked: the user caught the figure, and a definition rule was recorded.
4. The "near-tautological" label overstates the problem. 70.6% of customers supplying 97.0% of revenue does say something real: one-time wholesale buyers were small. It is a descriptive point the user would rather not see on the Answer slide, not a figure true by construction.

At most there is an enhancement idea: have the step-7 report point out Answer-slide numbers the user has not yet seen. That is not a defect the release causes.

The separate gap is that the definition was missing even though findings-template.md:66 asks "How we know" for "the definitions the answer depends on". That is a different finding, and there the agent and reviewer missed an existing instruction.
verdicts.release_evidence: none found. The metric comes from the agent-written project/investigations/marketing-investment/queries/repeat-profile.sql, which no release file prescribes. awb-package/SKILL.md:47 has the headline checkpoint show headlines only, so bullet numbers are meant to be reviewed in the draft. findings-template.md:39 asks for key findings with numbers on the Answer slide but does not name this metric. workbench-guides/analysis.md:13 already asks for a metrics judgment. The agent's own exposure caveat is in the draft's methodology.md:102.

consolidated.title: Unrecorded StockCode normalization changes a ranking
consolidated.description: The publication SQL trims and upper-cases StockCode, merging 47566b into 47566B, and nothing in quality.md, the catalog or the methodology records it. It moves Tea Time Party Bunting from 17.4% (rank 7) to 16.3% (rank 9).
consolidated.evidence: retail-A-29: project/src/preparation/retail_lines.sql line 10; referee/spot.out and spot2.out.

verdicts.reasoning:
The harness did not cause this, but the release is only part of the cause.

What the evidence shows:

- **The facts check out.** retail-A/project/src/preparation/retail_lines.sql:10 reads `upper(trim(StockCode)) AS stock_code` inside the publication's conversion SELECT.
- **Nothing records the change.** foundation/quality.md (DQ-001 to DQ-006) does not mention it. The catalog rows for retail_lines (catalog.md:7-8) do not mention it either. Worse, the catalog calls the publication a "Faithful union of both sheets" and DQ-003 says "Raw publication remains faithful".
- **The ranking does move.** referee/spot2.out shows 47566b (113 lines, £1,761.26 sales, £0 cancellations) sitting apart from 47566B (£25,831.99 sales, £4,490.50 cancellations). The agent's own number-review.md row 9 shows £27,593.25 and 16.3%, which is the sum of the two. On raw codes the rate is 17.4% (rank 7, spot.out). After the merge it falls below 71477's 16.4%, to rank 9.

Testing the harness explanations:

- The agent (Codex) wrote this SQL in agent-002, during the landing and publishing step. It had read the workbook columns and checked the timestamp conversion. It never looked for stock-code case variants and never discussed them with the user.
- Nothing about the setup explains that choice or the missing record. That covers the sandbox (heredoc and xcrun failures only), non-interactive exec, auto-approved MCP tools, the simulated home, the relay, and persona front-loading. The persona raised non-product codes, not case. The agent wrote quality.md and catalog rows freely in the same turn, so it was able to record the change.
- A real user running Codex with this release on an interactive host would see the same model, the same guidance and the same lack of any check. So the harness verdict does not hold.

Why confidence in "product" is low: the agent broke explicit release guidance.

- workbench-guides/data.md:43 says the rationale for normalization goes in foundation/quality.md.
- data.md:47 says normalization and corrections stay in views, not in materialized publications.
- awb-clean/SKILL.md:31 says case-only fixes must not be decided unilaterally in a code or identifier column, "where case, padding, and numeric form can carry meaning".

The agent read data.md in turn 1. It read awb-clean/SKILL.md in turn 2, after publishing, and chose not to run a cleaning pass.

How the release still contributes:

1. **The guidance contradicts itself on where normalization lives.** data.md:43 says "Preparation owns reusable parsing, normalization", and workbench README.md:24 places normalization code in src/preparation/, where the conversion SQL also lives. data.md:47 says normalization stays in views.
2. **Nothing catches a transform in a conversion.** Publish records only the agent's free-text notes and the declared checks. The awb-clean scan runs on the canonical view, which already sees the merged codes, so it could never surface the variant afterwards.

This is a guidance-compliance and enforcement gap that real users could hit, not a harness artifact. It is one run with one occurrence, and minor severity is right.

One bookkeeping error: the finding cites "retail-A-29", but in retail-A/feedback/findings.json that ID is the Codex-sandbox heredoc finding, tagged harness. The stock-code finding is retail-A-17, which the referee tagged "unclear".
verdicts.release_evidence: Nothing in the release tells the agent to upper-case StockCode; the agent's own SQL did it (retail-A/project/src/preparation/retail_lines.sql:10). Release guidance against the agent's behaviour: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/data.md:43 (normalization rationale goes in foundation/quality.md), data.md:47 (normalization stays in views), awb-clean/SKILL.md:31 (case in a code or identifier column is not decided unilaterally). Where the release contributes: data.md:43 together with awb-init/assets/workbench/README.md:24 places normalization in src/preparation/ alongside the conversion, which conflicts with data.md:47; and the publish and scan steps (data.md:33-39, awb-clean/SKILL.md step 1 on the canonical view) have no check that would catch a transform inside a conversion.

verdicts.reasoning:
The run evidence is accurate, but the release did not cause the problem. The release tells the agent to do the opposite of what it did.

What the run shows:
- retail-A/project/src/preparation/retail_lines.sql line 10 reads `upper(trim(StockCode)) AS stock_code`, inside the publication conversion.
- referee/spot2.out shows raw codes 47566B (sales 25,831.99, cancellations 4,490.50) and 47566b (sales 1,761.26, cancellations 0). Merged, that is 4,490.50 / 27,593.25 = 16.27%. In referee/spot.out, on raw codes, the product is at 17.4%, rank 7.
- The agent's own results/products-without-reversal.csv has 47566B at rank 9 (0.16274, sales 27,593.25), so the rank change is real.
- Nothing records the normalization. foundation/quality.md (DQ-001 to DQ-006), the catalog's preparation rules and the publication.json notes never mention it. The catalog's view row even calls the data a "Faithful union of both sheets".

What the release says:
- workbench-guides/data.md line 47: "normalization and corrections stay in views". Only publications are materialized.
- data.md line 43: "Preparation owns reusable parsing, normalization, checks, and corrections; their rationale goes in `foundation/quality.md`."
- The catalog template (foundation/catalog.md): "cleanliness comes from the quality record, not conversion".
- The quality template: record "accepted corrections that affect canonical data".
- awb-clean/SKILL.md lines 8 and 37: corrections go into view definitions under foundation/views/ and are recorded through record_cleaning.py. Its example change is "`foundation/views/02_orders.sql` trims dept", which puts a trim in a view, not in the conversion.
- references/landing.md, the guidance for writing the conversion SELECT, covers only reading cells as text, casting each column and converting Excel dates. It never suggests trimming or upper-casing keys.

The relay logs show the agent read data.md in agent-001.jsonl, where the "normalization and corrections stay in views" text appears. In agent-002 it then wrote the upper(trim()) into the conversion SQL with no exploration or stated reason, published, and filled in the catalog and quality rows without mentioning it.

One wording point could be read loosely: "Preparation owns ... normalization", and the conversion file lives in src/preparation/. Even on that reading, the same sentence requires the rationale in quality.md, which the agent skipped.

This is a single instance of the agent ignoring clear, consistent instructions, not something a template, helper or README produced. The scan helpers (eda_scan case_or_space_variants, the scan_dataset near-variants check) could not catch it because they read the already-normalized publication, but that is a missing safeguard, not a cause.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/data.md:47 ("normalization and corrections stay in views") and :43 ("their rationale goes in `foundation/quality.md`"); awb-init/assets/workbench/foundation/catalog.md ("cleanliness comes from the quality record, not conversion"); awb-clean/SKILL.md:8,37,58 (corrections go into view definitions and are recorded through record_cleaning.py); awb-init/references/landing.md:31-37 (conversion guidance limited to casting and date parsing). The agent read data.md in relay/agent-001.jsonl, then wrote line 10 of retail_lines.sql in relay/agent-002.jsonl.

consolidated.title: An undisclosed 'purchase' definition shifts repeat counts slightly
consolidated.description: Q3's purchase definition (a day without a cancellation that has a goods line with positive quantity) was never shown to the user or in the audience note. It moves repeat counts by 1-3 customers per cohort.
consolidated.evidence: retail-B-40: settings.toml line 76; referee/check3.py (Jan 194/368 vs 193/368).

verdicts.reasoning:
I couldn't find a harness cause, so this stays a product finding. It is a small disclosure gap, not a wrong number.

What happened:
- At scoping (reply 1), the agent proposed that buying again means "another order, not cancelled, on a later day within 90 days", and the user agreed to that (message 2).
- In agent turn 2, after cleaning the data, the agent narrowed the rule in foundation/glossary.md line 16: a purchase is "a non-cancellation invoice with at least one goods line of positive quantity", so an invoice with only postage does not count. The same rule is in settings.toml line 76 and in the internal methodology.md line 19.
- None of the agent's relayed messages mention it. I searched every relay/agent-*.out.md and the transcript.
- The audience note defines "Bought again within 90 days" only as "another purchase on a later day" (methodology-note.md line 21) and never defines a purchase.
- The agent sent the user to findings.md, methodology-note.md, the datasets and START-HERE.md. It labelled methodology.md as internal. The simulated user read exactly those files (human-006), as a real user would.

Numbers check:
- I re-ran referee/check3.py read-only. It matches the agent's table exactly, for example January 193/368.
- My own variant counts any non-cancelled goods or postage order as a purchase. It gives January 194, February 181 vs 179, April 114 vs 112, June 94 vs 92, and +1 in May, September and November. The July cohort grows from 185 to 186 customers.
- So the real shift is 0 to 2 customers per cohort, not "1-3 per cohort". The headline range does not change.

Harness causes I checked and ruled out:
- Relay: nothing was dropped.
- Simulated user front-loading answers: the user simply accepted the proposed definition, as a busy real user would.
- Sandbox, auto-approved tools, simulated home: they have nothing to do with this choice.
- Headless "cannot ask mid-turn" note: no effect. The agent did end turns to ask about other definition questions, for example the repeated lines (DQ-013), and simply judged this one not worth raising.
- The agent's behaviour is what a real user gets from the same model with these skills on an interactive host.

How the release contributes:
- AGENTS.md line 44 tells the agent to settle unclear terms with examples and the data and record them in the glossary. It does not say to send a definition the user approved back to the user when the data narrows it.
- The note template asks for "the terms the answer depends on", but the release's review only checks that the note claims nothing methodology.md doesn't support. Nothing catches a definition that is left out.

The rule itself is sensible, and the referee's tag of "unclear" reflects that. So this is minor, and I hold medium confidence that the release, not just the agent's judgment, is the cause.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:44 (settle unclear terms with the data and record them in the glossary; no step sends a narrowed approved definition back to the user); awb-package/assets/package-format/methodology-note-template.md:23-25 (Definitions should list the terms the answer depends on, but nothing enforces it); awb-package/references/review.md:22 (the reviewer checks that the note claims nothing methodology.md doesn't support, not what it leaves out). Project side: retail-B/project/foundation/glossary.md:16 holds the purchase rule; released/001/methodology-note.md:21 leaves it out.

verdicts.reasoning:
The numbers in the finding hold up. The release is not the cause, and calling the definition "undisclosed" overstates what happened.

What I confirmed:
- Before seeing any data, the agent's scope question (A1, transcript.md line 37) offered "another order, not cancelled, on a later day within 90 days". The user agreed to that.
- In A2 the agent narrowed "purchase" to a non-cancellation invoice day with a positive-quantity goods line. It never said this in chat.
- The audience note (released/001/methodology-note.md) defines "Bought again within 90 days" as "another purchase on a later day" but never defines "purchase". findings.md does not define it either.
- The referee's check3.py reproduces the agent's 12 cohort counts exactly (Jan 193/368).
- I re-ran the same logic with postage lines counted as purchases. Repeat counts move by 0 to 2 per cohort: Jan 194, Feb 181, Apr 114, Jun 94, Sep 104, Nov 99. The July cohort grows by one customer. So the finding's "1-3" is slightly high (the largest change is 2), and the headline range does not change.

Why the release is not the cause:
- **The definition was disclosed, just not in the short note.** The agent wrote it into the shared glossary, with postage-only invoices as the stated boundary case (foundation/glossary.md, "Purchase" row, written in A2 per relay/agent-002.jsonl). It also appears in the delivered internal methodology.md at line 19 and in settings.toml line 76. Recording it this way follows AGENTS.md: "Settle ambiguous terms with concrete examples and the data. Record shared meanings in foundation/glossary.md".
- **Several release instructions already call for it in the audience note:**
  - methodology-note-template.md, "## Definitions": "The terms the answer depends on, in the glossary's business terms".
  - findings-template.md line 66: "the definitions the answer depends on".
  - package-contract.md line 48: the narratives must agree in "qualifications, and caveats".
  - awb-scope SKILL.md: "Leave no answer recorded in a form two analysts could read differently".
- **Nothing in the release tells the agent to leave the definition out.** No helper, template or README text does. The gap is one drafting omission of a sub-definition, plus a draft review that did not catch it. It is not a repeated failure to follow a clear instruction, and nothing in the release produces it.
- **The release could be more explicit, but that is a suggestion, not a cause.** One template phrase, "with any departure from their usual meaning", may have nudged the agent to drop a definition that arguably matches the plain meaning of "purchase". The release also never asks the agent to report back when analysis narrows a definition the user agreed to. Both are possible improvements; neither causes this finding.

Overall this is minor agent behaviour, not a release defect, which matches the referee's own "unclear" tag on retail-B-29 in feedback/findings.json.
verdicts.release_evidence: Contradicts (the release already asks for the definition): awb-package/assets/package-format/methodology-note-template.md, "## Definitions" section (about line 23: "The terms the answer depends on, in the glossary's business terms"); awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:66; awb-package/references/package-contract.md:48 (narratives agree in qualifications); awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md, "Record maintenance" section (settle ambiguous terms and record them in the glossary, which the agent did); awb-scope/SKILL.md, "Follow up before moving on". No release file causes the omission.

consolidated.title: Agent promoted a classification to a shared foundation view unasked
consolidated.description: Without being asked, the agent moved its line-type classification into the shared foundation view 20_online_retail_line_types.sql. AGENTS.md says broader preparation needs an explicit request. It happened once.
consolidated.evidence: retail-B-43: agent-002.

verdicts.reasoning:
The event is real, and I could not tie it to the harness.

What happened: in retail-B, relay/agent-002.in.md is a clean user message. It agrees the revenue definition and says "go ahead with downloading, checking and cleaning the data, then the analysis." It says nothing about where the line classification should live. The agent ran clean-record and then wrote "The rule that sorts lines into products, postage and non-trading is shared, so it goes in a foundation view" (agent-002.jsonl line 212). It then wrote project/foundation/views/20_online_retail_line_types.sql with a Bash heredoc and pointed the glossary at it. Its reply to the user (agent-002.out.md) never mentions creating a shared view. Its friction log (feedback/agent-notes.md, Turn 2) doesn't list the choice as a deviation, so it saw nothing to ask about.

Harness causes I checked and ruled out:
- **Relay mistake:** none. The input is verbatim and the decision is unrelated to its wording.
- **Persona front-loading:** none. The persona's broad go-ahead is what a real user would say.
- **Simulated home folder:** not involved.
- **Auto-approved MCP tools:** not involved. The view was written through Bash, not an awb MCP tool, and permission-prompts.jsonl holds only one line, unrelated.
- **Non-interactive host (no AskUserQuestion under claude -p):** the agent showed no hesitation that a mid-turn question would have caught.

The strongest point against harness: retail-A ran a different model (Codex) on a different host (codex exec). Its user also never asked for a shared view (retail-A relay/agent-002.in.md), yet it did the same thing and created project/foundation/views/10_retail_classified.sql in agent-002 (agent-002.jsonl, item_42). Two models on two hosts making the same choice points at the release's guidance, not at how one simulation was run. It also means "It happened once" undercounts: it happened in both retail runs.

Why the verdict is product, and why confidence is only medium: the release's instructions pull in two directions.
- AGENTS.md:36 says broader preparation needs an explicit request, which supports the finding.
- data.md:43 says preparation owns reusable normalization, and that a "generally valid exploratory rule" can be promoted into preparation "deliberately". It doesn't require the user to ask.
- AGENTS.md:44 says shared meanings go in foundation/glossary.md.
- awb-clean/SKILL.md:37 says accepted shared rules go in canonical views.

Read together, these invite an agent to treat a stock-code classification as shared preparation. It is also arguable that the classification is not "broader" at all, since the active question needs it and there is only one investigation. So the release is the cause, either by allowing this or by being ambiguous about it. A real user on an interactive host would very likely see the same behavior. Whether it counts as a rule violation is open to interpretation, and the impact is minor.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:36 (broader preparation needs an explicit request) conflicts with awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/data.md:43 (preparation owns reusable normalization; promote a generally valid rule deliberately, without asking), AGENTS.md:44 (shared meanings in the foundation glossary) and awb-clean/SKILL.md:37 (accepted shared rules go in canonical views). The same choice also shows up in retail-A at project/foundation/views/10_retail_classified.sql (Codex agent, never asked).

verdicts.reasoning:
The event did happen. In retail-B relay/agent-002.jsonl (event [212]-[213], also in agent-002.out.md), the agent wrote foundation/views/20_online_retail_line_types.sql. It said so in chat as it worked: "The rule that sorts lines into products, postage and non-trading is shared, so it goes in a foundation view." The only source for the finding is the agent's own list of deviations in feedback/agent.md line 65. The user never objected, and nothing in human/ or feedback/human.md mentions it.

The finding treats this as a breach of AGENTS.md. The release does not support that reading:
- **What the rule covers:** AGENTS.md:36 says "broader preparation needs an explicit request." In the design (docs/workbench-design.md:27, workbench-spec.md:66 and scenario 5), "broader preparation" means preparing data beyond what the active question needs. This view served the active question: all five result queries read it.
- **Promotion only has to be deliberate:** AGENTS.md:36 lets exploratory work leave the investigation "until deliberately promoted", with no user request required. workbench-guides/data.md:43 says "Promote a generally valid exploratory rule into preparation... deliberately." The agent's stated reason ("a neutral, generally valid rule") follows that sentence closely, and it announced the move.
- **The view classifies but filters nothing:** it adds line_type, is_cancellation and value columns and keeps every row. The exclusion itself (dropping non-trading lines from revenue) stays in the investigation's queries. That matches data.md:43 and design boundary 3 in workbench-spec.md (reusable normalization goes in the foundation; filters and exclusions stay local). The stock-code classification is also the net-revenue definition the user had agreed to ("Agreed on the revenue definition", agent-002.in.md), and the agent recorded it in the glossary as AGENTS.md:44 directs.
- **The design pushes the same way:** sessions load only foundation/views, and the investigation has no local view mechanism (run.py, awb_landing.session). analysis.md:7 says intermediate computation "stays in views". retail-A also built a foundation view of the same kind (10_retail_classified.sql), and its agent did not count it as a deviation.

So the agent did what the release asks for. A real user would see an announced, agreed classification placed where the design says it belongs, which is not a defect. The one possible criticism is that "deliberately" in data.md:43 does not say who decides. That made the agent doubt itself afterwards, but it did not cause wrong behavior.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:36 ("broader preparation needs an explicit request" is about data scope; promotion only has to be deliberate); awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/data.md:43 ("Promote a generally valid exploratory rule into preparation... deliberately"); awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:7 ("Intermediate computation stays in views"); run.py header and awb_landing.session load only foundation/views. None of these forbid the action. They permit it and push toward it.

consolidated.title: Findings re-promoted after reruns on the strength of an earlier acceptance
consolidated.description: After reruns that changed displayed values or added checks, the agent re-promoted findings to supported, citing the user's earlier acceptance without asking again. The guide does not say whether an acceptance carries over such a rerun.
consolidated.evidence: retail-B-44: A5; A6 reason 'user accepted the answers on 2026-10-16'; analysis.md line 17.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not tie this to the harness. What happened in retail-B: at A3 the agent told the user "All eight findings are provisional until you approve them". At U4 the user wrote "I accept the quantitative answers", and the agent promoted all eight findings with the reason "User accepted the quantitative answers on 2026-10-16" (history.md lines 101-163).

Rerun 1, at A5: the double-rounding fix changed two displayed figures (63.2% to 63.1%, 52.5% to 52.4%). The agent re-promoted every finding with the reason "...user accepted the answers on 2026-10-16" (history.md lines 237-301, "re-promoted on the user's earlier acceptance").

Rerun 2, at A6: after adding the reconciliation, identified-account and overlap checks, it did the same again (history.md lines 325-357). It did not ask the user either time. agent.md §4 lists this under deviations as a judgment call.

Harness explanations I checked and rejected:
- **Non-interactive turns.** The agent's system note bans mid-turn questions and AskUserQuestion is disallowed, but the note says to end the turn with a question when an answer is needed. The agent never showed any wish to ask. Its stated reason was that values were unchanged apart from the corrected percents, which it reported. With AskUserQuestion available, the same reasoning applies.
- **Persona front-loading.** The acceptance came at U4, after the agent showed full tables. A real user would accept findings the same way. The brief asks for acceptance but does not script how status works.
- **The requested checks.** At A6 the user asked for those checks themselves, so re-asking would not be expected on any host.
- **Relay, sandbox, simulated home, auto-approval.** None of these plays a part.

What the release says:
- analysis.md:17 treats re-promotion as an agent step gated only by the agent's own checks ("Before re-promoting, check the interpretation-driving values... and the prior caveats in the rerun's history entry").
- run.py's own history entries tell the agent to "re-promote with `awb.py state finding`" (awb_provenance.py:1463-1465).
- No guide, skill or template says whether 'supported' needs the user's acceptance, or whether an acceptance survives a rerun that changes displayed values or checks. state.md:10 lists the statuses without saying who promotes.

So the agent's choice to tie 'supported' to acceptance, and then to reuse that acceptance, comes from the release leaving the question open. A real user on an interactive host would get the same agent behavior.

The impact is small. The agent disclosed both reruns and their effects to the user at A5 and A6. The user approved the release at U7, and human.md does not complain about re-promotion. That fits 'minor' severity.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:17 (re-promotion gated only by the agent's own checks of values and caveats; nothing on user acceptance or whether it survives a rerun); awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py:1463-1465 (rerun history entry: "re-promote with `awb.py state finding`"); awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/state.md:10 (statuses defined without saying who promotes)

verdicts.reasoning:
The behavior did happen, but the release does not cause it and the run shows no harm. In retail-B the findings were re-promoted three times after reruns. history.md lines 237-293 record the precision fix ("values unchanged except two displayed percents, 63.1% and 52.4%"), lines 325/333 the added reconciliation and identified-account checks, and line 357 the overlap check. Each time the stated reason ends "user accepted the answers on 2026-10-16". The agent did not ask the user again.

The finding assumes that a user's acceptance is what makes a finding supported, and that the guide leaves open whether that acceptance survives a rerun. The release never makes acceptance a condition. Promotion is the agent's own validation step. analysis.md line 17 says a rerun makes a finding provisional and gives the gate for re-promoting: "check the interpretation-driving values ... and the prior caveats in the rerun's history entry." It does not mention user acceptance anywhere. Neither does any other shipped file: AGENTS.md, the state.md template (line 10), awb-status, awb-package, and the README's "What you will be asked" list (README.md lines 59-71) all leave it out. The release asks for the user's approval at the package headline checkpoint (awb-package/SKILL.md lines 47-50; package-contract.md line 39, which applies again whenever the storyline changes) and for warnings at release.

Tying "supported" to the user's approval was the agent's own convention. Its A3 reply said "All eight findings are provisional until you approve them". The user persona's U3 "Before I approve them" encouraged it. The agent itself lists the re-promotion as a judgment call (agent.md line 63; agent-notes.md line 60), not as friction from the release. It also followed the release's actual re-promotion gate: it checked which displayed values changed.

The run shows no harm. In the same A5 reply the agent told the user about both corrected percentages (52.4%, 63.1%) and about the headlines that differed from the preview. In A6 it said the new checks changed no figures. The user then reviewed the draft (U6), approved the release (U7), and never raised the issue (human.md, human/notes.md). Also, 52.4% was already the January value in the A3 cohort table the user accepted. A real user would not hit a problem the release created here.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:17 sets the re-promotion gate as checking interpretation-driving values and prior caveats, with no user acceptance involved. README.md:59-71 lists what the user is asked and does not include accepting findings. awb-package/SKILL.md:47-50 and awb-package/references/package-contract.md:39 put user approval at the headline checkpoint, repeated when the storyline changes. Nothing in the release makes acceptance a condition for promoting a finding to supported.

harness_findings.title: Personas front-load the facts they should give only when asked
harness_findings.description: In the first one or two messages, personas volunteered most of their 'if it asks' facts: definitions, storage paths, exclusions, the headline preview and skill names. They also pre-answered later package questions and agreed to an appendix move unprompted. Scoping shrank to one round, and package questions were skipped. The README's own first-message example invites some of this.
harness_findings.oct15_ref: synthesis 'Limits of this study' (personas front-loaded definitions)
harness_findings.evidence: taxi-A-28 (transcript lines 5-22, 192, 239); taxi-B-52 (msg 1); co2-B-29 (U1); retail-A-40 (U1, U2); retail-B-51 (U1, U2). Each compared with its human/BRIEF.md list 'Things you can tell the agent if it asks'.

harness_findings.title: Agents wrote to /tmp and listed or searched directories above the simulation folder
harness_findings.description: Agents wrote scratch files to /tmp or /tmp/claude-501, later deleting or moving them. They listed SIMDIR's parent and /private/tmp/claude-501, and walked eight levels of ancestors looking for AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, which exposed the study folder names beside the project. No study file contents were read. On a real host, /tmp writes and the ancestor walk (awb-init step 1.3) are normal, and review.md itself suggests the system temp folder.
harness_findings.evidence: taxi-B-47: 'ls -la project/..'; '/tmp/awb-export-board.sh'. co2-B-27: /tmp/q.sql and /tmp/claude-501/review-diff.txt. retail-B-49: 'rm -f /tmp/claude-501/export.json ...'. co2-B-31: 'ls project/..' printed human, relay, REFEREE.md. co2-A-38: ancestor loop 8 levels up.

harness_findings.title: The harness's private friction log leaks into replies and adds overhead
harness_findings.description: Interim lines mentioned the harness-only friction log ('Now the private notes file.', 'then the friction log', 'Now the friction log.'), and users saw them as unexplained jargon. Appending to the log every turn also added overhead and caused one failed functions.exec call.

harness_findings.title: Codex sandbox blocked heredoc temp files, tool caches and system-temp writes
harness_findings.description: Codex's workspace-write sandbox and the simulated home blocked zsh heredoc temp files (one failure led to an awb/setup refusal), the xcrun and pip caches, and writes to the system temp directory. Review copies therefore went to .venv/tmp or agent-home.

harness_findings.title: Agents read Claude Code's own session files outside the simulated home
harness_findings.description: The agent and its reviewer subagents read Claude Code's spilled tool-result files under the real ~/.claude/projects, and a background-task output under /private/tmp/claude-501. These held only the session's own output.

harness_findings.title: Agent system prompt says the user sees only the final reply, but the relay forwards interim messages
harness_findings.description: The harness's agent prompt says 'The user sees only your final reply each turn', but the relay forwards every interim message verbatim. Narration written as if no one would read it reached the simulated user, which confounds how C-02 should be read.
harness_findings.evidence: taxi-B-49: prompts/claude-agent-system.md 'Conversation' vs transcript.md. retail-B-48: kit/relay.py line 7.

harness_findings.title: Harness pre-approval hides the permission-prompt burden
harness_findings.description: Pre-allowed Bash and auto-approved awb MCP tools meant permission prompts were almost never recorded. The runs therefore cannot show the approval cost of about 95 CLI helper calls (taxi-B) or of 67 MCP calls in a single turn (co2-A).
